statuses.title: calibration probes run under a tighter discretization than the runtime accountant
statuses.note: The headline defect is fixed: calibration.py:321-342 re-enters `_use_discretization(overall_config)` and re-evaluates `budget.evaluate(process(result.param))`, so the returned CalibrateResult.achieved is now the number the runtime accountant will reproduce. Same for b_min_sep(mf_gaussian(nm, band_mf_strategy(bands=4)), n_steps=32, p0=0.05): achieved 2.971823 == runtime 2.9718226111291606. The final-PLD mc_resolution now also uses overall_config rather than probe_config (:348-352). TWO CAVEATS, both filed as findings: (1) the `if not runtime_safe` branch (:331-341) re-runs the ENTIRE adaptive bisection inside the runtime context, discarding the deliberate union bound (probe_config = overall beta / (max_iterations+2), :302-309) while :353 still reports mc_failure_probability = overall beta; instrumented run shows 23 probes at beta/32 followed by 23 probes at beta; (2) `achieved` is now a different evaluation from the one the bisection converged on, so the documented invariant math.isclose(achieved, target, rel_tol=tolerance) (docstring :139-142, docs/reference/accounting.md:722-724) can be false while converged=True. The trainer-side assertion from the OPQ-323 fix sketch ('assert privacy_calibration_achieved_epsilon >= ctx.accounting.epsilon_at(target_delta)') was not added; that is opaque-transformers scope.

statuses.title: b-min-sep warm-start likelihood ratio misnormalizes the stationary mixture
statuses.note: 9df5a8dc rewrote likelihood_ratio_warm into a log-space WarmLogLikelihoodRatio. packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:102-106 now computes `log_numerator = log_add(log_f[0], log_p + log_sumexp(&log_f[1..bands]))` then `log_numerator - self.log_denominator` with `log_denominator = ln(1+(bands-1)p)` (:71) -- i.e. (f[0] + p*tail)/denom, the parenthesisation OPQ-300 asked for. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, not against the repo's own oracle: I re-implemented (a) the warm-start participation law by exhaustive enumeration over initial barred states x all 2^n masks and (b) the shipped DP, in Python (scratchpad/vfy_opq300.py). Shipped DP == exact enumeration to <=1e-15 relative over 6 cases (bands 1..5, n 3..10, p 0.17/0.5/0.999/1.0, sigma^2 0.81..2.0); the pre-fix formula overstated by 1.14x-1.71x on the same cases. The repo's pinned constant `privacy_loss_matches_jax_reference` (0.8329398380809252) equals my exact enumeration's ln bit-for-bit. End-to-end: bands=1 MC delta dominates `poisson_pld(gaussian_pld(sigma)).self_compose(n)` at every eps in {0,.25,.5,1,2,4} for (n,p,sigma) in {(8,.15,1.2),(20,.1,1.0),(50,.05,0.8)}. PERF REWRITE CHECKED: d0257cbf only hoists the evaluator into `for_each_init` state; the evaluator's only state is the `log_f` scratch, which is `resize`d to n+bands, has [n..] refilled with 0 and [0..n] fully rewritten on every call (mc.rs:81-101), so reuse across samples cannot leak state. Sibling check: the balls-in-bins MC ratio (balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:84-97) is the correctly 1/b-normalised mixture log-ratio and has no analogous defect. cargo test --workspace --lib: 397 passed / 0 failed.

statuses.title: random_allocation.rs docstring claims discretisation error does not accumulate
statuses.note: 0cb6b7b7 replaced the false claim. packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:13-18 now reads "The grid size does not grow across them, which makes large `t` tractable. Each pairwise convolution contributes at most `alpha` of privacy-loss discretisation error, so the total error for a `t`-fold convolution is bounded by `(floor(log2 t) + popcount(t) - 1) * alpha`." I checked the stated count against the implementation: `GeomPmf::self_conv` (pld/pmf/geom.rs:316-336) is binary exponentiation -- floor(log2 t) squarings (`base = base.conv(&base, dir)` guarded by `rem > 0`) plus popcount(t) accumulator merges of which the first is a `clone()` rather than a `conv`, i.e. exactly floor(log2 t) + popcount(t) - 1 convolutions, each rounding up one geometric grid step (`Rounding::Up`, error <= alpha in log-value, multiplicative errors compose additively in log space). `alpha` is a named field of the module's `Accuracy` struct (:36-47), so the symbol resolves. Docs-only change; per AGENTS.md test design guidance no verbatim-prose test is expected, and the pre-existing `test_larger_max_conv_grid_tightens_bound` still encodes the grid dependence.

statuses.title: self-convolution exponent silently truncated to u32 on the budgeted circular path
statuses.note: e858a470 added the boundary guard. packages/opaque-accounting/src/numerics/fft.rs:295-300 rejects `count > u32::MAX as usize` with InvalidParameter, and it sits after the singleton short-circuit (:288, which uses `pow_usize` and keeps full usize range) and strictly before the only `powu(count as u32)` site (:331). Grepped the whole crate for `as u32` / `powu`: the only other `as u32` casts are `(raw_ratio.log2().ceil() as u32).max(1)` in discretization/config.rs:219 and pld/pmf/dense.rs:458, which saturate to 0 on negative/NaN and are then clamped to >=1, so no second truncation site survives. Both entry points are covered because `self_convolve` (:161-162) delegates to `self_convolve_with_bounds`. Regression tests `test_fft_self_convolution_rejects_count_above_u32_max` and `test_circular_self_convolution_accepts_count_at_u32_max` exercise exactly the reproducer from the OPQ entry (`&[0.5,0.5]`, count = u32::MAX+1, Some((0,15)), allow_circular=true); both pass. Python boundary at python/pld.rs:36 still raises OverflowError above u32::MAX, so the two boundaries now agree.

statuses.title: asymmetric PLD beta metrics renormalize negative_infinity_mass away
statuses.note: e67927d7 resolved the inconsistency in the direction the symmetric path already used. `clean_probs` now takes negative_infinity_mass and renormalises to `1 - infinity_mass - negative_infinity_mass` (pld/metrics.rs:127-141); `pmf_beta_asymmetric` anchors the -inf atoms explicitly -- `cdf_y[0] = pmf_remove.negative_infinity_mass + probs_y[0]` (:317) and `cdf_add[0] = pmf_add.negative_infinity_mass + probs_x_add[0]` (:325, which is X = -L_add's +inf atom and so belongs in every ccdf_x entry); `pmf_beta_symmetrized` seeds `alpha_bar = pmf_add.negative_infinity_mass` (:427) and `f_alpha_bar = pmf_remove.negative_infinity_mass` (:435). I re-derived the new regression test's expected value from first principles rather than trusting it: for remove = {0.3 at -inf, 0.7 at loss 0} and add = {1.0 at loss 0}, the randomised Neyman-Pearson test at alpha=0.5 rejects the single finite atom with probability 0.5, giving beta = 0.3 + 0.5*0.7 = 0.65 -- exactly what `test_beta_asymmetric_includes_negative_infinity_mass` asserts, and 0.5 (wrong) under the pre-fix renormalisation. The same commit also repairs a latent negative-to-usize wrap: `((-x0 + 1).max(0) as usize)` / `((-y0 + 1).max(0) as usize)` (:425, :433) -- previously a negative intermediate wrapped to a huge usize and was clamped by `.min(n)`, silently returning Pr[X>0]=0 when the whole add PMF sat at loss index <= -2 and Pr[Y<=0]=full mass when the whole remove PMF sat at loss index >= 2. Epsilon is untouched (`pmf_delta`/`pmf_epsilon` read only infinity_mass), matching the OPQ entry's eps:no. 397 lib tests pass.

statuses.title: per-group adaptive clip sync reduces group counts positionally
statuses.note: Fix commit 23521ab6 (#888). packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_distributed.py:64-71 now derives the collective schedule from the replicated schema: `current_pg = state._current_clipping_norm; group_names = sorted(current_pg.values)` and reduces `state._num_clipped[gname]` in that order, so the i-th all_reduce carries the same group on every rank regardless of dict insertion order. All three construction sites named in the OPQ entry were canonicalised too: `_empty_num_clipped()` -> `dict.fromkeys(sorted(initial_clipping_norm.values), 0.0)` (_adaptive.py:396), the stats path builds `{gname: stats.num_clipped[gname] for gname in sorted(current_pg.values)}` (_adaptive.py:539-551), and the engine's `_compute_clipping_stats` / `clipped_grad` empty paths sort as well (engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:412,495,513 and _clipped_grad.py:268). Traced the noise-fold index: the single-process per-group path folds `(ADAPTIVE_CLIPPING_STREAM_FOLD, state._step, i)` on the pre-increment step (_adaptive.py:559,592) and the sync folds `step_for_noise = max(0, state._step - 1)` on the post-increment state (_distributed.py:76-82), so both reach the same integer. `new_state._current_clipping_norm = state._next_clipping_norm` on both the empty and non-empty paths, so the schema is identical on an empty rank. No KeyError risk: `per_group()` drops unmatched patterns from `values` (engine/clipping/_per_group.py:180-185), so every key in `values` has at least one leaf. Ran the 2-rank gloo lane: packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/ddp/test_dpsgd_cpu_gloo.py 6 passed, including test_per_group_adaptive_clipping_one_rank_empty_syncs, which now all_gathers the resulting thresholds and asserts rank agreement. Sibling scan for the same positional-reduce pattern found none left (engine `_gather_aux_fields` iterates the registered aux schema; `_sync_clipping_rate` issues a fixed two-collective schedule).

statuses.title: samplers seed numpy directly from the caller's key (no namespaced stream root)
statuses.note: Fix commit dd65957d (#884), DP-SGD scope (the dpftrl samplers in the same OPQ entry belong to the dpftrl reviewer). `POISSON_STREAM_FOLD = "opaque.dpsgd.poisson"` (sampling/_poisson.py:34) and `K_OUT_OF_T_STREAM_FOLD = "opaque.dpsgd.k_out_of_t"` (sampling/_k_out_of_t.py:26) are folded at construction (_poisson.py:97 `fold_in(key, POISSON_STREAM_FOLD)`; _k_out_of_t.py:55 `fold_in(key, K_OUT_OF_T_STREAM_FOLD, allocation)`), and the per-block derivation is `fold_in(self._stream_key, block)` (_k_out_of_t.py:129) - the RandomAllocation bare-integer fold the OPQ entry called out is gone with that class. Verified by execution: the Poisson stream no longer matches `np.random.default_rng(key.seed)`; neither sampler root lands in the caller-reachable set {key.seed} u split(key,16) u {fold_in(key,i) for i in -63..511}; block/total/Poisson built from one key(42) all produce different batch sequences. State-dict compatibility is handled by storing the post-fold stream key and restoring with `_from_stream_key` (test_poisson_state_dict.py::test_pre_domain_snapshot_uses_saved_seed_without_folding pins that a pre-#884 Poisson snapshot still replays its original stream, which is correct because pre-#884 Poisson seeded from the raw key). Tags are registered in docs/reference/rng.md:222-223.

statuses.title: accounting rejects sample_rate=1.0 that the runtime PoissonSampler supports
statuses.note: Fix commit 280e4969 (#853). `Poisson.__post_init__` now validates `not 0 < sample_rate <= 1` (accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:49) and `pld()` short-circuits `sample_rate == 1.0` by delegating to `self.inner.pld(...)` (:126-135). Verified numerically: `poisson(gaussian(1.1), 1.0) * 1000` gives epsilon 534.8979126040266 at delta=1e-5, bit-identical to `gaussian(1.1) * 1000`; the AdaClip inner path matches its unamplified counterpart to full precision (79.39286932042074 both ways); a q=1.0 process state-dicts and reloads. The truncated combination is still rejected with an explanatory ConfigurationError (:58-66). Runtime and accounting ranges now agree - the sampler validates `0 < sample_rate <= 1` (sampling/_poisson.py:~120) and docs/user-guide/sampling.md:42-45 and :76 both publish `(0, 1]` with the `sample_rate < 1` caveat for truncated Poisson.

statuses.title: O(G^2) random-allocation epoch transform rebuilt on every distinct step count
statuses.note: Resolved by two commits acting together. 87404a1b (#894) deleted horizon prefix accounting, so `KOutOfT` no longer exposes `pld_at(n)` - `pld()` computes the whole declared horizon once (accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_k_out_of_t.py:87-118) and `grep -rn 'pld_at|per_step'` over source and docs now returns nothing. 20dd47aa (#881) added the `epoch_pld` lru_cache (opaque-accounting/.../core/_random_allocation_cache.py:29-46) keyed on (nm, t, k, config). The OPQ-313 failure scenario is gone: measured k=8,t=512 - first `epsilon_at(1e-5)` 16.68 s, the second 0.01 s, and a structurally identical fresh `KOutOfT` instance also 0.01 s, so a trainer querying at every log boundary with a fixed delta pays once. CAVEAT (filed as a finding): the memoisation that the issue asked for is inert. `DpProcess.epsilon_at` rewrites `mc_resolution` to `delta/2` before calling `pld()` (opaque-accounting/.../core/_base.py:209-227), and that Monte-Carlo-only field is part of the `DiscretizationConfig` the lru_cache hashes, even though `random_allocation_gaussian_pld` never reads it. Measured `epoch_pld.cache_info()` after eps(1e-5) x2, eps(1e-6) and delta_at(3.0): hits=0, misses=3, with 16.2-16.7 s paid on each of the three misses.

(3) _dpftrl.py:294-302 build_sampler raises the same way, so a direct caller bypassing TrainingArguments also fails closed. The runtime/accountant desync the OPQ described is closed at the source: _dpftrl.py:388-394 builds CyclicPoissonSampler(sample_rate=float(amp.sample_rate), bands=int(mf.strategy.bands)) by reading the rate straight off the built amplifier instance (amp = mf.amplifier_factory(noise_multiplier)), and _dpftrl.py:127-163 _cyclic_poisson_group_rate converts the per-example rate to the per-active-group conditional rate (and rejects group_rate > 1 and group_size < 1). statuses.title: random_allocation.rs docstring claims discretisation error does not accumulate across exponentiation-by-squaring convolutions

statuses.title: lambda-CGD noise stream is unrooted: fold_in(key, step) collides with the caller's documented integer key space
statuses.note: Fixed by f2d90d61 (fix(random)!: namespace lambda-CGD noise stream, #1018), and the three things the task asked about all check out. (a) Tag registered: the fix introduced _mf_gaussian_column_key at packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_engine.py:41-53, which folds MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD ("opaque.dpftrl.mf_gaussian") + "mf_gaussian_column" + column before any integer, and _lambda_cgd.py:281 and :293 now call it for current_key and prev_key; the bare `from opaque.random import fold_in as rng_fold_in` import was removed from _lambda_cgd.py. grep for fold_in across packages/opaque-dpftrl/src finds no remaining bare integer fold outside the helper. (b) Namespacing test covers it: tests/integration/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py:32 lists ("opaque.dpftrl.mf_gaussian", MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD) and the three tests assert the literal value, non-aliasing against split()/fold_in(base, i) for i in [-64, 512), and mutual distinctness; docs/reference/rng.md:224 already published that tag for mf_gaussian_noise, which is now true on this dispatch. (c) Reproducibility: shipped as a breaking `fix(random)!` (same class as #728), and I confirmed resume is bit-exact - state_dict/from_state_dict on a lambda-CGD MFNoiseState at step 4 of 10 reproduces the uninterrupted draws exactly. Live repro of the fix: with base=key(42), step-0 lambda-CGD noise is now tensor([1.9233, 0.5949, 0.2548, -0.0236, -0.8815]) while torch.randn(5, generator=generator_from_key(split(base,2)[0])) and generator_from_key(fold_in(base,0)) both give tensor([-1.1799, -1.6930, -1.7177, -0.3407, 0.8943]) - the byte-identity the OPQ demonstrated is gone - and the step-0 draw equals torch.randn(5, generator=generator_from_key(fold_in(base, MF_GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, "mf_gaussian_column", 0))) exactly. Second-moment roots are intact (_second_moment.py:38-39, 93, 102 pre-fold opaque.dpftrl.second_moment.first/.second before the mechanism root). Note (not a defect): lambda-CGD now shares the mf_gaussian_column iid stream with the dense/streaming MF path, so two MF strategies handed the same base key draw the same underlying iid vectors; that is within one documented namespace and no shipped path runs two first-moment MF mechanisms off one key.

statuses.title: lr_schedule is compare=False, so the accountant's structural merge collapses MF processes with different schedules
statuses.note: Fixed by 4bfd0c16 (fix(accounting): preserve schedule identity during composition, #883) via the third option in the OPQ fix sketch: DpProcess.__or__ no longer merges by dataclass equality. packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:396-416 adds _repeated_pld_cache_key/_has_same_repeated_pld, and :503 and :511 replace `left_leaf == right_leaf` / `r_leaf == right_leaf` with _has_same_repeated_pld(..., merged_count), which compares Repeated(leaf, count)._pld_cache_key(); those keys go through strategy_cache_key -> materialize_schedule (_schedule_fingerprint.py:14-21, 36-46), which evaluates the schedule at every step in [0, n_steps). Verified on the OPQ's own scenario (b) and beyond, at n_steps=64, bands=4, momentum=0.9: b_min_sep with linear vs exponential schedules gives eps 1.11657 vs 1.13009 and `pa|pb`, `pb|pa`, `pa|none` all return Composed (1.35368), never Repeated; the identical pair `pa|pa` still collapses to Repeated (1.34701), so the optimisation is not lost; the right-spine path ((blt|pa)|pb) and the CachedProcess path also return Composed for differing schedules and Repeated for identical ones. Same result for the cyclic-Poisson amplifier. Scenario (a) is now unreachable by a stronger route: LambdaCgdStrategy.__post_init__ (_lambda_cgd.py:111-121) and BisrStrategy.__post_init__ (_bisr.py:645-655) reject any non-None lr_schedule outright. CAVEAT, not filed as a finding because I could find no path where it changes a number: the four strategies still declare lr_schedule with compare=False (_band_mf.py:114, _blt.py:133, _bisr.py:642, _lambda_cgd.py:109), so `pa == pb` is still True for two processes with different epsilon. I checked the places that could bite - PLD caching keys on _pld_cache_key not __eq__; the BandMF/BLT coefficient lru_caches key on the materialized lr_key tuple (_band_mf.py:72-78, _blt.py:65-73), not on the strategy object; and trainer resume compares the serialized horizon_process_state (which carries the schedule recipe) as drift="dp_relevant" (_checkpoint.py:272-275) - so the residual is an API wart, not a live miscount.

statuses.title: BISR keeps n_steps-1 gradient-sized buffers, contradicting the documented p-1-vector design
statuses.note: Rewritten by d09d7b9a (fix(dpftrl): bound BISR noise state by bandwidth, #886) into a direct signed FIR convolution over a bounded newest-first ring: packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_bisr.py:321-408 _direct_bisr_streaming_matrix, with window = len(inverse_coefficients) - 1 where inverse = strategy._inv_coefs()[:n_steps] (so min(p, n_steps)-1 buffers), effective_taps = column_scales[step] * inv[:count+1] at :379-383 and next_history = (iid_noise, *state.history[:window-1]) at :399. _make_bisr_noise (:586-592) now builds that operator instead of inverse_as_streaming_matrix(bisr_strategy_coefficients(inv, n_steps)). NUMERICAL EQUIVALENCE (the task's specific ask): I ran the public mf_gaussian_noise path against the dense forward-substitution reference (BisrStrategy.streaming_matrix(n_steps=...) driven through _streaming_mf_noise with the same key, so both consume the identical iid stream) over 418 configurations - bandwidth in {2,3,4,6,12}, n_steps in {1,2,3,5,8,13,32,64,129,256}, normalized in {True,False}, momentum in {0.0,0.5,0.9,0.99}, plus three signed/non-monotone custom inv_coefficients sets ((1,-0.5,0.25), (2,-1,0.5,-0.25), (1,0.3,-0.7,0.2,0.1)) at n in {4,16,64}. Worst relative error 3.680e-15, zero mismatches, zero exceptions; the reversed-prefix-norm column_scales at :519-528 reproduce exactly the row_scale = sqrt(cumsum(coef^2)).flip(0) that _toeplitz.py:281-283 applies to the reference operator. Realized per-step sigma also matches: the NoisedPytree.noise_stddev sequence equals streaming_matrix(n).row_norms_squared(n).sqrt() to <1e-9 relative across bandwidth {2,3,5} x n {1,4,16,64,257} x normalized x momentum. MEMORY: with bandwidth=4 and a 50k-parameter leaf, len(state._inner_state.history) == 3 and 600,000 bytes at n_steps in {64, 256, 1024} - flat in the horizon, versus the linear 204 MB -> 818 MB the OPQ measured. RESUME: state_dict -> from_state_dict into a fresh template built with a different seed reproduces the remaining draws bit-exactly. The new state is fail-closed on provenance (_BisrExecutionIdentity over inverse_coefficients/normalized/n_steps/compute_dtype, checked at :351-360 and :99-125) and on layout version (:126-146). CAVEATS, both intentional and documented, neither filed as a defect: (1) legacy dense-history BISR checkpoints are rejected with CheckpointError rather than migrated (docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/bisr.md carries a "Checkpoint layout change" warning) - shipped in a non-breaking-typed commit, but the failure is loud; (2) the docs correctly no longer claim PRNG replay, only a bounded ring. Two hygiene findings from this commit are filed separately. 620 dpftrl tests and 5 CPU/Gloo distributed dpftrl tests pass.

Verified the intended behaviour now happens rather than merely the warning disappearing: with a CyclicPoisson(mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=4)), q=0.01, n_steps=64) accountant, acc.cached(a) returns an Accountant whose process is a CachedProcess (not the unchanged accountant), warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) with simplefilter('always') captures an empty list, and epsilon_at(1e-5) is 0.4292410045079024 both cached and uncached. statuses.title: Loss-scale backoff/growth is an unaccounted data-dependent adaptive choice
statuses.note: Resolved by 7f55aae5 delete(engine)!: remove data-dependent loss scaling (#889). The removal is complete and coherent. Verified: (a) git ls-files shows no packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/precision or .../api/engine/precision source files remain (only stale untracked __pycache__ dirs on disk); (b) packages/opaque-engine/pyproject.toml:43-52 no longer lists 'opaque.precision*' in [tool.setuptools.packages.find].include; (c) the private statistic itself is gone -- ClippingStats no longer carries all_finite and _all_finite() was deleted from _clipped_fun.py (grep for 'all_finite' over packages/ returns nothing); (d) grep for 'loss_scal|LossScaler|opaque.precision|engine.precision' over packages/, docs/, examples/ finds no library or doc reference; (e) docs/user-guide/precision.md was rewritten (91 lines) and now states 'Opaque does not provide dynamic loss scaling and DPTrainer does not support fp16 training' and 'Opaque therefore does not expose a loss scaler or an aggregate pre-clipping finiteness signal', with a torch.amp compatibility table saying GradScaler has 'No Opaque counterpart. statuses.title: Empty-batch short-circuit ignores dtype= and pre_clipping_transform structure
statuses.note: Fixed by f59e3c12 fix(clipping): preserve dtype and transform structure in empty-batch short-circuit (#856). statuses.title: fold_in's int/str domain disjointness is not structural
statuses.note: Fixed by e785a9f4 fix(random)!: separate fold-in input domains (#868). packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/random/_engine.py:29-38 now writes a one-byte type tag before each part (b'i' before the 16-byte signed little-endian int, b's' before the UTF-8 string). The two encodings can no longer share a byte stream because the first byte differs, so the disjointness is structural rather than conventional. Reproduced the exact OPQ-335 collision on the current tree: fold_in(key(42), 1).seed = 13284133143826279601 while fold_in(key(42), '\x01' + '\x00'*15).seed = 17548297796905688016 -- they no longer match (the finding recorded both as 2142789487919306769). fold_in(k,1) != fold_in(k,'1') still holds and split(k,n) is still exactly the integer folds. The docstring (lines 68-72) and docs/reference/rng.md:203-205, docs/user-guide/rng-key.md:100-102 were amended to say the separation is enforced by a type tag. The breaking key-derivation change was versioned: _checkpoint.py DP_STATE_BUNDLE_VERSION was bumped (4 -> 5 in this commit, now 8), and _checkpoint.py:399-403 refuses a bundle at a different version. grep confirms _stable_hash64 is the only key-derivation hash in the monorepo (the only other blake2b use is a 48-bit string fingerprint in opaque-optimizers/distributed.py:96, not key material). The cross-package stream-root registry test that the finding referenced was moved out of engine by dd65957d (#884) into tests/integration/rng/test_stream_root_namespacing.py, where it is broader (15 roots vs 9) and still runs in CI -- .github/workflows/python-tests.yml:89 declares a 'paths: tests' suite. statuses.title: Per-group adaptive clip sync reduces group counts positionally, so an empty rank receives permuted counts and thresholds diverge
statuses.note: Fix commit 23521ab6 (#888). The collective schedule is now schema-derived at both levels. (a) sync: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_distributed.py:64-71 pins `group_names = sorted(current_pg.values)` off `_current_clipping_norm` and indexes `state._num_clipped[gname]`, so the i-th reduce_scalar is bound to a key, not a dict position; the threshold loop at :78 reuses the same list. (b) every construction site of the per-group count dict is canonicalized: _adaptive.py:397, :483-487, :538-556, :584, _clipped_fun.py:248-250, :329-331, :343-348, _clipped_grad.py:269-271. I grepped every `num_clipped` / `dict.fromkeys` site in opaque-engine/opaque-dpsgd/opaque-dpftrl sources; none is left unsorted. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: (1) a 40-step 2-rank gloo run of the real stack (PoissonSampler -> adaptive_clipped_grad(PerGroup) -> sum_gradients -> sync -> gaussian_noise) with a non-sorted, non-leaf PerGroup order ({zzz:1.0, aaa:1000.0} over leaves [zzz_w, aaa_b]; sorted order ('aaa','zzz') differs from both) produced 9 partially-empty and 3 fully-empty rounds and ended with byte-identical thresholds and identical `_num_clipped` key order on both ranks; (2) a DISCRIMINATING control: I re-implemented the pre-#888 positional loop in-process and permuted rank 1's `_num_clipped` dict -- legacy DIVERGES (rank0 zzz=0.904837 vs rank1 zzz=1.105171) while the current `sync_adaptive_clip_state` agrees, proving the sync itself (not only the upstream ordering) is order-insensitive; (3) the shipped regression packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/ddp/test_dpsgd_cpu_gloo.py::test_per_group_adaptive_clipping_one_rank_empty_syncs runs on 2 real gloo ranks with one empty rank, asserts a non-sorted `bounds.values` order and all_gather_objects the thresholds; it is `pytestmark = pytest.mark.distributed`, so the PR/main distributed lane executes it.

statuses.note: Cross-checked because the defect lived half in engine/distributed/_state.py, which is in my lane. `_assert_float_equal` (packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/distributed.py:74-87) now calls assert_scalar_equal(..., atol=0.0, rtol=0.0, compute_dtype=torch.float64), i.e. exact float64 comparison rather than the float32/rtol=1e-5 default; assert_scalar_equal honours compute_dtype on both the reduction and the isclose (engine/distributed/_state.py:56-72). statuses.title: Compare optimizer drift fingerprints in float64
statuses.note: Fix commit 6ea47e6e. All five previously-untyped float comparisons are converted: the four fingerprint statistics (packages/opaque-optimizers/src/opaque/api/optimizers/distributed.py:119-122) and the plain-float leaf at :148 now route through the new _assert_float_equal (:73-86), which passes compute_dtype=torch.float64 AND atol=0.0/rtol=0.0. statuses.title: Remove unused Adadelta bc_floor plumbing
statuses.note: Fix commit 51fcf562. The dead-code removal itself is complete and correct: `grep -rn bc_floor packages/ docs/` now returns zero hits in _adadelta.py; the parameter is gone from _scale_by_adadelta's signature and `bc_floor = eps * eps` is gone from adadelta(). Every surviving bc_floor is live (_rmsprop.py:128, _adam.py:197, _radam.py:240, _ademamix.py:139). The commit also fixed a fourth doc-drift OPQ-347 did not list: the module docstring's `E[dx^2]_corrected = max(E[dx^2] - phi_dx, eps^2)` became the accurate where-fallback at _adadelta.py:26-27. No state-dict/back-compat impact: bc_floor was a closure argument, never a state field, so serialization round-trips are unaffected (232 optimizer tests pass). Caveat (filed as a finding): OPQ-347's fix sketch offered 'delete the parameter ... or actually apply it in the substitution branch and say which'. Deletion was chosen without saying which, and the substitution branch the finding inspected (_adadelta.py:252-253, `torch.clamp(v_g_corrected, min=0.0)`) turns out not to be benign - it lacks the negative-v fallback that adam/rmsprop/ademamix all apply, and adadelta diverges geometrically on a privatised g-squared stream. OPQ-347's 'No runtime behaviour change' conclusion holds for the removal but its premise that the clamp-plus-eps combination is an adequate guard does not.

statuses.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO paper's per-token weight-alignment term (Eq. 2)
statuses.note: Fixed by 0cd83ff0 (fix(alignment): add WPO token weight alignment (#1025)). Verified against the PRIMARY SOURCE, not the docstring: I downloaded arXiv:2406.11827v2 and extracted Sec. 3.3, which gives Eq. (2) as w(x,y) = exp( (1/|y|) * sum_t log[ pi(y_t|x,y_<t) / sum_{v in V} pi(v|x,y_<t)^2 ] ) and states 'We use sampled alignment as the default alignment method in WPO'; Algorithm 1 says 'Calculate the alignment weight via Eq. (2)'. Current _wpo.py:74-85 computes log_denom = logsumexp(2*logits,-1) - 2*logsumexp(logits,-1) (== log sum_v p_v^2), subtracts it from per_token_logps, masked-means and exponentiates. I reproduced Eq. (2) independently in elementary form (softmax -> p_y / sum p^2 -> log -> masked mean -> exp) and got agreement to 1.5e-8 on random non-uniform logits, and confirmed the aligned/unaligned ratio varies per example (2.51 / 2.62 / 3.19 on my 3-row probe), i.e. the original defect was real and is now gone. Parity against the INSTALLED trl 1.10.0 (trainer/dpo_trainer.py:1596-1607, 'Eq (2) of the WPO paper', lse1/lse2/log_denom form) passes: packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py::test_wpo_weights_match_trl_use_weighting, whose strict xfail was removed in the same commit, passes on non-uniform randn logits (so it is not vacuous). Call site is complete: _dpo_trainer.py:1288 now passes shifted_logits, and _dpo_trainer.py:1159-1166 multiplies the per-pair loss by w_chosen*w_rejected, matching Eq. (1). DP safety preserved: I verified torch.no_grad() is honoured under torch.func.grad and vmap(grad(...)) (gradients bit-identical to an explicitly .detach()ed weight), so the weight adds no gradient path and per-record sensitivity is unchanged. Reference values in tests/test_reference_values.py were re-derived from the formula, not from the implementation (I hand-checked wpo/geometric-mean-of-aligned-token-weights = sqrt(1 * 0.125/0.78125) = 0.4). Residual noted but NOT filed as a finding because it duplicates tracked issue #862 'Upcasting the logits to fp32': _wpo.py:77-80 materialises logits.to(float32) and then 2.0*compute_logits, i.e. two extra fp32 (..., T, V) temporaries that TRL does not create; with use_weighting=True the fused logits-free path is already disabled (_dpo_trainer.py:345-349), so this is added peak memory on top of an already logits-bound branch.

statuses.title: Calibrated DP-FTRL resume silently changes sigma mid-horizon; drift guard disabled for calibrated runs
statuses.note: Fixed by pinning, not by recalibrating. _setup_training now passes resume_runtime.noise_multiplier into _calibrate_noise whenever the saved payload is a horizon process (_dp_trainer.py:1623-1635), and _calibrate_noise returns it verbatim before any calibration runs (:4566-4583, 'Restoring whole-horizon noise multiplier'). A new pre-setup guard _validate_horizon_resume_calibration (:5647-5678, called at :1180 before _setup_training) rejects calibration-mode drift AND privacy_target_epsilon drift on horizon resumes -- the gap OPQ-319 called out explicitly ('privacy_target_epsilon is absent from _current_values_for_drift entirely'). _current_values_for_drift still returns None for noise_multiplier under calibration (:5796-5807), but that is now harmless because the multiplier can no longer change. Reproduced end to end (mf_band bands=4, cyclic_poisson, target eps=3.0, 16 steps, checkpoints at 4/8/12): phase-1 nm=1.760345458984375; resume at every checkpoint returns ratio exactly 1.000000 and eps 2.998220940430295 unchanged (the original report measured ratios 1.0248-1.0909 here). Resuming with privacy_target_epsilon 3.0 -> 2.8 now raises CheckpointError at all three checkpoints. Verified that every reachable MF pairing (mf_identity/poisson, mf_identity/balls_in_bins, mf_band/cyclic_poisson, mf_band/b_min_sep, mf_blt/balls_in_bins) and gaussian/k_out_of_t all produce DpHorizonProcess, so no DP-FTRL configuration escapes the pin. The sigma-mixed MF noise buffer is therefore unreachable by construction.

statuses.title: Stop-at-epsilon not enforced per step for Monte-Carlo samplers (auto default for 5 of 6 MF mechanisms)

Verified by construction: mf_band/auto, mf_band/b_min_sep, mf_blt, mf_bisr, mf_bsr, mf_lambda_cgd, mf_identity/auto, mf_identity/balls_in_bins and gaussian/k_out_of_t are all REJECTED; only gaussian/poisson is ACCEPTED. Since _ALLOWED_SAMPLERS (:206-218) confines b_min_sep and balls_in_bins to MF mechanisms, the original failure config (mf_band + b_min_sep + nm=1.0 + target 0.5, which ran all 16 steps to eps 3.4072 against a 0.5 cap) can no longer be constructed. The residual MC carve-out at _dp_trainer.py:1248-1252 ('a.sampling_mode not in ("b_min_sep", "balls_in_bins")') and the log-boundary fallback at :4216-4225 are now dead code for those modes, and the in-loop stop at :2024 is a per-step integer comparison for the one surviving config. Whole-suite run (949 passed) confirms nothing depended on the old acceptance.

statuses.title: DataLoader prefetch advances the allocation cursor past global_step, misaligning accountant and sampler on resume
statuses.note: Fixed on both the save and the restore side. _TrainingContext gained sampler_step_offset (:255-258), snapshotted once in _inner_training_loop after get_train_dataloader() but before iter() so prefetch cannot pollute it (:1880-1886); _save_dp_runtime clamps the checkpointed cursor to min(sampler.consumed, global_step - sampler_step_offset) (:5284-5293); and _train_once additionally normalises legacy snapshots whose consumed exceeds global_step, with a warning (:1275-1292). Confirmed every reachable sampler serialises its cursor under the key 'consumed' (dpsgd _poisson.py:221, _k_out_of_t.py:183; dpftrl _b_min_sep.py:221, _balls_in_bins.py:223, _poisson.py:261, _sequential.py:138), so the `"consumed" in sampler_state` guard covers all of them rather than only the k-out-of-t path. A single sampler instance spans all epochs (one iter() for the whole run, :1879-1888), so the offset stays valid; _reset_state_for_batch_size_retry clears _ctx and _train_dataloader (:1364-1372) so an auto_find_microbatch_size retry cannot carry a stale cursor into a negative offset. Ran the full TestDPTrainerCheckpointing class (34 passed), including the three new regression tests that assert live_consumed_at_save[0] > 2 under num_workers=2/prefetch_factor=2 and payload.sampler_state['consumed'] == global_step, plus the ignore_data_skip rebase chain.

statuses.title: num_bins drift on resume resolved in favour of the sampler snapshot while the accountant uses the new value

statuses.title: compute_loss_func and label_smoothing_factor silently ignored on the default eval path
statuses.note: The reported symptom is fixed: prediction_step's batched branch now routes through the custom loss (_dp_trainer.py:2719-2726) and rebuilds label-smoothed cross-entropy with a causal-LM-aware shift when no custom loss is set (:2728-2758, gated on the new self._is_causal_lm at :153-161). 19 new/existing contract tests pass. BUT the fix calls a callable whose documented contract is per-example-under-vmap (compute_per_example_loss docstring :2392-2395; docs/alignment/trainers.md:114 still says 'it runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op') with BATCH-ranked tensors, and validates nothing. For a rank-sensitive loss this silently produces a different eval objective than training -- the exact OPQ-325 failure scenario with a new cause. Reproduced: a per-example shifted causal-LM CE gives train objective 1.47203; default eval reports eval_loss 1.51315, while the same trainer with include_for_metrics=['loss'] reports 1.47203. Filed as finding 'compute_loss_func is invoked at two different tensor ranks'.

statuses.title: DPTrainer never consults ScheduleFreeState.x: schedule-free eval, checkpoints and saves use the wrong weight sequence
statuses.note: ebb2e2c3 added _published_params (:4670-4675), _use_published_functional_params (:4677-4689) and _use_published_model_params (:4691-4705) and wired every publication boundary: evaluate() (:3184), predict() (:3201), save_model() (:5031), checkpoint model artifacts (:5156), end-of-train restore (:1302), and _load_best_model re-seeds opt_state.x from the loaded best weights (:4920-4927). Resume reconstructs the training iterate y = (1-beta)*z + beta*x from the restored optimizer state (:5569-5573); beta round-trips through the serializer (verified: state_dict keys include 'beta', 'x.w', 'z.w'). Verified end to end with optim='schedule_free', base=adamw, beta=0.9, 8 steps: ||saved_checkpoint - x|| = 0.000e+00, ||saved_checkpoint - y|| = 1.017e-02, ||x - y|| = 1.017e-02, the post-train in-memory model equals x, and a resume reconstructs y to 0.000e+00. The trl SFT/DPO prediction_step overrides read ctx.trainable_params (_sft_trainer.py:672, _dpo_trainer.py:1317) and are reached only from evaluate()/predict(), i.e. inside the swap, so the stack-specific eval paths publish x too. Residual (not filed, low): a resumed run silently keeps the checkpoint's beta because ScheduleFreeState.update reads state.beta, so changing optim_args beta across a resume is ignored without warning.

statuses.title: _compile_with_fullgraph_fallback catches every Exception on the first call, masking non-compile failures
statuses.note: Two-step. f55c2a89 first narrowed the handler to torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException exactly as the fix sketch asked, so torch.OutOfMemoryError propagated to the trainer's OOM path. fae93a55 then deleted _compile_with_fullgraph_fallback outright and replaced it with _compile_strict_chunk (:209-219), which compiles only the tensor-only chunk kernel with fullgraph=True, dynamic=True and NO fallback and NO exception handling, so the reported double-execution and the misleading warning are both structurally unreachable. The removal is internally coherent: no dangling references (grep for _compile_with_fullgraph_fallback returns nothing), the docs were updated to drop the 'falls back with a warning' language (docs/reference/transformers.md:218, docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:216), and training_step's failure path was rebuilt around _synchronize_grad_failure (:1322-1348) which re-raises the original exception on a single process and MAX-all-reduces OOM vs non-OOM flags under DDP. The removal is NOT behaviourally free, however: what used to degrade to fullgraph=False now aborts the run, and I reproduced that torch_compile=True is unusable with Hugging Face models as a result. Filed as a separate finding.

statuses.title: SDPA sliding-window constraint silently dropped when attention_mask is None
statuses.note: The original fix (171da1c7, PR #877) is correct and I reproduced it end to end against clean out-of-process upstream references on transformers 5.15.1 / torch 2.13: with attn_implementation='sdpa', attention_mask=None, sliding_window=4, seq=12, patched logits are bit-identical to upstream for mistral (sum 7.7641603413794655 both), gemma3 (22.49240287952125 both, layer_types=['sliding_attention','sliding_attention']), cohere2 (1.5250016759855498 both) and phi3 (-6.6575579488126095 both), while the window-free control (sliding_window=64) gives visibly different values (5.1619938626, 18.4146024592, 1.7716508644, 0.2774928018). A seq sweep at the window boundary (seq=3,4,5,6,9 with sliding_window=4) is bit-exact, so the `target_length <= sliding_window` skip predicate at runtime/masking.py:370,381 has no off-by-one. HOWEVER the later compact-mask perf work (4e61b09d PR #925, d80d3f99 PR #954, Sep 6) reopened the same defect for the three families that now use vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask (mistral, ministral, gemma2): the builder elides the mask on the assumption that the family's patched SDPA forward applies the window, but the two preconditions are independently written predicates and diverge. Reproduced twice — gemma2 with attn_logit_softcapping=None (patched 19.25782148790313 == no-window reference 19.25782148790313, true reference 10.66509758651955) and mistral in train()+no_grad() with attention_dropout=0.1 and dropout=False (patched 4.206265495965454 == no-window reference 4.206265495965454, true reference 7.156000263028545). Filed as a finding.

statuses.title: Parity suite's upstream reference contaminated by unreverted module-global patches
statuses.note: parity_model_patches (_test_utils.py:256-303) now snapshots and restores the five rebindable module names plus the whole ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS object, and that restore works: I snapshotted every function, nn.Module class forward and attention registry across every loaded transformers.* module before and after `with parity_model_patches(model): pass` for llama, mistral, gemma2, gemma3, cohere2 and phi3 — zero attributes changed. tests/transformers/models/test_parity_harness.py (4 tests) passes. BUT the contamination the issue describes is still present in the suite as it actually runs: 21 sibling per-family test modules (test_cohere.py:33, test_gemma2.py:33, test_llama.py:33, test_mistral.py:36, ...) call `apply_model_patches(model, eager_attention=True)` with no restore, and pytest collects them before test_parity.py alphabetically. Probed at test_parity setup after test_llama.py: modeling_llama.eager_attention_forward is opaque's vmap_eager_attention_forward, create_causal_mask is vmap_create_causal_mask, repeat_kv is vmap_repeat_kv. Filed as a finding.

statuses.title: Unregistered HF family silently skips the dropout/batchify contract

statuses.title: Gemma2 SDPA shim installed in the process-global attention registry
statuses.note: _family.py:67-97 (_scoped_attention_functions) clones the shared AttentionInterface into a module-private instance, copies its existing _local_mapping, tags it _opaque_scoped_to, and rebinds mod.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS; _family.py:217-223 then writes 'sdpa' into that private instance. Verified in-process on transformers 5.15.1: before patching, modeling_llama.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS is modeling_utils.ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS (True). After apply_gemma2_family_patches(), modeling_gemma2's registry is a fresh instance whose 'sdpa' is vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2, while modeling_llama's registry is still the shared object with the stock transformers.integrations.sdpa_attention.sdpa_attention_forward, and so is the shared modeling_utils instance and never-patched modeling_qwen2. After additionally patching llama, gemma2 keeps its own shim and the shared registry is still stock. The clone remains correct because AttentionInterface._global_mapping (flash/flex/paged/sdpa) is a class attribute that GeneralInterface.__getitem__ falls back to, and AttentionInterface.register() writes that class mapping, so later library-wide registrations stay visible to scoped modules. Modeling modules resolve the interface through the module global at call time (e.g. modeling_mistral.py:161 ALL_ATTENTION_FUNCTIONS.get_interface(...)), so the rebind takes effect. No residual.

statuses.title: Fused activation backward mutates saved gate/up activations in place
statuses.note: The fix takes the 'detect the second traversal' option from OPQ-343's own fix sketch rather than cloning: a ctx._opaque_backward_done latch at the top of Opaque_SwiGLU.backward (swiglu.py:250-253), Opaque_GeGLU_Exact.backward (geglu.py:248-251), Opaque_GeGLU_Approx.backward (geglu.py:514-519) and Opaque_LoRA_MLP.backward (lora.py:1119-1122), so a retained-graph re-traversal raises NotImplementedError instead of reading overwritten activations. I verified the mechanism itself on this torch 2.13 build with an equivalent pure-torch autograd.Function using setup_context: the first torch.autograd.grad(..., retain_graph=True) succeeds and the second raises NotImplementedError, confirming ctx attributes persist across traversals of the same node. The in-place overwrite itself is unchanged (lora.py:726-738, 860-861, 946-947 still hand storage-sharing gate/up views to act_backward_fused), so the guarantee now rests entirely on the latch. Caveats: (1) this host has no CUDA and the kernels are Triton-only (Opaque_SwiGLU.forward at swiglu.py:218-240 calls _fg_kernel unconditionally, no CPU fallback), so the numerical consequence and the new CUDA-marked tests could not be executed here; (2) the latch was added only to the four entry points OPQ-343 named — the wider sweep across the other fused kernels (rope_embedding, rms_norm, fused_add_rms_norm, moe, Opaque_LoRA_QKV, Opaque_LoRA_W) is tracked in open issue #898 and I did not re-report it.

statuses.title: Raise the GDP grid floor so coarse grids cannot erase detectable leakage
statuses.note: Fix commit 3ccf15ba. _MIN_GRID_SIZE is now 1_000 (packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/one_run/_estimate.py:44) and OneRunEstimate.gdp() rejects anything below it (:192-195, ConfigurationError which subclasses ValueError, so the documented `Raises: ValueError` still holds). gdp() is the only door to GdpMethod: GdpMethod is in no __all__ and is reachable only through estimate.gdp() / the epsilon_at/delta_at/beta_at/advantage shortcuts (_estimate.py:199-268), which all use the 10_000 default. Reproduced the finding and the fix on the shipped code (n_in=n_out=500): u=250 -> eps 0.0 at grid 16 vs 5.108 at 10_000 (pre-fix hazard), and the now-lowest accepted grid 1_000 gives 5.075; u=350 -> 0.0 at grids 16 and 64 (the finding's exact numbers, 2.298 at 10_000) vs 2.270 at grid 1_000. Checked the floor is not merely a bigger-but-still-too-coarse constant by sweeping larger audits: m=2000 u=700/850/900 -> 2.513/0.820/0.333 at grid 1000 vs 2.577/0.876/0.385 at 10_000; m=5000 u=1800/2100 and m=10000 u=4000/4400 are identical to 4 dp between grid 1_000 and 10_000 (6.4637, 2.3316, 4.2377, 1.7912); m=10000 u=4700 gives 0.693 vs 0.727; at the largest scale the guide tabulates, m=100000 u=48800, grid 1_000 and 10_000 return the identical 3.41397 (and both raise the same OperationError at u=45000/48000, the open-#828 truncation regime). The eps=0 boundary also agrees between the floor and the default (m=1000: both positive at u=455, both 0.0 at u=465/475/485), so the floor never erases a leak the default grid resolves in the range tested. Cost claim holds too (~1.2-1.7 s at grid 1_000 vs ~8-20 s at 10_000). Docs updated consistently (docs/user-guide/auditing.md:113-115, docs/reference/auditing.md:366-367, :436) and no doc/example/test passes a grid below the floor. #829 did not change the shape of open #828: the truncation failure is grid-independent (expected error count >= n_trunc/2 regardless of the grid; verified that m=100000 u=45000 raises OperationError identically at grid 1_000 and 10_000, and TestMuAtTermination still passes), so no workaround was removed by the higher floor. One residual, filed as a finding rather than a caveat because the behavior is correct: the justification comment at _estimate.py:35-43 cites a measurement that does not reproduce. Full opaque-auditing suite: 237 passed.

statuses.title: Validate the scored CoinFlip dataset
statuses.note: Fix commits e6e3d478 (+ ff174f11 converting the two raises to ConfigurationError for the ruff TRY003 gate). CoinFlip now carries dataset_size (_coin_flip.py:168), the coin_flip() factory records it (:398), and _scoring_loader validates both length and canary-index bounds (attacks/_helpers.py:159-178) before building the loader. Both scoring call sites are covered: attacks/_loss.py:117 and attacks/_gradient.py:136 are the only callers, and both take coin_flip= and dataset= as required keyword arguments, so there is no unvalidated scoring mode. Reproduced the finding's exact scenario on the shipped code: cf = coin_flip(20-row TensorDataset, num_canaries=4/5) then loss_scores(..., dataset=cf.train_subset(ds)) now raises ConfigurationError('dataset length (19) does not match the dataset size (20) the CoinFlip was constructed from; scoring requires the full concatenated dataset, not a training subset or split') where it previously returned silently corrupted scores. No regression for the documented workflows: the crafted-canary recipe (docs/user-guide/auditing.md:256-268) and all four examples/train_*.py keep the full pre-selection dataset for scoring (e.g. examples/train_dpsgd.py:1240 'audit_dataset = train_dataset  # Keep reference before filtering'), so they still pass the new check. Caveats, both filed as findings: (1) only the length is compared, so an equal-length reordering (dataset.shuffle()/select(permutation)) is still scored silently - the fingerprint half of the fix sketch did not land; (2) the recorded dataset_size is not enforced on train_indices()/train_subset(), the sibling path that produces the training set, where an explicit size silently overrides it. A third, smaller gap: dataset_size defaults to None and the length check is skipped entirely for a directly constructed CoinFlip (_helpers.py:160), which the docs discourage but the type system permits.

The registry is reachable anonymously (https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/ -> HTTP 200) and really serves opaque wheels (opaque-0.15.0-py3-none-any.whl and later listed), so the documented install command works for the public. The unregistered-name exposure this publishing choice creates is a separate finding (1).

statuses.title: Modularize and reuse more in CI/CD
statuses.note: Modularization is real and did NOT drop lane coverage. Five reusable workflows (python-tests.yml, rust-tests.yml, qodana.yml, build-distributions.yml, validate-distributions.yml) plus four composite actions (setup-python, setup-rust, run-qodana, upload-python-coverage) are called from pr.yml and ci.yml. I compared every lane's marker expression against AGENTS.md's documented list and all 13 match exactly - PR linux-amd64 "not cuda and not mps and not slow and not distributed" (pr.yml:73), PR distributed "distributed and not cuda" (pr.yml:84), PR macOS "not cuda and not slow and not distributed" (pr.yml:114), main linux-amd64 drops "and not slow" (ci.yml:30), main CUDA locked is bare "cuda" (ci.yml:98), CUDA dependency-boundary lanes stay "cuda and not slow" (ci.yml:111,124). The authors deliberately added matrix-independent gate jobs "Python tests" (pr.yml:184-217) and "Rust tests" (pr.yml:221-235) for branch protection, and the Python gate's jq explicitly tolerates skipped python-tests-cuda* legs. Caveat: that same pattern was not applied to Qodana - "Qodana / Qodana" is required directly and its caller job is fork-guarded, so it cannot report on fork PRs (finding 7).

findings.title: DpProcess.__or__ walks the whole process tree on every composition, making heterogeneous accountant accumulation quadratic
findings.claim: 4bfd0c16 (fix(accounting): preserve schedule identity during composition, #883) replaced the O(1) structural-equality merge test in DpProcess.__or__ with `_has_same_repeated_pld`, which materialises `Repeated(left_leaf, merged_count)._pld_cache_key()`. When `self` is a Composed or CachedProcess, `_leaf_and_count()` returns `(self, 1)` (the DEFAULT implementation at _base.py:379), so `left_leaf` is the entire accumulated tree and `iter_cache_key` walks every node of it — once per composition. Accumulating n heterogeneous steps is therefore O(n^2) where it used to be O(n): `Composed.__eq__` -> `iter_eq` short-circuits on `type(x) is not type(y)` in O(1). Measured on the current tree with a freshly built extension: `Accountant() | poisson(gaussian(1.0+0.001*i), 0.01)` for n steps takes 0.233 s (n=250), 0.896 s (n=500), 3.928 s (n=1000) — a clean 4x per doubling. cProfile attributes 8.065 s of 8.069 s at n=700 to __or__ -> _has_same_repeated_pld -> iter_cache_key -> _pld_cache_key (493,490 calls). Monkeypatching `_has_same_repeated_pld` back to `self is other or self == other` restores linearity: 0.0021 s (n=200) ... 0.0318 s (n=3200). The homogeneous path (the DPTrainer's, where ctx.step_process is one cached object reused every step) is unaffected: 20,000 identical compositions take 0.07 s, because Repeated._leaf_and_count returns the small inner leaf. Severity is 'low' strictly by the rubric (no wrong result, no epsilon change), but the practical impact is large: extrapolating the measured quadratic, 10,000 heterogeneous steps costs ~6.5 minutes and 50,000 costs ~2.7 hours of pure accountant bookkeeping.
findings.failure_scenario: A user follows the documented loop in Accountant's own docstring (_accountant.py:50-60) and in docs/reference/accounting.md, but with a per-step noise schedule (or any step whose parameters change): `for i in range(50_000): acct = acct | dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(sigma_i), q)`. No two steps merge, so the Composed spine grows, and each iteration re-walks it. The loop that took ~0.5 s before #883 now takes hours, with no warning, no progress output, and no indication that the cost is in `|` rather than in PLD computation. The same shape appears in `predict_stop_step` style code and in any research script sweeping per-step parameters.

findings.title: calibrate()'s runtime-safety fallback re-runs the whole adaptive search without the union bound, while still reporting the undivided mc_failure_probability
findings.claim: calibrate() deliberately runs its adaptive probes under `probe_config = replace(overall_config, mc_failure_probability = overall / (max_iterations + 2))` (:302-309) so that, by a union bound over the two endpoint probes and up to max_iterations interior probes, every probe's Monte-Carlo confidence band holds simultaneously with probability >= 1 - beta. The OPQ-323 fix (aa15e6ac) added a fallback: if the calibrated parameter is not privacy-safe when re-evaluated under the RUNTIME config, the entire bisection is re-run — but inside `with _use_discretization(overall_config)` (:323), i.e. with each probe at the full beta rather than beta/(max_iterations+2). The returned `achieved` is then one adaptively-selected probe from that second search (:336-342), yet :353 still stamps `result.mc_failure_probability = overall_config.mc_failure_probability`, so `CalibrateResult.mc_confidence` reports 1 - beta. The honest simultaneous bound for the fallback search is 1 - (number of probes) * beta. Instrumented run (budget whose evaluate() reads get_discretization().mc_failure_probability, overall beta = 0.1, max_iterations = 30): 46 probes total, Counter({0.003125: 23, 0.1: 23}) — 23 probes at beta/32 that are thrown away, then 23 probes at the full beta that determine the returned param and achieved. The repo's own docs assert the discarded property: docs/reference/accounting.md:730-734 'calibration divides the configured failure probability across the two endpoint probes and at most max_iterations interior probes. result.mc_confidence therefore covers the adaptive search as a whole rather than only its selected final parameter.' In the fallback path that sentence is false. Secondary, and relevant to tracked issue #911 ('Monte Carlo calibration performance may be unusable'): this fallback roughly DOUBLES the Monte-Carlo probe count for exactly the mechanisms #911 is about, on top of the one extra full runtime evaluation the fix adds on every call.
findings.failure_scenario: A team calibrates BandMF + b_min_sep (or BLT + balls_in_bins) to epsilon = 3.0 at delta = 1e-5 with the default tolerance 1e-6. The probe-config bisection converges to achieved ~ 3.0 * (1 - 1e-6); the runtime-config re-evaluation differs by Monte-Carlo estimation noise (the probe config draws 3,417,797 samples versus the runtime config's 2,940,252 at the defaults — I confirmed both counts via DiscretizationConfig.resolved_num_mc_samples), and roughly half the time that noise is positive, pushing the runtime value just above 3.0 and firing the fallback. The team then publishes '(epsilon = 3.0, delta = 1e-5) with Monte-Carlo confidence 1 - 1e-6' from result.mc_confidence, when the parameter was in fact selected by up to 102 adaptive probes each holding only with probability 1 - 1e-6, i.e. a simultaneous confidence no better than 1 - 1.02e-4 — a stated confidence optimistic by ~100x on the fail-open side of the reported epsilon.

findings.title: CalibrateResult.achieved can violate the documented isclose(achieved, target, rel_tol=tolerance) contract while reporting converged=True
findings.claim: Before aa15e6ac, `result.achieved` was produced by the bisection itself and the loop only returned when `math.isclose(current, budget.value, rel_tol=tolerance, abs_tol=0.0)` held (:523). The fix now OVERWRITES it at :342 with a separate evaluation of the same process under the runtime discretization (`achieved = budget.evaluate(final_process)`, :325), which for Monte-Carlo PLDs is a different draw and therefore a different number. Nothing re-checks closeness; only privacy-safety is re-checked (:326-330). Both calibrate()'s own docstring ('In both cases, achieved and target are close under the requested relative tolerance', :139-142, and :171) and docs/reference/accounting.md:722-724 ('math.isclose(achieved, target, rel_tol=tolerance, abs_tol=0.0) is true') still assert the old invariant, and CalibrateResult.converged is still hard-coded True. Reproduced: a budget whose value moves with get_discretization().mc_failure_probability in the privacy-SAFE direction returns CalibrateResult(param=0.984375, achieved=0.515625, target=1.000000, iterations=7, converged) with math.isclose(0.515625, 1.0, rel_tol=1e-6) == False. For real Monte-Carlo mechanisms the drift is the ~0.4%-of-epsilon estimation noise OPQ-323 measured, which at the default tolerance=1e-6 breaks the isclose claim on essentially every MC calibration whose drift happens to be negative.
findings.failure_scenario: A user or a downstream check asserts the documented postcondition — `assert math.isclose(result.achieved, result.target, rel_tol=tolerance)` — or reports 'calibrated to within tolerance of the target' in a paper/run card. For any Monte-Carlo-backed process at the default tolerance the assertion fails (or the claim is wrong) even though calibrate() returned converged=True, because `achieved` is now a re-measurement rather than the converged probe. The direction is privacy-safe (over-noised), so nothing breaks silently in the epsilon sense — it is the contract and the reported convergence quality that are wrong.
