Update calibration.py:139-142 and docs/reference/accounting.md:722-724 to match whichever is chosen.

findings.title: A checkpoint budget silently overrides a stricter template budget on Accountant restore, leaving budget_exceeded on the looser cap
findings.claim: The OPQ-302 fix (51a18563) made the template's budget survive when the checkpoint has none, but left the opposite direction fail-open: when the checkpoint DOES carry a budget it always wins, and the only signal is `logger.warning(... 'the template budget is discarded.')` at :243-249. So a caller who deliberately tightens the cap on resume — `from_state_dict(Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, delta=1e-5)), saved)` — silently continues under the saved, looser cap. `budget_exceeded` (:207-222) still cannot tell 'no budget configured' (returns False) from 'the budget I was constructed with was replaced', which was the second half of OPQ-302's fix sketch ('make budget_exceeded distinguish ... (raise or tri-state)') and did not land. Reproduced: save Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(10.0, delta=1e-5)) after 5 x eps_delta(0.5, 1e-7); restore into Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, delta=1e-5)); restored._budget == EpsilonBudget(10.0, 1e-5), epsilon_at(1e-5) == 2.4999905, budget_exceeded == False even though the caller asked for epsilon <= 1.0. Mitigating: the warning does reach stderr through logging's lastResort handler in a bare process, and DPTrainer never writes a budget key (_dp_trainer.py builds a bare Accountant), so the trainer's own resume path is not affected.
findings.failure_scenario: Stage 1 of a two-stage run is trained under a generous exploratory budget (epsilon <= 10) and its accountant.json is saved with that budget embedded. Stage 2 is the production run and is written as `acct = from_state_dict(Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, delta=1e-5)), json.load(f))` followed by the documented `acct = acct | step; if acct.budget_exceeded: break` loop. The restored accountant carries the stage-1 budget of 10.0, so the loop runs ten times past the intended cap. The only evidence is one WARNING line that a training harness with a configured logging level (or `logging.disable`, or a warnings filter) will typically not surface to the operator.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_accountant.py:240-249 — `budget = template._budget`, then unconditionally replaced when `state.get("budget") is not None`, with only a logger.warning when they differ
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_accountant.py:216-222 — `if self._budget is None: return False`; no tri-state for 'replaced'
executed repro: template EpsilonBudget(1.0, 1e-05), restored EpsilonBudget(10.0, 1e-05), eps 2.499990499950025, budget_exceeded False

packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_budget_serialization.py:89-99 (test_checkpoint_budget_override_logs_warning) pins the override as intended behaviour, asserting only that the warning text appears
OPQ-302 fix sketch (NEW-FINDINGS-MASTER-LIST.md): 'make budget_exceeded distinguish "no budget configured" from "budget could not be restored" (raise or tri-state)'
findings.fix_sketch: When both the template and the checkpoint carry a budget and they differ, prefer the template (the caller's explicit, current intent) and warn, or raise a CheckpointError naming both budgets and require the caller to pick — a resume that changes the privacy cap should be an explicit decision, not a log line. Independently, give Accountant a `has_budget` / `budget` public accessor so `budget_exceeded is False` can be distinguished from 'no cap configured' without reading `_budget`.

findings.title: The OPQ-307 cross-package dependency is back in opaque-accounting's own source as an executed doctest
findings.claim: OPQ-307 was closed by moving the one test in packages/opaque-accounting/tests that imported opaque.dpftrl into the owning wheel (4867feb1). Commit 12146ec4 then turned the opaque-accounting public facade's module docstring example into a live doctest that imports a DOWNSTREAM package: `>>> import opaque.dpsgd.accounting as dpsgd_acc` (:19), followed by three statements that build and evaluate a Poisson-Gaussian process. .github/workflows/pr.yml:293 executes it with `uv run python -m doctest packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py` inside the docs job, which syncs `--all-packages`, so it passes there. But packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml declares only opaque-base and ships no extras, and opaque-dpsgd depends on opaque-accounting, not the reverse — so the doctest embedded in the wheel's own shipped source cannot run against that wheel's declared dependency set. It is not currently collected by pytest, so ARC-006's wheel-local-TEST clause is not violated today; enabling --doctest-modules for the package, or anyone running `python -m doctest` on an install of opaque-accounting alone, reproduces exactly the ModuleNotFoundError OPQ-307 described. The doctest also asserts no output, so it verifies importability rather than any numerical property.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor adds `--doctest-modules` to the accounting package's pytest invocation (or a downstream packager runs the shipped doctests as a smoke test on a `pip install opaque-accounting` environment). Collection fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'opaque.dpsgd' — the same failure OPQ-307 documented, now originating from src/ rather than tests/. In CI it stays invisible because every lane syncs --all-packages.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py:17-22 — `Example (requires ``opaque-dpsgd`` in the environment):` followed by `>>> import opaque.dpsgd.accounting as dpsgd_acc` and three more `>>>` lines

.github/workflows/pr.yml:290-293 — the docs job runs `uv run python -m doctest packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py` after `uv sync --group docs --group examples --all-packages`
packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml declares opaque-base as its only opaque dependency and no optional-dependencies
commit 12146ec4 converted the previously inert `Example::` block into `>>>` doctest form
grep over packages/opaque-accounting/tests confirms the test tree itself is now clean of cross-package imports (the OPQ-307 fix held)
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the facade docstring example against core-only surface (`acc.eps_delta(...)`, `acc.identity()`, `acc.calibrate(...)`) so it runs on opaque-base + opaque-accounting alone, and move the dpsgd-flavoured example to docs/ or to opaque-dpsgd's own facade docstring where the dependency exists. If the cross-package example must stay, mark it `# doctest: +SKIP` in the shipped source and keep the executed copy in docs/ or examples/quickstart.py, which the same CI step already runs.

findings.title: The exception taxonomy inverts two pre-existing error relationships it claims to preserve, breaking except-clauses without a breaking-change marker
findings.claim: 7b26f655 ('feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy (#760)' — a feat, not a feat!) migrated the accounting package's raise sites to the new taxonomy. The module docstring of opaque/exceptions/__init__.py:4-7 says the types 'preserve familiar Python error relationships', and for most sites they do (ValueError -> ConfigurationError/CalibrationError/PrivacyBudgetError, all ValueError subclasses). Two migrations invert the relationship instead: (a) calibrate()'s non-convergence error was `RuntimeError` and is now `CalibrationError`, which derives from ConfigurationError -> ValueError and is NOT a RuntimeError; (b) every checkpoint/codec raise in _process_codec.py and _budgets.py was `ValueError` (and one `TypeError` at budget_state_dict) and is now `CheckpointError`, which derives from OperationError -> RuntimeError and is NOT a ValueError or TypeError — even though the taxonomy ships an `InputTypeError(OpaqueError, TypeError)` that would have preserved the TypeError case. Verified by execution against the current tree: `budget_state_dict(Foo())` is 'NOT a TypeError anymore: CheckpointError' (isinstance RuntimeError True), and a non-converging calibrate() is 'NOT a RuntimeError anymore: CalibrationError' (isinstance ValueError True). The repo's own tests were updated in lockstep (test_calibrate_direction.py, test_deep_composition.py), so nothing in-tree catches the change.
findings.failure_scenario: Downstream code written against v0.15.x does `try: result = cal.calibrate(...) except RuntimeError: widen_the_bracket_and_retry()` or `try: acct = from_state_dict(Accountant(), json.load(f)) except ValueError: start_fresh()`. After upgrading, neither handler fires: the calibration failure escapes as an uncaught ValueError subclass and the malformed-checkpoint failure escapes as an uncaught RuntimeError subclass, crashing the job instead of taking the recovery path. Nothing in the commit title, the taxonomy docstring, or the calibrate docstring's Raises section flags this as breaking.
evidence: packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:27-48 — ConfigurationError(OpaqueError, ValueError); OperationError(OpaqueError, RuntimeError); CalibrationError(ConfigurationError); CheckpointError(OperationError); InputTypeError(OpaqueError, TypeError) exists but is unused by these sites
packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/exceptions/__init__.py:4-7 — 'They preserve familiar Python error relationships'
git diff 4b13d82..12146ec4 calibration.py: `- raise RuntimeError("Calibration for ... did not converge` -> `+ raise CalibrationError(`
git diff 4b13d82..12146ec4 _budgets.py: `- raise TypeError("Cannot serialize budget ...` -> `+ raise CheckpointError(`
git diff 4b13d82..12146ec4 _process_codec.py: seven `- raise ValueError(` -> `+ raise CheckpointError(` sites
executed: 'NOT a TypeError anymore: CheckpointError True' and 'NOT a RuntimeError anymore: CalibrationError True'
commit 7b26f655 subject is `feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy (#760)` with no `!` and no BREAKING CHANGE footer
findings.fix_sketch: Either make the two inverted cases multiply inherit so old handlers keep working (a `CalibrationTimeoutError(CalibrationError, RuntimeError)` for non-convergence, and `CheckpointError(OperationError, ValueError)` plus an `InputTypeError`-based raise for budget_state_dict's unregistered-type case), or accept the break and record it explicitly — amend the taxonomy docstring, list it in the release notes as a breaking change, and note it in calibrate()'s Raises section and in docs/reference/accounting.md.

findings.title: Monte Carlo shard seeds alias across nearby user seeds: seeds S and S+2 share all but one shard of the transcript corpus
findings.claim: The shard-seeding scheme introduced by the OPQ-301 fix (6e3a7d03) derives every per-shard RNG seed as `seed.wrapping_add((shard as u64).wrapping_mul(2)).wrapping_add(direction as u64)` -- i.e. the flat sequence seed, seed+1, seed+2, ... over (shard, direction) pairs. It is unique within one run (the crate test `shard_seeds_separate_adjacency_directions` only checks that), but it is not domain-separated across runs: `shard_seed(S, k, Remove) == shard_seed(S+2, k-1, Remove)` and `shard_seed(S, k, Add) == shard_seed(S+2, k-1, Add)` for every k >= 1. With the default discretization config, `resolved_num_mc_samples(2)` is 2_940_252 = 2872 shards of 1024, so a run at seed S and a run at seed S+2 draw 2871 of 2872 identical shards in each direction. Since `samples_to_pmf` is a pure function of the (sorted) sample multiset, the two runs are not independent Monte Carlo replicates -- they are the same estimate with one shard swapped. The scheme was copied verbatim from `balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:50-55` (the closed #331 fix), so both MC accountants -- b-min-sep, the auto sampler for BandMF, and balls-in-bins, the auto sampler for the correlated-noise MF mechanisms -- carry it.
findings.failure_scenario: A user wants to know how much of their reported BandMF epsilon is Monte Carlo noise, so they rerun the accountant at seeds 1000, 1002, 1004, ... and see a tight cluster, concluding the bound is stable. Measured through a fresh build of 12146ec4 (coef [sqrt .7, sqrt .3], n_steps=40, p=0.05, sigma=1.0, mc_resolution=1e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-3 -> 17354 samples = 17 shards): seeds 1000,1002,1004,1006,1008,1010 give epsilon_at(1e-2) = 1.20193276, 1.20075917, 1.20075735, 1.21128410, 1.20904665, 1.21426936 (stdev 0.0059), while seeds 1000,2000,...,6000 give 1.20193276, 1.23670628, 1.21629628, 1.18018413, 1.22964362, 1.22441048 (stdev 0.0208). The stride-2 spread is 3.5x too small, matching the sqrt(2/17)=0.34 predicted by sharing 16 of 17 shards. At the default config the sharing is 2871/2872 and the stride-2 seeds are effectively indistinguishable. This does not invalidate any individual run -- each still carries its own simultaneous KL confidence band -- but it silently defeats seed variation as a stability check and makes an apparently reproduced (epsilon, delta, seed) triple less independent evidence than it looks.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:34-37 -- `fn shard_seed(seed: u64, shard: usize, direction: AdjacencyDirection) -> u64 { seed.wrapping_add((shard as u64).wrapping_mul(2)).wrapping_add(direction as u64) }`; introduced by 6e3a7d03 (#902).
packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:50-55 -- identical arithmetic, the sibling path the fix was ported from (closed #331).
packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:710-721 -- `shard_seeds_separate_adjacency_directions` only asserts within-run uniqueness, so no test can see the cross-seed aliasing.

packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:314 -- `samples.par_sort_unstable_by(f64::total_cmp)` in `samples_to_pmf`: the PMF depends only on the sample multiset, so shared shards propagate directly into the reported epsilon.

Measured with a release build of 12146ec4 (`cargo build --release --features python-extension`) driven from Python: stride-2 seed stdev 0.00594 vs stride-1000 seed stdev 0.0208 at 17 shards (numbers quoted in the failure scenario).

packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.pyi:166 documents `seed` only as "RNG seed for reproducibility across worker counts within a fixed build" -- it makes no independence claim, which is why this is low rather than medium.
findings.fix_sketch: Hash the (seed, shard, direction) triple instead of adding them: e.g. seed a SplitMix64/ChaCha stream from `splitmix64(seed ^ (0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 * (shard as u64)) ^ (direction_tag << 63))`, or use explicit stream separation (`StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed)` + per-shard jump), so that distinct user seeds produce disjoint shard streams. Apply it to both `b_min_sep/mc.rs::shard_seed` and `balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs::shard_seed` together (the two must stay consistent, and the balls-in-bins copy is the origin of the pattern). Add a test asserting that the shard-seed sets for seed S and seed S+1 / S+2 are disjoint, not merely that they are unique within one run. Note this changes the sample corpus for a fixed seed, so cached transcript corpora and any pinned golden epsilons need regenerating.

findings.title: dpsgd_acc.poisson() lost its inner-mechanism guard and now silently amplifies already-amplified and whole-horizon processes
findings.claim: 3b22a6af (feat(accounting): generalize Poisson PLD amplification, #850) widened `_Inner` from `Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` to `DpProcess` and deleted the factory's `match inner: case Gaussian() | AdaClip() | NonPrivate(): pass; case _: raise` guard that existed at the audit baseline. `Poisson.__post_init__` now only checks `isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess)` (:40), and `pld()` falls through to `_native.poisson_pld(self.inner.pld(...), self.sample_rate)` (:162) for anything non-truncated. The generic PLD-subsampling transform is sound for the model it implements (subsample the dataset once, then run the inner mechanism), but that is not what any Opaque runtime does, and the API offers no signal that the composed expression has left the DP-SGD model. Only the truncated branch kept a type guard (:91-98); the DP-FTRL sibling `dpftrl_acc.poisson` still restricts its inner to `MfGaussian` (packages/opaque-dpftrl/.../amplification/_poisson.py:279).
findings.failure_scenario: A user who already holds a per-step process and re-applies the amplification factory - `step = dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.1), 0.01)` then `dpsgd_acc.poisson(step, 0.01) * 1000` - gets epsilon 0.00984 at delta=1e-5 where the correct DP-SGD figure is 1.51544, a 154x understatement, with no error and no warning. At the audit baseline that expression raised `TypeError: poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner mechanism, got Poisson`. Wrapping a whole-horizon process is equally silent: `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.1), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'), 0.1)` reports 0.10865 against the 0.97034 the horizon process reports on its own, and no Opaque sampler realises 'Poisson-subsample the dataset, then run k-out-of-t on the subsample'.
evidence: git show 3b22a6af -- packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py shows `-_Inner = Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` / `+_Inner = DpProcess` and the removal of the factory guard.

git show 4b13d82:packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:170-175 contains the removed `case _: raise TypeError('poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner ...')`.

Executed on the current tree with a build of the current Rust extension: single = poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01); (single*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.5154423566628403; (poisson(single, 0.01)*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.009836885508304796.
Executed: kt = k_out_of_t(gaussian(1.1), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'); kt.epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.970343695110472; poisson(kt, 0.1).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.10865088995647369.
The Gaussian path itself is unchanged and correct - cross-validated against dp_accounting (connect-dots, disc 1e-4) at four (nm,q,T) points, Opaque conservative by 7e-5 to 6.7e-4.
findings.fix_sketch: Restore a guard in `Poisson.__post_init__` that rejects inner processes which are themselves participation models or compositions: `DpHorizonProcess` (KOutOfT, BMinSep, BallsInBins, CyclicPoisson), `Poisson`/`ParallelPoisson`, and the composition wrappers `Composed`/`Repeated`. Keep the generalisation for genuine single-release mechanisms, and say in the error which construction the user probably meant (`poisson(gaussian(nm), q) * n_steps`).

findings.title: adaclip is priced with train_batch_size under sampling_mode='k_out_of_t', whose expected batch size is dataset_size*k/t
findings.claim: `_build_mechanism` wraps the base Gaussian in `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(..., expected_batch_size=expected_batch_size, num_groups=num_groups)` (:4475-4479) before it branches on `a.sampling_mode`, and `expected_batch_size = a.train_batch_size` (:1472). That is the correct expectation only for Poisson sampling, where `sample_rate = train_batch_size / dataset_size`. Under `sampling_mode='k_out_of_t'` the sampler's own expectation is `num_samples * k / t` (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_k_out_of_t.py:114-116), and `t = total_steps ~ num_train_epochs * ceil(dataset_size/train_batch_size)` (_dp_trainer.py:4758-4767), so the two agree only when the user happens to set `k == num_train_epochs`. Nothing derives, constrains or warns about `k`: `_training_arguments.py:1311-1327` checks only that `k` and `allocation` are present and that `allocation` is 'block' or 'total'. This coupling used to be structural - at the audit baseline the equivalent parameter was `num_bins = expected_steps_per_epoch`, computed from `train_batch_size` (git show 4b13d82:.../_dp_trainer.py:4264-4277), so `dataset_size/num_bins ~= train_batch_size` by construction. fc44ec8d (#761) replaced the derived `num_bins` with a free user-supplied `k` and did not re-establish the link.
findings.failure_scenario: dataset_size=10000, per_device_train_batch_size=32, num_train_epochs=3 (so total_steps=900), clipping_mode='adaptive', sampling_mode='k_out_of_t', sampling_kwargs={'k': 1, 'allocation': 'block'}. TrainingArguments accepts this with no warning (verified). The sampler yields batches averaging 10000*1/900 = 11.1 examples, and `_adaptive.py:592-600` noises the realised rate `num_clipped/batch_size` with `fraction_noise_std`, i.e. an absolute count noise of about 11.1*0.05. The accountant is handed expected_batch_size=32, i.e. sigma_b = 32*0.05. At nm=1.0 the reported whole-horizon epsilon is 0.16890 while the value at the true expected batch size is 0.45493 - a 2.7x understatement. The direction is dangerous whenever k < num_train_epochs and conservative when k > num_train_epochs.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1472 `expected_batch_size = a.train_batch_size` and :4478 `expected_batch_size=expected_batch_size` inside the `clipping_mode == 'adaptive'` wrapper, which is applied before the `if a.sampling_mode == 'k_out_of_t':` branch at :4494.
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_k_out_of_t.py:114-116 `return self._num_samples * self.k / self.t`.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:1311-1336 - the only k_out_of_t validation is presence of 'k'/'allocation' plus the allocation literal; :1284-1292 resolves adaptive to fixed only for DP-FTRL mechanisms, so gaussian + k_out_of_t + adaptive is permitted.

Executed: TrainingArguments(per_device_train_batch_size=32, num_train_epochs=3, privacy_target_epsilon=3.0, clipping_mode='adaptive', sampling_mode='k_out_of_t', sampling_kwargs={'k':1,'allocation':'block'}) is accepted with clipping_mode still 'adaptive' and zero warnings.

Executed: k_out_of_t(adaclip(gaussian(1.0), expected_batch_size=32), k=1, t=900, allocation='block').epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.16890 vs the same with expected_batch_size=10000/900=11.11 -> 0.45493 (effective_noise_multiplier 0.954480 vs 0.743294).
git show 4b13d82:.../_dp_trainer.py:1472,4264-4277 shows the pre-delta `num_bins=expected_steps_per_epoch` coupling that fc44ec8d removed.
findings.fix_sketch: Compute the accounting expected batch size from the sampling model rather than from `train_batch_size`: for `sampling_mode='k_out_of_t'` pass `dataset_size * k / n_steps` into `dpsgd_acc.adaclip` (and use it for `normalize_by` too, so the gradient scale matches the batches actually drawn). Alternatively derive `k` from `num_train_epochs` and reject an explicit `k` that contradicts it, restoring the pre-#761 structural coupling. Either way add a TrainingArguments check that `dataset_size * k / total_steps` is within a tolerance of `train_batch_size`, or a loud warning naming both values.

findings.title: the #881 random-allocation memoisation never serves a hit because epsilon_at folds a Monte-Carlo-only field into its cache key
findings.claim: `epoch_pld` is an `lru_cache` keyed on `(noise_multiplier, t, k, config)` where `config` is the whole frozen `DiscretizationConfig`, including `mc_resolution` and `mc_failure_probability`. `DpProcess.epsilon_at` overwrites `mc_resolution` with `min(configured, delta/2.0)` before calling `pld()` (packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:209-227), and `delta_at` does not, so every distinct delta and every switch between the two entry points produces a distinct cache key. The underlying transform is deterministic and reads only `discretization`, `max_grid_size` and `tail_mass_truncation` (packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:164-224) - no Monte-Carlo field reaches it. The per-process `pld_cache` already covers the repeated-identical-query case, so `epoch_pld` contributes nothing through any public entry point. The package's own regression test calls `process.pld(**_CFG)` directly rather than `epsilon_at`, so it cannot observe this (packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_k_out_of_t_cache.py:35-39).
findings.failure_scenario: A user builds an epsilon-vs-delta curve, or simply calls `epsilon_at(1e-5)` and then `delta_at(target)`, on a k-out-of-t or balls-in-bins/identity process. Each new delta re-pays the full O(G^2) geometric-grid transform. Measured at k=8, t=512 with default discretization: 16.68 s for eps(1e-5), 0.01 s for the repeat, then 16.22 s for eps(1e-6) and 16.30 s for delta_at(3.0), with `epoch_pld.cache_info()` reporting hits=0, misses=3 throughout.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_random_allocation_cache.py:29-35 - `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8) def epoch_pld(noise_multiplier, t, k, config)`.
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:209-227 - `effective_resolution = min(configured_resolution, delta / 2.0)` passed as `mc_resolution` into `self.pld(...)`.
packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:164-224 - the transform reads config.discretization / max_grid_size / tail_mass_truncation only.

Executed after clear_random_allocation_caches() + KOutOfT.pld.cache_clear(): eps(1e-5)=1.98192 in 16.68s (misses=1), eps(1e-5) repeat 0.01s (misses=1, hits=0), eps(1e-6)=2.29745 in 16.22s (misses=2, hits=0), delta_at(3.0)=6.67e-09 in 16.30s (misses=3, hits=0), then a structurally identical fresh KOutOfT instance at 1e-5 in 0.01s with misses still 3 and hits still 0 (served by pld_cache, not by epoch_pld).
packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_k_out_of_t_cache.py:35-39 asserts misses==1 across two `process.pld(**_CFG)` calls, which the per-process pld_cache satisfies on its own.
findings.fix_sketch: Key `epoch_pld` on only the fields the transform reads - e.g. `(noise_multiplier, t, k, config.discretization, config.log_x_mass_truncation_bound, config.max_grid_size, config.max_conv_grid)` - or give `DiscretizationConfig` a `deterministic_key()` projection that drops `mc_resolution` / `mc_failure_probability` and hash that. Then retarget the regression test at `epsilon_at` with two different deltas and assert `epoch_pld.cache_info().hits >= 1`.

findings.title: AdaClip.__post_init__ guards only the non-positive half of its range, so expected_batch_size=inf still prices the quantile release as free
findings.claim: The #859 validation added to close OPQ-310 checks `fraction_noise_std <= 0`, `expected_batch_size <= 0` and `num_groups < 1 or != int(...)`. None of those comparisons is true for `+inf`, so a deserialized `AdaClip` with `expected_batch_size=inf` or `fraction_noise_std=inf` is accepted, `sigma_b` becomes infinite, the `K/(4*sigma_b^2)` term in `adaclip_sensitivity` vanishes, and `effective_noise_multiplier` collapses to the bare inner multiplier. That is the same 'prices adaptive clipping as free' outcome, in the same threat model (the generic `DpProcess` codec rebuilding with `cls(**kwargs)` from a corrupted or hand-edited checkpoint), that the comment at :41-44 says the validation exists to prevent. `inner` is also left unvalidated in `__post_init__` while the factory validates it (:164-173), so a foreign inner makes the `match` in `effective_noise_multiplier` (:74-80) fall through and return `None` from a `-> float` property.
findings.failure_scenario: A checkpoint's accountant JSON is edited or corrupted so `expected_batch_size` reads `Infinity`. `from_state_dict` rebuilds the AdaClip without error and `poisson(adaclip_process, 0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5)` reports 0.1422978 - bit-identical to the unamplified-quantile `poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01)` figure, and matching to five digits the 0.14229 the original OPQ-310 report measured for `num_groups=0`. The run's adaptive-clipping quantile releases are then unaccounted. NaN in either field fails closed further downstream (ValueError from the native PLD), so +inf is the surviving fail-open value.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/mechanisms/_adaclip.py:41-44 - 'Validate here (not only in adaclip()) so direct construction and deserialization ... cannot produce an instance that prices the quantile release as free (e.g. num_groups=0).'
Same file :45-56 - the only bounds are `self.fraction_noise_std <= 0` and `self.expected_batch_size <= 0`.

Executed through the real codec (`state_dict(adaclip(gaussian(1.1), expected_batch_size=250.0, num_groups=4))`, field replaced, `from_state_dict`): expected_batch_size=inf -> ACCEPTED, effective_noise_multiplier=1.1, poisson(...,0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5)=0.1422977567766371; fraction_noise_std=inf -> identical result; the untampered process reports 0.14418327866598055 and `poisson(gaussian(1.1),0.01)` reports 0.1422977567766371.

Executed: AdaClip(inner=poisson(gaussian(1.1),0.01), ...) constructs without error and `effective_noise_multiplier` returns None; its pld() takes the generic `case _` branch and is conservative (6.038 vs 1.515 over 1000 steps), and no shipped path consumes the None.
findings.fix_sketch: Change the bounds to require finiteness: `if not math.isfinite(self.fraction_noise_std) or self.fraction_noise_std <= 0` and the same for `expected_batch_size`; do the same for `Gaussian.noise_multiplier` in mechanisms/_gaussian.py:28. Add an `isinstance(self.inner, (Gaussian, NonPrivate))` check to `AdaClip.__post_init__` so the dataclass and the factory agree, and give `effective_noise_multiplier` an explicit `case _: raise` instead of an implicit None.

findings.title: docs still name the removed random_allocation accounting factory
findings.claim: fc44ec8d (#761) deleted `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.random_allocation` and its module, folding the scheme into `k_out_of_t(..., allocation='block')`. The Monte-Carlo note in the accounting user guide still lists it as a live factory: 'Balls-in-Bins with identity_strategy(), and `random_allocation` and `k_out_of_t`, use deterministic transforms.' Verified the name is gone: `opaque.dpsgd.accounting.__all__ == ['adaclip', 'gaussian', 'k_out_of_t', 'parallel_poisson', 'poisson']`. This is the same defect class as OPQ-357 (docs naming factories that do not exist), which the #843/#844 doc sweeps were closed for; the sweeps predate or missed this line.

findings.title: IdentityStrategy.sensitivity ignores the participation schema, so bare mf_gaussian under-reports epsilon by sqrt(k) - the one sibling the participation-schema fix did not convert
findings.claim: Commit e44d6ab6 (fix(dpftrl): honour the participation schema in BandMF sensitivity, #998) converted MfStrategy.sensitivity from a single-participation column norm into a schema-aware quantity and updated BandMF accordingly, and BLT/BSR/BISR/lambda-CGD already honoured the schema. IdentityStrategy was left as `def sensitivity(self, **_) -> float: return 1.0`, which swallows min_sep and max_participations entirely. MfGaussian.pld (_mf_gaussian.py:132-141) feeds exactly that value to _native.mf_gaussian_pld as the sensitivity of the whole bare release, so a bare identity MF process with a declared multi-participation schema is priced as if each protected unit contributed once. For C = I the correct L2 sensitivity over a participation pattern pi is ||sum_{j in pi} e_j|| = sqrt(k), not 1. The same commit's new MfStrategy protocol docstring (types.py:55-59) actively blesses the exemption: "A strategy whose sensitivity is genuinely participation-independent may ignore the schema and document that it does; IdentityStrategy returns 1.0 unconditionally on that basis" - which is false under the schema-sensitivity definition the neighbouring sentences use. The API fails open: it returns a number rather than refusing, and mf_gaussian's own docstring (_mf_gaussian.py:169-171) documents min_sep/max_participations as bare-use participation bounds with no caveat.
findings.failure_scenario: A user accounts an unamplified MF run with the identity encoder and five participations at least 100 steps apart over a 1000-step horizon: `fa.mf_gaussian(1.0, identity_strategy(), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5).epsilon_at(1e-5)` returns 4.37717809602987. The mechanism actually run releases a sum whose sensitivity is sqrt(5)*C, i.e. an effective multiplier of 1/sqrt(5), whose true epsilon at the same delta is 11.480022787731485 - a 2.62x under-report, with no warning or error. Every other strategy in the same call shape scales correctly at the same (n=1000, min_sep=100, k=5) point: band_mf 1.00000 -> 2.23607 (exactly sqrt(5)), bsr 1.12413 -> 2.51364, lambda_cgd 1.00000 -> 2.23607, bisr 1.00000 -> 2.69449, blt 1.78601 -> 4.43081; identity alone stays at 1.00000 -> 1.00000. A mitigating prose caveat exists at docs/reference/accounting.md:420 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:280, but that same sentence is now wrong about BandMF (see the companion finding), so a reader who notices the BandMF half is stale has reason to discount the Identity half too.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_identity.py:45-46 - `def sensitivity(self, **_) -> float:` / `return 1.0`; class docstring :22 asserts "sensitivity == 1 for any horizon".

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/mechanisms/_mf_gaussian.py:132-141 - `sens = self.strategy.sensitivity(n_steps=n_steps, min_sep=self.min_sep, max_participations=self._effective_max_participations)` then `_native.mf_gaussian_pld(self.noise_multiplier, sens, ...)`.
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/types.py:55-59 - the post-e44d6ab6 protocol docstring declaring the Identity exemption legitimate.

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_band_mf.py:138-187 - the converted sibling: k = minsep_true_max_participations(...); if k == 1 return coefs.norm(); else sqrt(minsep_sensitivity_upper_bound(...)).

Measured on this tree (12146ec4, native rebuilt from source): sensitivity ratios sens(min_sep=100,k=5)/sens(k=1) are identity 1.0000, band_mf 2.2361, bsr 2.2361, lambda_cgd 2.2361, bisr 2.6945, blt 2.4808 (sqrt(5) = 2.2361); reported eps 4.37717809602987 vs correct 11.480022787731485 (da.gaussian(1.0/sqrt(5)).epsilon_at(1e-5)).
Repro script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/vid2.py
findings.fix_sketch: Give IdentityStrategy the same schema-aware sensitivity as its siblings: `def sensitivity(self, *, n_steps, min_sep=1, max_participations=None) -> float: return math.sqrt(minsep_true_max_participations(n=n_steps, min_sep=min_sep, max_participations=max_participations))` - for C = I the exact Theorem-2 value is sqrt(k), and _toeplitz.minsep_sensitivity_squared on the coefficient vector [1, 0, ..., 0] already returns k, so it can simply delegate. Verify the three amplified call sites are unaffected: CyclicPoisson never calls sensitivity for Identity (_poisson.py:190-192 sets effective_nm = nm directly), BallsInBins uses sigma_eff = nm/sqrt(num_epochs) (_balls_in_bins.py:190-197), and _second_moment.py:140-145 asks for min_sep=n_steps/max_participations=1 which still yields 1.0. If a fix is deferred, make it fail closed instead of fail open: raise from IdentityStrategy.sensitivity when minsep_true_max_participations(...) > 1, and drop the "may ignore the schema" clause at types.py:55-59.

findings.title: Reference and user-guide accounting docs still claim bare BandMF sensitivity accounts for one participation, contradicting the code and band-mf.md after #998
findings.claim: Both files say "Bare BandMF and Identity sensitivity currently accounts for one participation. Do not use bare calls with these strategies to budget repeated participation." Commit e44d6ab6 made BandMfStrategy.sensitivity schema-aware (_band_mf.py:138-187), so the BandMF half is false, and docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md - updated in the same commit - says the opposite twice: :74-76 ("band_mf_strategy(...).sensitivity(n_steps=..., min_sep=..., max_participations=...) returns this value [S = kappa*sqrt(k')]; pass min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1 to ask for kappa instead") and :181-186 ("Pass the participation schema you actually run under ... because the bare PLD is calibrated to the schema sensitivity S"). The Identity half is still true - and this one sentence is the only place the Identity limitation is documented at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Two readers get opposite answers from the shipped docs for the same API call. A reader of docs/reference/accounting.md avoids bare BandMF multi-participation accounting that now works correctly (a utility cost, conservative). Worse for privacy: a reader who checks band-mf.md, finds the reference sentence contradicted for BandMF, and concludes the sentence is stale, loses the only published warning about IdentityStrategy - the case that genuinely still under-reports epsilon by sqrt(k) (companion finding). Reproduced: band_mf_strategy(bands=100).sensitivity(n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5) = 2.23607 against 1.00000 at k=1, i.e. the reference sentence is measurably false for BandMF on this tree.

docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:74-76 and :181-186 - the contradicting, correct description, added by the same commit that changed the code.
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_band_mf.py:138-187 - schema-aware sensitivity with the k == 1 shortcut, so only an explicit min_sep=n_steps/max_participations=1 returns kappa.

findings.title: Empty-batch short-circuit runs pre_clipping_transform on zeros without NaN/Inf sanitization, so value-dependent transforms emit NaN gradients on empty Poisson rounds
findings.claim: The #856 fix for OPQ-334 (commit f59e3c12) made the empty-batch short-circuit call the user's pre_clipping_transform: 'zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums); transformed = pre_clipping_transform(zeros)'. On a non-empty step the transform's output passes through clip_pytree, which begins by sanitizing every leaf with torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0) (_pytree.py:599-606, and the AUTO-S twin at :463-470). The empty path has no such sanitizer: empty_clipped_grads_like returns the transformed zeros straight into clipped(zeros, max_norm=...). Any transform whose output depends on the gradient values -- the obvious case is a per-example direction/normalization transform, t / global_norm(g) -- evaluates 0/0 on the zero pytree and yields NaN. Before f59e3c12 the empty path was plain zero_grads_like and could not produce a non-finite value, so this is a regression introduced by the fix.
findings.failure_scenario: Functional DP-SGD with Poisson sampling and a normalizing pre_clipping_transform, e.g. tr = lambda g: tree_map(lambda t: t / global_norm(g), g). Reproduced on the current tree (12146ec4): clipped_grad(loss, argnums=0, batch_argnums=(1,2), clipping_norm=1.0, pre_clipping_transform=tr) returns finite gradients on a batch of 4, and tensor([nan, nan, nan]) on the empty draw. auto_clipped_grad(..., R=1.0, pre_clipping_transform=tr) and adaptive_clipped_grad(..., initial_clipping_norm=1.0, pre_clipping_transform=tr) do the same, because all three go through empty_clipped_grads_like. The NaN is not contained: feeding the empty-step ClippedPytree into gaussian_noise(noise_multiplier=1.0) returns tensor([nan, nan, nan]), so the first empty Poisson round permanently NaNs the parameters through the optimizer. The failure is silent -- no warning, no exception -- and the non-empty steps that surround it look healthy, which is precisely the shape the empty-batch short-circuit exists to avoid.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_helpers.py:120-127 -- 'zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums); transformed = pre_clipping_transform(zeros); if dtype is None: return transformed; return tree_map(lambda x: x.to(dtype) ..., transformed)' -- no finiteness handling.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_pytree.py:599-606 -- clip_pytree opens with 'pytree = tree_map(lambda t: torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0) if isinstance(t, torch.Tensor) else t, pytree)'; _pytree.py:463-470 is the identical opener in auto_scale_pytree. The non-empty path is sanitized; the empty path bypasses both.
Commit f59e3c12 diff: the old body was 'zeros = zero_grads_like(args, argnums_tuple)' with no transform, so the pre-fix empty path could not emit NaN.

Reproduced (PYTHONPATH into packages/*/src, torch 2.13.0): clipped_grad / auto_clipped_grad / adaptive_clipped_grad each return tensor([nan, nan, nan]) for an empty (0,3) batch with the normalizing transform, and gaussian_noise on that output is also all-NaN, while the same factories on a 4-example batch return finite values.
findings.fix_sketch: Sanitize the empty-batch zeros the same way the non-empty path does: in empty_clipped_grads_like, wrap the transformed tree in torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0) before the dtype cast (and do the same for the squared-stream zeros built in _clipped_grad.py:238-245). That keeps the OPQ-334 structure/dtype guarantee while restoring the pre-fix invariant that an empty draw contributes exactly zero. A stricter alternative is to derive the empty output's structure and dtype from the transform without evaluating it on data (e.g. cache the template from the first non-empty step, as empty_collate does) so a value-dependent transform is never called on a synthetic input at all.

findings.title: clipped_fun and auto_clipped_fun, the public power-user primitives, have no empty-batch handling at all and die with an opaque IndexError on a zero-length batch
findings.line: 688 (outputs = vmapped(...) in clipped_fn, no batch_size==0 short-circuit anywhere in the module); packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_auto.py:111 (auto_clipped_fun delegates)
findings.claim: OPQ-334 and its fix (#856) are entirely about clipped_grad's empty-batch short-circuit being structure- and dtype-faithful. The sibling primitives one level down -- clipped_fun and auto_clipped_fun, which packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/fun.py:14-16 advertises as 'stable, supported public API ... for users who need to clip arbitrary per-example outputs or compose custom pipelines' -- have no empty-batch path at all. They call torch.func.vmap directly on a zero-length batch and fail inside vmap. The module that produces the empty batches, packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/functional/_collate.py:4-8, states that empty batches 'arise from any Poisson-style sampler', so the two supported surfaces disagree about whether an empty batch is a supported input.
findings.failure_scenario: A user composes a custom DP pipeline with opaque.api.engine.clipping.fun.clipped_fun (or auto_clipped_fun) plus PoissonSampler and empty_collate, exactly as the collate docstring describes. On the first round where the Poisson draw is empty the loader hands the clip function a zero-length batch and the step dies with 'IndexError: select(): index 0 out of range for tensor of size [0] at dimension 0' raised from inside vmap -- an error that names neither the empty batch nor the API. Reproduced on the current tree for both clipped_fun(f, clipping_norm=1.0, batch_argnums=1) and auto_clipped_fun(f, R=1.0, batch_argnums=1) with a (0,3) batch, while the same calls on a (4,3) batch return correctly. Fail-closed, so no privacy or numerical consequence -- but it aborts training mid-run and the same configuration works through clipped_grad, which is why the inconsistency is a trap rather than a documented limit. This predates the delta; the #856 fix did not extend the empty-batch contract down to these primitives.
evidence: grep for 'numel() == 0|batch_size == 0|is_empty|empty_batch' over packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py returns only line 327, which is inside _compute_clipping_stats (a stats-shaping branch, not a short-circuit); _auto.py has no 'empty' occurrence at all.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:686-688 -- 'vmapped = _vmap(per_example_fn, in_dims=(None, *in_dims), out_dims=out_dims, randomness="same"); outputs = vmapped(kernel_clipping_norm, *args, **kwargs)' is reached unconditionally.

Contrast packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py:222-258, where _empty_batch_response exists precisely so 'downstream buffers stay stable across empty and non-empty draws'.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/fun.py:14-16 -- 'These are stable, supported public API'.
Reproduced: both factories raise IndexError('select(): index 0 out of range for tensor of size [0] at dimension 0') on a zero-length batch and succeed on a 4-example batch.
findings.fix_sketch: Give clipped_fun the same guard clipped_grad has: when batch_size_from_args(args, batch_argnums) == 0, skip the vmap and return an empty-batch-shaped output. Because clipped_fun's output structure is fun's, not the parameter pytree's, the template cannot be derived from args -- so either require the caller to supply an out_template= for the empty case, or (cheapest) raise a ConfigurationError naming the empty batch and pointing at clipped_grad, so the limitation is explicit rather than an IndexError from inside vmap. Either way document it in fun.py's module docstring next to the 'stable, supported public API' sentence.

findings.title: tree_leaves still returns [] for a ClippedPytree/NoisedPytree -- the same silent fail-open shape #869 hardened in global_norm, in the same module
findings.claim: 3acdba01 (#869) fixed OPQ-333 by making global_norm raise InputTypeError on the four DP wrapper types, telling the caller to use .pytree. Its immediate neighbour in the same file, tree_leaves, keeps the old behavior: it flattens with optree (for which ClippedPytree is an unregistered frozen dataclass and therefore a single opaque leaf) and then filters with 'isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)', so a wrapper is dropped and the function returns []. The module header even pairs the two -- 'Only tensor leaves are considered for tree_leaves and global_norm' -- so after the fix the file's own stated contract no longer matches one of the two functions it names. tree_flatten, by contrast, returns the wrapper as a leaf, so the three sibling entry points now disagree three ways on the same input.
findings.failure_scenario: A user inspecting DP gradients writes 'total = sum(t.numel() for t in tree_leaves(grads))' or 'max(t.abs().max() for t in tree_leaves(grads))' on the ClippedPytree that clipped_grad returns (the same mental slip OPQ-333 documented for global_norm). tree_leaves returns [], so the sum is 0 and the max raises a bare 'max() arg is an empty sequence' with nothing pointing at the wrapper. Reproduced on the current tree: tree_leaves(clipped({'g': tensor([3.,4.])}, max_norm=1.0)) -> [], while global_norm on the same value now raises InputTypeError and tree_map returns a correctly scaled ClippedPytree. No privacy or numerical consequence -- a monitoring or sizing figure silently reads zero.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:126-127 -- 'flat, _ = _ot.tree_flatten(tree); return [x for x in flat if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)]'.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:377-400 -- the guard 3acdba01 added, covering ClippedPytree, NoisedPytree, SecondMomentClippingOutput, SecondMomentNoiseOutput.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/pytree.py:16 -- 'Only tensor leaves are considered for tree_leaves and global_norm' (now true of only one of them).

Reproduced side by side on 12146ec4: tree_leaves -> [] ; global_norm -> InputTypeError ; tree_flatten -> ([ClippedPytree(...)], PyTreeSpec(*)) ; tree_map -> ClippedPytree(pytree={'g': tensor([6., 8.])}, max_norm=2.0).
findings.fix_sketch: Mirror the global_norm guard in tree_leaves (and tree_flatten_with_paths, which has the same shape): raise the same InputTypeError naming .pytree when the top-level argument is one of the four wrapper types. Keeping a bare wrapper at the root silently empty is the fail-open the #869 fix set out to remove; nested non-tensor leaves can still be dropped as documented.

findings.title: per_group's own documented example raises for any model with 11 or more layers because substring patterns collide by prefix
findings.line: 116 (Examples block), also 69 and 71 in the module docstring
findings.claim: The Examples block in per_group's docstring -- the file the #867 fix rewrote to document the new unmatched-pattern rule -- ends with '>>> per_group(params, **{f"layers.{i}": norms[i] for i in range(32)})'. Patterns are matched as plain substrings of the leaf's dotted display path ('matches = [pat for pat in all_patterns if pat in display]', _per_group.py:142), so for i >= 10 the pattern 'layers.1' is a substring of the display path 'model.layers.10...'. The parameter then matches two patterns and per_group raises the multi-match ConfigurationError at _per_group.py:155-162. The example therefore cannot work for any transformer with 11+ layers, which is every model family the project supports.
findings.failure_scenario: A user copies the shipped per-layer example to give each layer its own clipping norm on an 8B LLaMA. Reproduced on the current tree with 12 synthetic layers: ConfigurationError("Parameter path ('model.layers.10.mlp.weight') ... matched multiple patterns: ['layers.1', 'layers.10']. Each parameter must match exactly one pattern."). The same call with 10 layers succeeds, so the example looks correct in a small smoke test and fails on the real model. Fail-closed, but the error names neither the substring semantics nor a workaround, and the docstring gives no hint that patterns must be mutually non-prefixing.
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:116 -- '>>> per_group(params, **{f\'layers.{i}\': norms[i] for i in range(32)})'.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:142 -- 'matches = [pat for pat in all_patterns if pat in display]' (substring, not regex, not anchored).
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:155-162 -- the multi-match ConfigurationError.
Reproduced: 12-layer params raise the multi-match error on 'model.layers.10.mlp.weight'; the identical call with 10 layers succeeds.
findings.fix_sketch: Change the example to a form that is prefix-free, e.g. '>>> per_group(params, **{f"layers.{i}.": norms[i] for i in range(32)})' (trailing dot) and state in the Args/Notes that patterns are matched as substrings of the dotted display path, so one pattern must not be a prefix of another. Optionally add a construction-time check that no explicit pattern is a substring of another and raise with the trailing-dot suggestion, which turns the confusing per-parameter multi-match error into a single actionable message.

findings.title: DPTrainer documents per-group clipping_norm keys as regex when they are plain substrings, and offers no allow_unused_patterns escape hatch
findings.claim: The trainer documentation says clipping_norm 'accepts a positive scalar (global clipping), a dict keyed by regex on parameter names with a "fallback" entry (per-group clipping)'. The implementation does no regex matching: _dp_trainer.py:1538-1546 strips 'fallback' and forwards the remaining keys verbatim as per_group(**patterns), and per_group matches with 'pat in display' (_per_group.py:142). Per-group clipping norms feed the accountant through PerGroup.effective = sqrt(sum v^2), so which leaves land in which group is sensitivity-relevant, and the doc misdescribes the rule that decides it. The same call site also hard-codes the new strict behavior: it never passes allow_unused_patterns, so the legitimate 'one config across architectures' case that #867 added the flag for is unreachable from DPTrainer.
findings.failure_scenario: A user follows the doc and writes clipping_norm={'model\\.layers\\.\\d+\\.self_attn': 0.1, 'fallback': 1.0}. As a substring that key matches nothing. Before 88f81f2f this degraded silently -- every attention parameter was clipped at the fallback 1.0 instead of 0.1, which is the OPQ-332 defect. After 88f81f2f it raises ConfigurationError at trainer construction, so the outcome is now fail-closed; the residual harm is that the error contradicts the documentation the user was following, and there is no supported way to express a deliberately-partial pattern set from TrainingArguments. Separately, the substring rule quietly widens intent: a doc-following user who writes 'layers.1' expecting an anchored regex match gets every layer whose index starts with 1 (10..19) or, if they also list 'layers.10', the multi-match error.
evidence: docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:92-93 -- 'clipping_norm accepts a positive scalar (global clipping), a dict keyed by regex on parameter names with a "fallback" entry'. Present unchanged at both 4b13d82 (line 84) and 12146ec4 (line 93), so two doc-reconciliation commits in the delta (ba39783d, 12146ec4) passed over it.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1537-1546 -- 'fb = float(mgn["fallback"]); patterns = {k: float(v) for k, v in mgn.items() if k != "fallback"}; ... clip_norm = per_group_clipper(trainable_params, fallback=fb, **patterns)' -- no regex compilation, no allow_unused_patterns.
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_per_group.py:142 -- substring matching.
docs/user-guide/clipping.md:365-373 gets it right ('matched by substring against the patterns, using the leaf's display path'), so the two user-facing docs contradict each other.
grep for 'allow_unused_patterns' over the repo finds it only in opaque-engine source, its tests and docs/user-guide/clipping.md -- nothing in opaque-transformers.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace 'keyed by regex on parameter names' with 'keyed by substring patterns matched against the parameter's dotted display path (see the clipping guide)', and cross-link docs/user-guide/clipping.md so the two pages agree. If cross-architecture pattern sharing is meant to be supported from the trainer, plumb an allow_unused_patterns knob (for example a TrainingArguments.clipping_kwargs key) through to the per_group_clipper call at _dp_trainer.py:1541; otherwise state in the doc that every non-fallback key must match at least one trainable parameter and that the trainer fails at construction if one does not.

findings.title: DDP resume collapses every rank's Poisson sampler stream to rank 0's, so co-indexed records across shards are perfectly co-included while the accountant still prices independent Poisson
findings.line: 1871-1877 (restore on every rank), 3945-3950 (per-rank fold, fresh runs only), 5195-5197 + 5279-5284 (snapshot written only where should_save is true), 3878-3885 (the acknowledging comment)
findings.claim: Under DDP the trainer shards the dataset per rank and folds the rank into the sampler key (`sampler_key = fold_in(sampler_key, self._ddp.rank)`, _dp_trainer.py:3949) precisely so each rank draws an INDEPENDENT Bernoulli(q) mask over its shard -- that independence is what makes the union of the shard draws an exact Poisson sample of the whole population, which is the hypothesis `acc.poisson` prices (_dp_trainer.py:1492: 'The accountant uses regular ``acc.poisson`` over the global rate'). The sampler snapshot, however, is written ONLY by the saving rank (`_save_dp_runtime` is inside `if _distributed.should_save(...)`, :5195-5197, default world-rank-0) and is restored by EVERY rank (`ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)`, :1875-1877). Every sampler family restores the stream key straight out of the snapshot (`stream_key=RngKey(seed=int(sd['key_seed']), ...)`: dpsgd/_poisson.py:261, dpsgd/_k_out_of_t.py:218, dpftrl/_poisson.py:304, dpftrl/_b_min_sep.py:259, dpftrl/_balls_in_bins.py:260), so after a resume all W ranks replay rank 0's stream and select the SAME LOCAL OFFSETS in their disjoint shards. Records sharing a local index across shards are then included or excluded together with probability 1 for the rest of training. The in-file comment at :3869-3873 asserts the opposite -- 'the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected' -- which is false: Poisson amplification needs independence across records, not just the right marginal.
findings.failure_scenario: torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 (or 4/8) with the default save_strategy='steps'; the job is preempted and restarted with resume_from_checkpoint. REPRODUCED END TO END on a real 2-rank gloo DPTrainer run (TinyForCausalLM, 16 examples, per_device_train_batch_size=2, save_steps=2, resume from checkpoint-2): fresh-run stream keys were rank0=1950457451192556855, rank1=16528425509808239245 (independent); after resume BOTH ranks reported 1950457451192556855 -- rank 0's key -- on every step. Confirmed at the sampler level too: two PoissonSamplers seeded with fold_in(key(42),0)/fold_in(key(42),1) emit different index lists ([[4,5,8],[1,5,9,14,15],...] vs [[3,5,7,13,15],[0,6],...]); after both are rebuilt through from_state_dict with rank 0's snapshot they emit byte-identical lists. QUANTIFIED: at sigma=1.0, q=0.01, delta=1e-5, a single step of the intended independent Poisson mechanism has eps = 0.1995 (numerically integrated hockey-stick on the standard dominating pair N(0) vs (1-q)N(0)+qN(1)). The neighbouring pair actually realised by W=2 correlated groups -- D={w}, D'={w,z} where w and z share one Bernoulli, i.e. (1-q)N(0)+qN(1) vs (1-q)N(0)+qN(2) -- gives eps = 2.3989 for the same one step; at W=4 it is 3.1387. So the reported per-step epsilon understates a worst-case realisable one by ~12x at W=2 in this configuration, with no warning, no accountant signal, and nothing in docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md (which has no resume section at all).
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:3945-3950 -- `if self._ddp.world_size > 1: sampler_key = fold_in(sampler_key, self._ddp.rank)` (fresh-run per-rank independence)

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1871-1877 -- every rank overwrites its rank-folded template with `from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)`

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:5195-5197 + 5279-5284 -- `_save_dp_runtime` (which serialises ctx.current_sampler) runs only under `_distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp)`, i.e. world rank 0 by default (trainer/_distributed.py:211-222)

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_poisson.py:219 and :261 -- key_seed serialised and restored verbatim; identical pattern at _k_out_of_t.py:181/218, dpftrl/_poisson.py:259/304, _b_min_sep.py:219/259, _balls_in_bins.py:221/260

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:3869-3873 -- 'the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected'; :3878-3885 -- 'resuming a DDP run currently restores rank 0's per-rank key on every rank, re-introducing the cross-rank correlation after the resume point'
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1487-1494 -- 'The accountant uses regular ``acc.poisson`` over the global rate.'
Numerical hockey-stick at sigma=1, q=0.01, delta=1e-5: independent Poisson eps=0.1995, W=2 correlated-group pair eps=2.3989, W=4 eps=3.1387
docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md has no mention of resume, per-rank sampler snapshots, or this caveat; no runtime warning is emitted
findings.fix_sketch: Write per-rank sampler snapshots (dp_runtime_rank<N>.pt, unconditional of should_save, mirroring the existing per-rank RNG snapshot that _save_rng_state already writes) and restore each rank's own; or, minimally, re-apply the per-rank fold after deserialisation (requires storing the pre-fold root in the snapshot so the cursor replay stays meaningful). Failing either, refuse to resume a world_size>1 run from a single-rank snapshot, or emit a loud runtime warning and stop calling the resulting epsilon a Poisson-amplified bound. Also correct the :3869-3873 comment: independence, not the marginal, is what the amplification theorem needs.

findings.title: The distributed guide documents a `ddp_shard` TrainingArguments option (and a `global` / parallel_poisson accounting mode) that does not exist; its launch example raises TypeError
findings.line: 36-44 (runnable example), 46-58 (mode table + the paragraph added by #1007)
findings.claim: docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md publishes `ddp_shard` as a TrainingArguments field, shows it in the page's only runnable launch snippet (`ddp_shard="per_rank"`), and documents two modes with different privacy accounting: `per_rank` ('disjoint shard per rank, Poisson accounting') and `global` ('full dataset per rank with rank-folded streams and `parallel_poisson` accounting'). No such argument, attribute, or branch exists anywhere in the codebase -- `grep -rn ddp_shard --include=*.py packages/` returns nothing, TrainingArguments has only ddp_backend and ddp_timeout, and the trainer unconditionally does local_shard(...) at world_size>1 (_dp_trainer.py:3909-3913) with acc.poisson accounting (:1492). `parallel_poisson` exists as an accounting factory but no trainer path ever selects it. This is not a leftover of a removed feature: the option has never existed (it dates from the original DPTrainer commit 65518ae4) -- and the delta made it worse, because a624a34b (#1007) ADDED a paragraph describing per_rank divisibility requirements, and ba39783d (#1026, 'docs(transformers): reconcile trainer references') swept this page without catching it.
findings.failure_scenario: A user following the distributed guide copies the launch snippet verbatim and gets `TypeError: TrainingArguments.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ddp_shard'` (reproduced). Worse for the reader who does not copy it: they believe a `global` mode exists in which every rank sees the full dataset and the run is priced with parallel_poisson, and may size their noise/epsilon expectations around a mode the trainer cannot enter -- so the page's only statement about which amplification theorem applies to multi-GPU training is unverifiable against the code.
evidence: docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md:41 `ddp_shard="per_rank",` inside the documented TrainingArguments(...) call; :46-58 the `## ddp_shard modes` section
`grep -rn 'ddp_shard' --include=*.py packages/` -> no matches; `[f.name for f in dataclasses.fields(TrainingArguments) if 'ddp' in f.name]` -> ['ddp_backend', 'ddp_timeout']
Reproduced: `TrainingArguments(output_dir='/tmp/x', ddp_shard='per_rank')` -> `TypeError: TrainingArguments.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ddp_shard'`
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:3893-3913 -- the world_size>1 branch always trims and local_shards; there is no alternative branch
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1487-1494 -- accounting is always acc.poisson over the global rate

git log --oneline 4b13d82..12146ec4 -- docs/user-guide/distributed-trainer.md -> ba39783d (#1026 docs reconciliation), a624a34b (#1007, which added the per_rank divisibility paragraph on top of the nonexistent option)
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the ddp_shard kwarg from the example and either delete the `## ddp_shard modes` section or rewrite it as a statement of the single implemented behaviour ('at WORLD_SIZE>1 the training population is trimmed to a multiple of WORLD_SIZE, sharded disjointly with local_shard, and accounted with acc.poisson at the global rate'). If a `global` / parallel_poisson mode is actually wanted, file it as a feature rather than documenting it as shipped.

findings.title: #1008 left the sibling `save_model` barrier untouched: a saving-rank failure there still strands peers in barrier()
findings.claim: fee28d2f (#1008) introduced `_distributed.checkpoint_barrier(ddp, local_error)` whose docstring says it 'Replaces plain ``barrier()`` calls that let a saving-rank failure leave peers blocked forever' (trainer/_distributed.py:234-243), and rewired the three stages of _save_checkpoint to use it (:5203, :5212, :5239). `save_model` -- the other rank-gated write path, with exactly the same shape (`if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp): ... self._save_model_artifacts(target) ...` followed by a plain `_distributed.barrier(self._ddp)`) -- was not converted. It is now the only surviving `_distributed.barrier(...)` call site in the trainer.
findings.failure_scenario: All ranks call trainer.save_model(dir) after training (the documented usage; the barrier comment 'so non-saving ranks don't proceed before the save lands' presumes it). Rank 0's save_pretrained fails -- read-only or full output volume, a safetensors shared-tensor error, an NFS hiccup. REPRODUCED on 2-rank gloo with an injected _save_model_artifacts failure: rank 0 raised the real `RuntimeError: injected save_model artifact failure` while rank 1 blocked inside barrier() and only unblocked when rank 0's process exited, surfacing `RuntimeError: [gloo/transport/tcp/pair.cc:537] Read error ... Connection reset by peer` instead of any diagnostic about the save. If the caller wraps save_model in try/except (natural for a best-effort final save) rank 0 stays alive and rank 1 blocks for the full store timeout. Not a privacy or numerical issue -- the cost is a hang / an unrelated gloo error in place of the clean cross-rank abort #1008 was written to provide.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:5031-5044 -- `if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp): ... self._save_model_artifacts(target) ...` then `if not _internal_call: _distributed.barrier(self._ddp)` with no try/except and no failure flag

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_distributed.py:234-243 -- checkpoint_barrier's own docstring: 'Replaces plain ``barrier()`` calls that let a saving-rank failure leave peers blocked forever'
`grep -n '_distributed.barrier(self._ddp)' _dp_trainer.py` -> only line 5044 remains; all three _save_checkpoint stages use checkpoint_barrier (:5203, :5212, :5239)

Live 2-rank gloo repro: rank0 'RAISED RuntimeError: injected save_model artifact failure'; rank1 'RAISED RuntimeError: [gloo ... pair.cc:537] Read error ... Connection reset by peer. This is typically caused by a remote worker hanging'
The #1008 regression test scenario_checkpoint_save_failure only covers _save_checkpoint (via an on_save callback); no scenario exercises save_model

Add a scenario_save_model_failure alongside scenario_checkpoint_save_failure in packages/opaque-transformers/tests/distributed/_ddp_runner.py.

findings.title: Adadelta's private second-moment branch diverges geometrically: it lacks the negative-v fallback every sibling optimizer applies
findings.claim: In the `noisy_squared_grads` (private second-moment) branch, `_scale_by_adadelta` guards a possibly-negative second moment with only `v_g_corrected = torch.clamp(v_g_corrected, min=0.0)` (:253). Adam (:197 `torch.where(v_hat > 0, v_hat, m_hat * m_hat).clamp(min=bc_floor)`), RMSprop (:128 `torch.where(v > 0, v, g * g).clamp(min=bc_floor)`) and AdEMAMix (:138) all instead fall back to the squared signal, which is precisely what _adam.py:194-196 documents: 'Falling back to the squared first moment keeps the update magnitude approx 1 ... instead of collapsing the denominator to bc_floor -> infinity update.' In Adadelta the collapse is worse than a one-off spike because it feeds back: clamping to 0 makes `rms_g = sqrt(0 + eps) = 1e-3` (:115-117, :267), so `coef = rms_dx_prev / rms_g` is inflated ~1e3x, `dx = coef * g` is inflated, and `v_dx_new = rho*v_dx + (1-rho)*dx*dx` (:273) carries the inflation into the next step's `rms_dx_prev`. The loop multiplies the update by roughly 4-50x per step.
findings.failure_scenario: A user follows docs/reference/optimizers.md:110-140 ('mf_gaussian_noise(..., second_moment_strategy=...) returns a paired output that Opaque optimizers route automatically') and picks adadelta - the LR-free optimizer the same docs recommend 'when learning-rate tuning is hard' (optimizers.md:48). _chain.py:138 sees `noisy_squared_grads` in the scaler signature and routes the privatised stream in (:172-181). In any realistic high-dimensional DP setting the per-coordinate second-moment signal (~||g||^2/d) is far below the per-coordinate release noise, so ~50% of the stream is negative. Reproduced at d=100000 with unit-norm clipped gradients and per-coordinate noise 1/sqrt(d) (49.99% of the squared stream negative): adadelta max|update| goes 2.0e-2, 8.5e-2, 3.5e-1, 1.2e0, 4.7e0, 1.9e1 ... 9.96e8 at step 19, while adamw/rmsprop/ademamix stay at 8-80 throughout. The repo's own guard test uses the identical fixture and a `< 10.0` bound but runs ONE step: re-running tests/test_adadelta.py:296-307 verbatim for 8 steps instead of 1 gives 1.51e-1, 7.20e0, 3.44e2, 1.64e4, 7.83e5, 3.74e7, 1.78e9, 8.52e10 - it breaches its own assertion at step 2. Training silently blows up to inf/NaN within ~15-25 steps with no exception and no warning. Verified the mechanism by patching :253 to `torch.where(v_g_corrected > 0, v_g_corrected, updates_node * updates_node).clamp(min=eps * eps)` in an overlay copy: the same 20-step run then stays flat at ~1e-2.
evidence: _adadelta.py:252-253 `if noisy_squared_grads is not None: v_g_corrected = torch.clamp(v_g_corrected, min=0.0)` - no where-fallback, no positive floor
_adadelta.py:115-117 `def _rms(tensor_or_zero, eps): return (tensor_or_zero + eps).sqrt()` with adadelta default eps=1e-6 (:321), so a fully clamped v_g gives rms_g = 1e-3
_adadelta.py:267-273 coef = rms_dx_prev / rms_g; dx = coef * updates_node; v_dx_new_t = rho * v_dx_node + (1 - rho) * dx * dx  <- the feedback path
_adam.py:194-197 and _rmsprop.py:126-128 and _ademamix.py:136-140: the sibling branches all use torch.where(v > 0, v, signal^2).clamp(min=bc_floor)

_bias_correction.py:31-34 asserts 'The separate bc_floor clamp seen in some optimizers belongs to the *private second-moment* branch (noisy_squared_grads), where v-hat ... can be genuinely negative' - adadelta has that branch and has neither the clamp nor the fallback
_chain.py:138 and :172-181 auto-route SecondMomentNoiseOutput.noisy_squared_grads into any scaler whose update() accepts the kwarg, adadelta included

tests/test_adadelta.py:296-307 test_negative_squared_stream_bounded asserts `updates[k].abs().max().item() < 10.0` but performs exactly one update from a fresh state (v_dx = 0), so the feedback loop has not started; the same fixture run 8 steps breaches the bound at step 2 (1.51e-1, 7.20e0, 3.44e2, 1.64e4, 7.83e5, 3.74e7, 1.78e9, 8.52e10)

Realistic-regime repro d=100000, ||g||=1, per-coord noise 1/sqrt(d): frac(noisy g^2 < 0)=0.4999; adadelta step19 max|u| = 9.96e8 vs adamw 4.12e1, rmsprop 7.65e1, ademamix 4.16e1
findings.fix_sketch: Mirror the sibling branches at _adadelta.py:253: `v_g_corrected = torch.where(v_g_corrected > 0, v_g_corrected, updates_node * updates_node).clamp(min=eps * eps)` (this is what OPQ-347's second option, 'actually apply it in the substitution branch', asked for; verified to hold max|update| at ~1e-2 over 20 steps in the realistic regime). Then extend tests/test_adadelta.py:296 from one update to at least 5-8, matching what tests/test_adam.py:502 already implies, so the bound can actually fail. If Adadelta is instead deemed unsupported with private second moments - as Adafactor explicitly is (_adafactor.py:34-38) - raise from the branch rather than diverging, and drop the auto-routing for it.

findings.title: RAdam's private second-moment branch collapses the denominator to bc_floor - the exact failure mode _adam.py documents guarding against - and has no boundedness test
findings.claim: RAdam's `noisy_squared_grads` branch computes `r_t * (m / bc1) / (torch.clamp(v / bc2, min=bc_floor).sqrt() + eps)` (:240). With the default eps=1e-8 (:301), bc_floor = eps*eps = 1e-16 (:348), so every coordinate whose privatised second moment is non-positive gets denominator sqrt(1e-16) + 1e-8 = 2e-8 and an update inflated by ~5e7. This is verbatim the behaviour _adam.py:194-196 calls out and guards against with `torch.where(v_hat > 0, v_hat, m_hat * m_hat)` before the same clamp. RAdam is the only one of the five substitution-capable scalers (adam, rmsprop, ademamix, radam, adadelta) that applies the clamp without the where-fallback, and the only one with no negative-stream regression test at all (grep 'negative' in tests/test_radam.py returns only test_negative_weight_decay).
findings.failure_scenario: radam + mf_gaussian_noise(..., second_moment_strategy=...) via the documented paired-stream flow. RAdam's rectification term r_t is None for the first steps, so the branch looks healthy; once r_t activates the update jumps by ~6 orders of magnitude. Reproduced with the repo's own test fixture from tests/test_adam.py:502 (sq = -ones, both streams at noise_stddev 0.1, lr=1e-3): max|update| is 1.51e-4 for steps 0-4, then 1.95e2, 2.47e2, 2.92e2 from step 5 - it would breach the `< 10.0` bound that the adam/rmsprop/ademamix versions of that test assert, if the test existed for radam. In the realistic d=100000 regime (49.6% of the state nu non-positive) max|update| goes from 1.66e-2 at step 4 to 1.75e4 at step 5 and stays at ~4e4, ~1000x adamw's bounded ~20 on identical inputs. Training does not NaN immediately - it silently takes enormous steps once rectification turns on.
evidence: _radam.py:237-245 the noisy_squared_grads branch: `r_t * (m / bc1) / (torch.clamp(v / bc2, min=bc_floor).sqrt() + eps)` - clamp only, no torch.where fallback
_radam.py:301 eps default 1e-8; :348 `bc_floor = eps * eps` = 1e-16 -> denominator floor 2e-8
_adam.py:194-197 the contrasting guard and its comment: 'instead of collapsing the denominator to bc_floor -> infinity update'
_rmsprop.py:128, _ademamix.py:138 - same where-fallback present
tests/: test_adam.py:502, test_rmsprop.py:239, test_ademamix.py:128 all have test_(second_moment_)negative_squared_stream_bounded; tests/test_radam.py has none
Repro with the test-suite fixture, 8 steps: radam 1.51e-4 x5 then 1.95e2, 2.47e2, 2.92e2 (adamw/rmsprop/ademamix flat at ~1e-3)
Repro at d=100000, ||g||=1, per-coord noise 1/sqrt(d): frac(nu <= 0) = 0.496 every step; max|update| 1.66e-2 (step 4) -> 1.75e4 (step 5) -> 3.95e4 (step 11)
findings.fix_sketch: At _radam.py:240 apply the same guard as _adam.py:197: `v_eff = torch.where(v / bc2 > 0, v / bc2, (m / bc1) * (m / bc1)).clamp(min=bc_floor)` and divide by `v_eff.sqrt() + eps`. Add tests/test_radam.py::test_negative_squared_stream_bounded modelled on tests/test_adam.py:502 but run for enough steps that r_t is not None (>= 6 with the default betas), asserting the same `< 10.0` magnitude bound.

findings.title: Exact-equality drift audit (#872) false-positives on bit-identical optimizer state when ranks differ in intra-op thread count
findings.claim: The #872 fix sets atol=0.0 and rtol=0.0 on _assert_float_equal, so the four tensor fingerprint statistics (:119-122) are compared bit-exactly. Those statistics are computed locally with `t.sum()` / `(t*t).sum()` on each rank (:118-120), and torch's CPU reduction is order-dependent in the number of intra-op threads, so two ranks holding byte-identical state can produce fingerprints differing by 1 ULP and the audit raises. The docstring's mitigation - ':78 Assumes ranks share an intra-op thread count, which standard launchers guarantee' - is an assumption, not a guarantee: it does not cover heterogeneous CPU core counts or per-node OMP_NUM_THREADS, nor differing CPU vector ISAs across nodes, nor mixed accelerator models. Before #872 the rtol=1e-5 default absorbed this class of artifact.
findings.failure_scenario: Two gloo ranks constructed with an identical AdamState (a 5,000,000-element float32 leaf built from the same seed, so bit-equal on both ranks) but torch.set_num_threads(4) on rank 0 and (1) on rank 1. Both ranks raise OperationError: "AdamState.mu['w'].sumsq mismatch across ranks: min=4997394.779571936, max=4997394.7795719365" - a 1-ULP difference produced entirely by the audit's own local reduction. A user who calls sync(opt_state) / sync_optimizer_state defensively on a CPU cluster whose nodes are not thread-count-identical gets a hard training abort on healthy state. The same local nondeterminism is directly observable single-process: the same 5M-element float32 tensor gives sum = -650.3623083472755 at 1/4/8 threads but -650.3623083472758 at 2 threads, and sumsq = 4997394.779571936 at 1/2 threads vs 4997394.7795719365 at 4/8. Blast radius is limited because no production path calls this audit - _dp_trainer.py:2231 syncs only clip_state and aux, never ctx.opt_state.
