findings.title: The optimizer chain silently discards a privately-released second-moment stream for optimizers that do not consume it, inflating first-moment noise by sqrt((D1+D2)/D1) for nothing
findings.claim: `_route_second_moment_output` (:169-176) inspects the moment scaler's signature (:138) and, when it does not accept `noisy_squared_grads`, does `return _route_noisy_pytree(updates.noisy_grads)` (:172-173, the drop is at :173) - dropping `updates.noisy_squared_grads` with no error, no warning and no record. adafactor, adagrad, sgd and lion all take that path. Meanwhile the paired mechanism that produced the output has already split a joint Mahalanobis budget across the two streams: paired_noise_stddevs (packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/noise_allocation.py:165-174) sets sigma1 = nm*sqrt(D1*(D1+D2)) instead of the single-stream nm*D1, so the first-moment gradient the optimizer does use carries a factor sqrt((D1+D2)/D1) more noise - sqrt(2) ~ 1.41x for equal sensitivities - purchased for a release that is thrown away.
findings.failure_scenario: A user builds mf_gaussian_noise(..., second_moment_strategy=...) as shown in docs/reference/optimizers.md:113-138 and pairs it with adafactor - which the same page (:50) calls the 'Recommended default for DP LM fine-tuning'. Every step, the privatised g-squared release is discarded; the run consumes exactly the same epsilon as a correctly-paired run but trains on ~41% noisier gradients than a single-stream run at the same epsilon would have. Verified: feeding SecondMomentNoiseOutput whose squared stream is a constant -1e9 to adafactor, adagrad, sgd and lion changes nothing in the resulting update and emits zero warnings (adafactor update[0,0] = 8.170018e-04 either way). The reference table at docs/reference/optimizers.md:44-52 lists second-moment support per optimizer, but nothing at runtime tells a user they picked a combination that wastes budget. Privacy accounting stays valid and conservative - this is a utility and budget-hygiene defect, not a privacy loss.
evidence: _chain.py:138 `accepts_second_moment = "noisy_squared_grads" in moment_update_params or any(...VAR_KEYWORD...)`

_chain.py:169-173 `if not isinstance(updates, SecondMomentNoiseOutput): return _route_noisy_pytree(updates)` / `if not accepts_second_moment: return _route_noisy_pytree(updates.noisy_grads)` - the squared stream is simply not referenced
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/noise_allocation.py:165-174 sigma1_g = nm*sqrt(D1_g*S), S = sum(D1+D2) - the first stream is deliberately over-noised to pay for the second
packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_second_moment.py:146-151 calls paired_noise_stddevs with both sensitivities whenever second_moment_strategy is set
Repro: adafactor/adagrad/sgd/lion given SecondMomentNoiseOutput with a -1e9 squared stream produce identical updates and no warnings (warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) empty)
_adafactor.py:34-38 documents that the substitution path is not offered for Adafactor, but the chain drops the stream rather than surfacing that at the call site
findings.fix_sketch: At _chain.py:172-173, raise a ConfigurationError naming the optimizer and pointing at the supported set, or at minimum emit a warnings.warn once per optimizer instance: a SecondMomentNoiseOutput reaching a scaler that cannot consume it is always a misconfiguration, since the user paid for the second release. A softer variant is to let mf_gaussian_noise/clipped_grad accept the optimizer (or a capability flag) so the paired budget split is only taken when the consumer exists.

findings.title: get_training_chat_template silently changes the rendered conversation text (Jinja trim_blocks eats the newline after the wrapped expression)
findings.claim: The transform inserts the Jinja BLOCK tags {% generation %} / {% endgeneration %} around a {{ ... }} expression. transformers compiles chat templates with trim_blocks=True (transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py::_compile_jinja_template), so a newline immediately following a block tag is deleted from the output. Whenever the wrapped expression is followed in the template source by a literal newline — the normal shape of a multi-line, non-whitespace-controlled template — inserting {% endgeneration %} there removes a newline the original template emitted. The only acceptance gate, _generation_block_marks_only_assistant (:469-520), inspects the CONTENT of the generation spans ('assistant probe in generated', 'user probe not in generated', 'system probe not in generated') and never compares the transformed render against the original render, so the change passes validation.
findings.failure_scenario:
A user runs DPTrainer with SFTConfig(assistant_only_loss=True) on any of these real Hub tokenizers. _sft_trainer.py:426-428 permanently overwrites processing_class.chat_template with the transformed template, and every row is then tokenized from it. I rendered the original and the transformed template with the same 4-message conversation through transformers' own _render_with_assistant_indices and got, for HuggingFaceH4/zephyr-7b-beta, TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 and stabilityai/stablelm-2-zephyr-1_6b, identically: original '<|user|>
U1</s>
<|assistant|>
A1</s>
<|user|>
U2</s>
<|assistant|>
A2</s>
' vs training '<|user|>
U1</s>
<|assistant|>
A1</s><|user|>
U2</s>
<|assistant|>
A2</s>' — one turn-separator newline dropped after every assistant turn, and the trailing newline dropped. The model is therefore fine-tuned on token sequences that the model's canonical chat template never produces; at inference time a freshly loaded tokenizer emits the newline the model was trained never to see. The assistant mask itself stays correct, so nothing warns.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_chat_template.py:326-332 — `return (template[:abs_start] + _GEN_START + template[abs_start:abs_end] + _GEN_END + template[abs_end:])` with _GEN_START/_GEN_END the block tags defined at :36-37.

packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_chat_template.py:469-520 — the validator only builds `generated = ''.join(rendered[start:end] ...)` and asserts probe membership; there is no comparison of `rendered` against the untransformed template's rendering.
transformers 5.15.1 utils/chat_template_utils.py::_compile_jinja_template compiles with trim_blocks=True, which is what deletes the newline after {% endgeneration %}.

Reproduced on the real templates: transformed zephyr-7b-beta template contains "...{% elif message['role'] == 'assistant' %}\n{% generation %}{{ '<|assistant|>\\n'  + message['content'] + eos_token }}{% endgeneration %}\n{% endif %}..."; rendering original vs transformed differs as quoted in the failure scenario (script: scratchpad/repro_trim.py, scratchpad/probe_all.py).

3 of the 9 real Hub templates that the transform currently accepts show the divergence (zephyr-7b-beta, TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0, stablelm-2-zephyr-1_6b); llama3, gemma-2, Qwen2.5, Phi-3, Mistral-v0.3 and SmolLM3 are unaffected because they are single-line or fully whitespace-controlled.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:426-428 — `processing_class.chat_template = get_training_chat_template(processing_class)` makes the transformed template the one that actually tokenizes training data.
findings.fix_sketch: Make _generation_block_marks_only_assistant reject any candidate whose full rendered string differs from the untransformed template's rendering for the same probe messages (it already renders both shapes; add `rendered_base == rendered_candidate`). Independently, emit whitespace-neutral markers — e.g. wrap as `{%+ generation +%}` / `{%+ endgeneration +%}`, or re-append the swallowed newline — so the insertion is text-preserving by construction rather than by validation.

findings.title: apply_chat_template_with_mask reports a per-row truncation as a chat-template misconfiguration and aborts the whole dataset map
findings.claim: 62a96b72 replaced `if not assistant_masks:` with `if not _has_assistant_tokens(assistant_masks):` (:114, helper at :136-142), so an all-zero mask now raises. But the function already validated the template up front at :93. By the time :114 runs, a False result can only mean 'this particular conversation rendered no assistant tokens', which for the trainer's call is caused by truncation, not by the template. The error text nonetheless asserts 'This means the chat template does not carry the {% generation %} / {% endgeneration %} markers' and tells the user to install markers that are already installed.
findings.failure_scenario: SFTConfig(assistant_only_loss=True, max_length=N) calls apply_chat_template_with_mask(..., max_length=N, truncation=True) from _sft_trainer.py:455-461 inside dataset.map. Any single conversation whose system+user prefix exceeds N tokens truncates before the first assistant token, so assistant_masks is all zeros and the call raises ConfigurationError — aborting preparation of the entire dataset with a diagnosis that points at the tokenizer instead of at max_length. Reproduced end to end with the real Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct tokenizer: get_training_chat_template succeeds, the untruncated conversation yields completion_mask.sum() == 16, and the same conversation with max_length=64, truncation=True raises 'ConfigurationError: apply_chat_template_with_mask: the tokenizer returned no assistant-token mask. This means the chat template does not carry the ...markers...'. Before 62a96b72 the same row passed with an all-zero mask (nll_loss clamps its divisor to 1, so it contributed a 0.0 loss rather than a NaN), so the change trades a silently useless row for a hard abort with the wrong remedy.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_completion_mask.py:93-103 — the template-level guard already ran and passed before line 114 is reached.

packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_completion_mask.py:114-124 — `if not _has_assistant_tokens(assistant_masks): raise ConfigurationError(... 'This means the chat template does not carry the ... markers' ...)`.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:455-461 — `apply_chat_template_with_mask(processing_class, example[chat_col], max_length=max_length, truncation=max_length is not None)` inside the dataset.map at :436-441.
Reproduced with the real Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct tokenizer: untruncated mask sum = 16; `max_length=64, truncation=True` -> ConfigurationError with the quoted text.
git show 62a96b72 -- .../_completion_mask.py: the old guard was `if not assistant_masks:`, which is True only for None/empty, so an all-zero list previously passed.
findings.fix_sketch: Split the two conditions. Keep the template check at :93 as the ConfigurationError. For an empty mask on a rendered row, raise a distinct error whose message names truncation/max_length and the offending conversation (or return the row with an all-zero mask and let the caller drop it), so a single over-long conversation does not abort dataset preparation with a misdirected remedy. The trainer can then filter or report the row.

That regex and that bail are unchanged at _chat_template.py:450-452. The fix took the documentation route instead, which the OPQ fix sketch allowed — but the commit simultaneously added a parametrized test whose ids are 'meta-llama-3-8b-instruct', 'gemma-3-1b-it' and 'shared-chatml' while the actual parameters are _LLAMA_3_TEMPLATE (genuinely the real Llama-3 template), _GEMMA_INLINE_TEMPLATE (a synthetic one-line `{% set role = 'model' if ... %}` template that is not gemma-3-1b-it and lacks its second content expression) and _CHATML_TEMPLATE (which has an explicit `{% elif message['role'] == 'assistant' %}` branch, i.e. it is not the shared-expression ChatML the finding named).

packages/opaque-alignment/tests/data/test_chat_template.py:74-81 — _GEMMA_INLINE_TEMPLATE is a one-line synthetic template; :40-48 — _CHATML_TEMPLATE carries an explicit `{% elif message['role'] == 'assistant' %}` branch.

packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_chat_template.py:450-452 — `content_pat = re.compile(r"\{\{-?\s*[^}]*\bcontent\b[^}]*-?\}\}")` / `if len(content_matches) != 1: return None`, unchanged by 62a96b72.

Running the real google/gemma-3-1b-it chat_template and the canonical shared-expression ChatML through the current tree: both raise ConfigurationError('could not identify and validate an assistant-only render path'); instrumenting the helpers shows content matches == ["{{ message['content'] | trim }}", '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}'] and all of _wrap_assistant_content / _wrap_shared_content_expression / _wrap_gemma_shared_expression / _wrap_shared_or_clause returning None.

findings.fix_sketch: Either rename the ids to describe the shapes actually exercised ('shared-set-content', 'inline-role-mapping', 'explicit-assistant-branch'), or make the named templates real: exclude `raise_exception(...)` expressions from content_pat (e.g. require the expression to reference `message` or a role/content variable) so the real gemma-3 template's single renderable content expression is found, and add a shared-expression ChatML strategy. findings.title: language_modeling_collator(completion_only_loss=True) now silently supervises the full sequence for rows that carry no completion_mask
findings.claim: 08d8b1dc inverted the maskless-row behaviour of the public collator. Before, a row without completion_mask had all real tokens set to -100 under completion_only_loss=True (fail-closed: no prompt tokens are ever supervised). Now the `if has_completion_mask and cm is not None` branch (:147) simply does not fire, the labels stay a full copy of input_ids, and the `elif has_completion_mask` branch (:158-161) additionally reports that row's completion_mask as all ones — asserting those prompt tokens ARE completion tokens.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller using the exported opaque.alignment.sft.collator.language_modeling_collator directly (not through DPTrainer) asks for completion_only_loss=True and feeds a batch in which some or all rows lack completion_mask — e.g. a hand-assembled mixed dataset, or a preprocessing step that dropped the column. Reproduced: `language_modeling_collator(pad_token_id=0, max_length=16, completion_only_loss=True)([{'input_ids':[1,2,3]},{'input_ids':[4,5,6]}])` returns labels [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] (full supervision, and no completion_mask key at all); the mixed case `[{'input_ids':[1,2,3],'completion_mask':[0,1,1]},{'input_ids':[4,5,6]}]` returns labels [[-100,2,3],[4,5,6]] and completion_mask [[0,1,1],[1,1,1]]. The prompt tokens the caller asked to exclude are trained on, and the returned mask claims they are completions. DPTrainer itself is guarded (_sft_trainer.py:406-417 raises when completion_only_loss=True has neither a prompt-completion dataset nor a completion_mask), so this is a defect of the public primitive rather than the default trainer path.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/sft/collator/_language_modeling.py:147-161 — `if has_completion_mask and cm is not None: ... elif has_completion_mask: completion_mask_t[i, :seq_len] = 1` with no branch that honours _completion_only_loss for a maskless row.
git show 08d8b1dc: the removed code was `else: if self._completion_only_loss: labels_t[i, :seq_len] = _IGNORE_INDEX` and `elif self._completion_only_loss: labels_t[i, :seq_len] = _IGNORE_INDEX`.
Reproduced against the current tree through the public facade opaque.alignment.sft.collator.language_modeling_collator, outputs as quoted in the failure scenario.
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:406-417 — the trainer-level guard that keeps the default path off this branch.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the TRL-matching default but make it explicit rather than silent: when _completion_only_loss is set and a row supplies no completion_mask, either raise (the collator already knows both facts) or emit a one-shot warning naming the row index, instead of flipping that row to full supervision and reporting an all-ones completion_mask. At minimum, do not fabricate completion_mask=1 for tokens the caller never marked as completions.

findings.title: mpo_combine changed its documented exception type from KeyError to ConfigurationError (a ValueError) in a non-breaking commit
findings.claim: 7b26f655 (feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy (#760)) replaced `raise KeyError(...)` with `raise ConfigurationError(...)` in the public mpo_combine. ConfigurationError derives from OpaqueError and ValueError (packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:27) — it is NOT a KeyError — so existing `except KeyError:` handlers around mpo_combine stop catching. The taxonomy's own docstring markets this property ('preserve familiar Python error relationships'), which it does for the ValueError/TypeError/RuntimeError swaps elsewhere in the same commit but not for this one.
findings.failure_scenario: User code that composes MPO heads and guards the weights/losses key mismatch with `except KeyError:` — the contract the previous docstring promised ('Raises: KeyError: If weights names a key that is absent from losses') — now propagates an uncaught ConfigurationError. The change shipped under a `feat` title without the `!` marker that AGENTS.md requires for breaking changes, so it does not appear as a breaking change in the changelog for the release line that contains it.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_mpo.py:58 and :70 — `raise ConfigurationError(...)` where the pre-delta code raised KeyError (git show 7b26f655 -- .../_mpo.py).
packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:27 — `class ConfigurationError(OpaqueError, ValueError)`; no KeyError in the MRO.
git show 7b26f655 diff of _mpo.py also rewrites the docstring from 'Raises: KeyError' to 'Raises: ConfigurationError', confirming the contract change was intentional and undeclared as breaking.
Commit subject is `feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy (#760)` — no `!` and no BREAKING CHANGE footer.
findings.fix_sketch: Either make the mpo_combine failure a type that is still a KeyError (e.g. a dedicated `class MissingLossKeyError(ConfigurationError, KeyError)` in the taxonomy, mirroring how ConfigurationError keeps ValueError) or record the change as breaking in the changelog for the release that contains 7b26f655.

findings.title: torch_compile=True aborts on the first training step for every Hugging Face model: the fullgraph fallback was deleted, not narrowed
findings.claim: fae93a55 (#979) replaced _compile_with_fullgraph_fallback with `_compile_strict_chunk`, which is a bare `torch.compile(fn, backend=backend, mode=mode, fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` with no exception handling. The compiled chunk kernel wraps `vmap(grad_and_value(per_example_loss))`, i.e. the whole model forward, and Hugging Face Transformers 5.15.1 calls `logger.warning_once` inside that forward (`use_return_dict` deprecation in configuration_utils, `loss_type=None` in modeling_utils). Dynamo rejects logging.Logger methods under fullgraph=True, so the first training step raises `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported` and the run dies. Before fae93a55 the same exception was caught (`except torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException` after f55c2a89 #891, `except Exception` at 4b13d82) and the step was retried under fullgraph=False, so the run completed.
findings.failure_scenario: `DPTrainer(model=LlamaForCausalLM(...), args=TrainingArguments(..., torch_compile=True))`; `trainer.train()` raises on step 1 with `Unsupported: logging.Logger method not supported for non-export cases ... Developer debug context: <Logger transformers.configuration_utils>.warning_once('`use_return_dict` is deprecated!...')`. Reproduced on a 2-layer LlamaForCausalLM and on the repo's own tiny GPT-2 + LoRA fixture, with clipping_mode fixed, adaptive and auto, on backends aot_eager and inductor -- 8/8 configurations fail. Monkeypatching `_compile_strict_chunk` back to fullgraph=False makes the identical run succeed (train_loss=3.64476 for all three clipping modes), proving the deleted fallback is the only thing that was making the feature work on HF models.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:209-219 — `def _compile_strict_chunk(fn, *, backend, mode): return torch.compile(fn, backend=backend, mode=mode, fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` (no try/except, no fallback)

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:4344-4368 — `_grad_compiler` returns `lambda fn: _compile_strict_chunk(fn, backend=backend, mode=mode)`; it is threaded into every clipping factory as `_chunk_compiler` (:4400, :4412, :4424)

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:588-601 — the compiled `_chunk_kernel` body is `vmapped = _vmap(_per_example_fn, ...); outputs = vmapped(kernel_clipping_norm, *chunk_args)`, i.e. the user's full model forward is inside the fullgraph region
git show fae93a55 — removes `_compile_with_fullgraph_fallback` (the `except torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException` handler that #891 had just corrected for OPQ-327) and adds `_compile_strict_chunk`

Reproduced: LlamaForCausalLM(2 layers, hidden 32) + apply_model_patches + torch_compile=True -> FAIL Unsupported for clipping_mode in {fixed, auto, adaptive}; same model with `_compile_strict_chunk` monkeypatched to fullgraph=False -> OK, train_loss=3.64476 in all three

packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/test_compile_and_kernel_args.py:112-140 — `test_torch_compile_runs_poisson_training_strictly` is the only end-to-end compile test and it uses the synthetic `_TinyLM`, which emits no warning_once; the full transformers suite (949 passed, 16 skipped) is green with the feature broken
docs/reference/transformers.md:218 — `| torch_compile | bool | False | Compile each tensor-only microbatch gradient/clipping kernel with fullgraph=True. |` (no mention that HF models will abort)
findings.fix_sketch: Either restore a narrow fallback (catch torch._dynamo.exc.TorchDynamoException on the first call, log, and recompile the same chunk with fullgraph=False, while explicitly re-raising torch.OutOfMemoryError so _synchronize_grad_failure still sees it first-hand -- exactly the f55c2a89 shape), or keep fullgraph=True and add the HF logging functions to `torch._dynamo.config.ignore_logging_functions` inside `_grad_compiler` before compiling. Either way add an end-to-end regression test that runs DPTrainer(torch_compile=True) against a real transformers causal-LM (a 2-layer LlamaForCausalLM is enough) rather than a synthetic nn.Module, since that is the gap that let this ship.

findings.title: dynamic=True from the Poisson graph-reuse change makes clipping_mode="auto" + torch_compile crash even with no graph break
findings.claim: afa0247f (#989) added `dynamic=True` to `_compile_strict_chunk` to reuse one compiled graph across realized Poisson batch shapes. On the trainer's stack (torch.func.functional_call plus the opaque-patches `_reparametrize_module` recompute patch) that flag makes Dynamo's speculation log diverge for the AUTO-S clipping path specifically: `clipping_mode="auto"` + `torch_compile=True` aborts with `torch._dynamo.exc.SpeculationLogDivergence`, while `fixed` and `adaptive` compile and run on the identical model. The trigger is the flag, not the mode: with `dynamic` left unset (PyTorch's automatic dynamic shapes, the pre-#989 behaviour) or with `dynamic=False`, AUTO-S compiles and produces bit-identical results to eager.
findings.failure_scenario: A model with no graph breaks (so finding #1 does not mask this): `TrainingArguments(clipping_mode="auto", clipping_kwargs={"gamma":0.01}, torch_compile=True)`. `trainer.train()` raises `SpeculationLogDivergence: SpeculationLog diverged at index 626 ... Expected: opaque/api/patches/torch/checkpoint/reparametrize_recompute.py:37 (STORE_ATTR)`. Reproduced in a fresh process at per_device_train_batch_size in {2,6} with and without an explicit microbatch_size, on backends aot_eager and inductor -- 6/6 auto runs fail, 4/4 fixed and adaptive runs on the same model succeed. Variant sweep on the same run: fullgraph=True+dynamic=True FAIL, fullgraph=False+dynamic=True FAIL, fullgraph=True+dynamic=False OK (eps 2.866847, loss 0.881958), fullgraph=True+dynamic unset OK (identical numbers) -- so `dynamic=True` alone is the cause.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:209-219 — `torch.compile(fn, backend=backend, mode=mode, fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)`; `dynamic=True` was added by afa0247f

findings.title: compute_loss_func is now invoked at two different tensor ranks; a per-example loss silently reports a different eval objective
findings.claim: The #819 fix makes the default (batched) eval path call `self._compute_loss_func(output, custom_labels)` on a batched ModelOutput, but training and the include_for_metrics=['loss'] eval path call the same callable under vmap with the leading batch dim stripped (`compute_per_example_loss`, :2452-2456, docstring at :2392-2395). Nothing validates the rank and nothing warns. A loss that indexes the leading axis -- the natural way to write a causal-LM objective under the documented per-example contract -- therefore computes a different quantity at eval than at training, and when sequence length equals vocab size it does so without raising. The token-weighted eval aggregation at :2946-2966 then multiplies that scalar by the batch's real-token count as if it were a per-token mean CE, compounding the error. docs/alignment/trainers.md:114 still states the SFT custom loss 'runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op', which is no longer true of the path SFTTrainer takes for loss_type='nll' (it delegates to `super().prediction_step` at _sft_trainer.py:647-650).
findings.failure_scenario: `compute_loss_func=lambda out, labels: F.cross_entropy(out['logits'][:-1], labels[1:])` (the documented per-example causal-LM shift) with eval_strategy='steps', metric_for_best_model='eval_loss', load_best_model_at_end=True. Reproduced on a causal-LM-shaped module with T=V=4: the training objective mean over the eval set is 1.47203; the default batched eval reports eval_loss=1.51315 (the function shifted along the BATCH axis and treated the sequence axis as the class axis, no exception); the same trainer with include_for_metrics=['loss'] reports 1.47203. Best-model selection, early stopping and every logged eval curve are driven by the 1.513 sequence. When T != V the same code path raises a shape error at eval instead, so a user who previously got a (wrong but harmless) built-in eval loss now gets a crash.
evidence: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2719-2726 — `if self._compute_loss_func is not None: custom_labels = next((labels_kwargs[k] for k in label_keys if k in labels_kwargs), None); loss = self._compute_loss_func(output, custom_labels)` on the batched forward output

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2452-2456 — the training/per-example call: `labels = next((inputs[k] for k in self._label_names if k in inputs), None); loss = self._compute_loss_func(output, labels)` where `inputs` is 'One example's input dict (under vmap; the caller stripped the leading batch dim)' (:2409-2412)

Reproduced: train objective 1.4720335006713867; default eval_loss 1.5131527185440063; include_for_metrics=['loss'] eval_loss 1.472033441066742; direct batched call of the same fn 1.5981327295303345 with logits[:-1].shape=(3,4,4) and labels[1:].shape=(3,4)

docs/alignment/trainers.md:114 — 'A custom `compute_loss_func(outputs, labels) -> scalar` is honoured **only** on the `"nll"` path (it runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op — no `num_items_in_batch`)' — not updated by 25bb4ed7

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:647-650 — non-DFT loss types delegate to `super().prediction_step(...)`, so SFT nll + compute_loss_func lands on the batched call

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:2946-2966 — the returned scalar is weighted by `int((labels[..., 1:] != _IGNORE_INDEX).sum())`, which only makes sense for a per-token-mean CE
The new tests added by 25bb4ed7 (test_trainer_contract.py) only use rank-agnostic losses (`F.cross_entropy(output['logits'], labels)` on 2-D logits), so the divergence is not covered
findings.fix_sketch: Make the contract single-ranked: on the batched branch, vmap the user callable over the batch (a Python loop over the batch dim reusing one forward's outputs preserves the per-example contract and the existing token weighting), or, if the batched call is kept, validate it: assert the returned value is 0-dim and emit a one-shot RuntimeWarning naming the rank change the first time `_compute_loss_func` is called from `prediction_step`'s batched branch. Update docs/alignment/trainers.md:114 and the `compute_per_example_loss` docstring to state whichever convention wins, and add a regression test with a leading-axis-sensitive loss asserting that default eval and include_for_metrics=['loss'] agree.

findings.title: Compact SDPA sliding-window elision reopens OPQ-337: gemma2 with softcapping disabled attends to the full context
findings.claim: The perf work in 4e61b09d (PR #925) and d80d3f99 (PR #954) made mistral, ministral and gemma2 use vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask, which returns None (no mask at all) whenever _can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window (runtime/masking.py:78-107) holds, on the assumption that the family's patched SDPA forward applies the look-back limit itself. That assumption is encoded twice, in two independently written predicates, and they diverge. (a) vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 (attention.py:670-738) consumes `sliding_window` only inside its `if softcap is not None:` branch (line 683); when Gemma2Attention passes softcap=self.attn_logit_softcapping=None (modeling_gemma2.py:282) it falls through to `return vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(...)` at line 729, whose signature has no sliding_window parameter at all — the window is dropped and plain causal SDPA runs. (b) The builder admits the elision when `not torch.is_grad_enabled() or config.attention_dropout == 0.0` (masking.py:103-105) while vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window requires the runtime `dropout == 0.0` (attention.py:297); in train mode under no_grad with a non-zero attention_dropout the builder elides and the forward declines. Nothing asserts that the forward actually applied what the builder skipped, so both paths fail open. This is exactly the defect OPQ-337 reported, in sibling paths that 171da1c7 (#877) fixed correctly and that later perf commits reopened.
findings.failure_scenario: Gemma2 with attn_logit_softcapping=None (a config people set precisely because softcapping is not expressible in fused SDPA/flash kernels), attn_implementation='sdpa' (the transformers default) and no attention_mask — the standard model(input_ids) shape in eval, perplexity and prefill code, and reachable from DPTrainer whenever the batch carries no attention_mask. Every sliding-attention layer attends to the entire causal prefix instead of the window, so the model trained or evaluated is not the architecture it claims to implement. Accounting is untouched.
evidence: End-to-end, transformers 5.15.1 / torch 2.13, tiny Gemma2 (hidden 64, 2 layers, default alternating layer_types=['sliding_attention','full_attention'], sliding_window=4, seq=12, attn_implementation='sdpa', attention_mask=None, attn_logit_softcapping=None), logits sum computed in separate processes on identical seeded weights: upstream reference 10.66509758651955, opaque-patched 19.25782148790313, upstream with the window disabled (sliding_window=64) 19.25782148790313 — the patched model reproduces the no-window reference to the last digit.
Same config with attn_logit_softcapping at its 50.0 default: reference 10.664953630010132 vs patched 10.664955383865163 (1.7e-6, fp32 noise) — the defect is confined to the softcap=None fallthrough.

Scoping: with an all-ones attention_mask the same softcap=None config matches exactly (12.104748404293787 both), and with attn_implementation='eager' it matches exactly (12.104748966979969 both) — the trigger profile is identical to OPQ-337's.

Unit level: vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2(module, q, k, v, None, scaling=1.0, softcap=None, sliding_window=3) on (1,2,8,4) tensors differs from a dense windowed reference by 1.1628184318542480 and from a dense NO-window reference by 1.1920928955078125e-07; the same call with softcap=1e9 matches the windowed reference to 1.19e-07.

Predicate-divergence path (b), tiny Mistral (sliding_window=4, seq=12, sdpa, attention_mask=None, attention_dropout=0.1, model.train() inside torch.no_grad(), apply_model_patches(..., dropout=False)): upstream 7.156000263028545, patched 4.206265495965454, upstream with sliding_window=64 4.206265495965454.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:683 `if softcap is not None:` and :729 `return vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(` — the fallthrough drops sliding_window; vmap_sdpa_attention_forward (attention.py:169-241) never reads it.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/runtime/masking.py:102-107 `and (not torch.is_grad_enabled() or getattr(config, "attention_dropout", None) == 0.0) and _query_length(input_embeds) > sliding_window` vs packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:297 `and dropout == 0.0`.

git show d80d3f99 -- .../models/gemma2.py adds `masking_module_patcher=apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch` (models/gemma2.py:35); before that commit gemma2 used the generic builder, which materialized the window.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the elision and the application one predicate instead of two. Either (i) have vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask receive the family's attention-side precondition (pass the concrete forward, or a capability probe, and require exactly the same conditions: runtime dropout, softcap disposition, position_bias), or (ii) make the family SDPA forwards total for sliding windows — give vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 a non-softcap branch that routes through _compact_sliding_window_sdpa when sliding_window is not None, and have vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window fall back to building the band mask itself (via _sdpa_sliding_window_mask) rather than to the window-blind vmap_sdpa_attention_forward. Add a debug assertion (or a fail-closed raise) when a compact-elided mask reaches a forward that will not apply the window. Extend test_parity.py::test_sliding_window_parity to gemma2 with attn_logit_softcapping parametrized over {50.0, None}, and add a component test for vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2 with softcap=None (the existing one, tests/transformers/components/test_attention.py:316-346, only covers softcap=1.0).

findings.title: Parity suite still compares patched against patched for 21 of 26 families — sibling test modules re-contaminate what #812 restores
findings.line: 33 (and test_cohere.py:33, test_cohere2.py:36, test_exaone4.py:36, test_gemma.py:33, test_gemma2.py:33, test_gemma3.py:43, test_glm4.py:33, test_gpt2.py:40, test_granite.py:36, test_mellum.py:74, test_ministral.py:36, test_mistral.py:36, test_olmo2.py:33, test_olmo3.py:33, test_attention_impls.py:38,95)

findings.title: Gemma3 bidirectional attention: or_mask_function / and_mask_function are accepted and silently ignored by opaque's mask builders
findings.line: 159-315 (vmap_create_causal_mask: or_mask_function/and_mask_function parameters at :165-166 are never read) and 318-447 (vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask forwards them to a function that ignores them)
findings.claim: The same defect pattern as OPQ-337 — opaque's mask builder silently discards a constraint upstream applies — survives in a sibling path the #811 fix did not touch. vmap_create_causal_mask declares or_mask_function and and_mask_function in its signature and never uses them; vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask passes them down to that function (masking.py:389-390) and its own compact/generic SDPA short-circuit at masking.py:361-372 does not even check whether they are set before returning a plain band mask. transformers 5.15.1's Gemma3TextModel uses or_mask_function to implement bidirectional attention (modeling_gemma3.py:547-549) and blockwise/sliding overlays for packed inputs (modeling_gemma3.py:748-752), and gemma3 is a registered opaque family. block_sequence_ids is dropped the same way (it is absorbed by **kwargs).
findings.failure_scenario: Fine-tuning or evaluating a Gemma3 text model with use_bidirectional_attention=True (the EmbeddingGemma configuration) under DPTrainer: opaque's patched model silently runs plain causal (and causal-windowed) attention while upstream runs bidirectional, so the optimized objective is not the advertised architecture. No warning is emitted and no parity test sets the flag.
evidence: Reproduced on transformers 5.15.1 / torch 2.13 with a tiny Gemma3ForCausalLM (Gemma3TextConfig, hidden 64, 2 layers, layer_types=['sliding_attention','full_attention'], sliding_window=4, seq=12, eager, all-ones mask), logits sum on identical seeded weights: use_bidirectional_attention=True -> upstream 24.917816297362833, opaque-patched 13.034685771737713; use_bidirectional_attention=False -> 18.334294046406285 for both.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/runtime/masking.py:165-166 declares `or_mask_function=None, and_mask_function=None` and no line in the body of vmap_create_causal_mask (masking.py:186-315) references either name.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/runtime/masking.py:361-372: the SDPA short-circuit returns `_sdpa_sliding_window_mask(...)` / `None` without consulting or_mask_function, and_mask_function or block_sequence_ids (contrast _can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window at masking.py:99-101, which does check all three).

.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/transformers/models/gemma3/modeling_gemma3.py:547-549 sets mask_kwargs['or_mask_function'] and sliding_mask_kwargs['or_mask_function'] when config.use_bidirectional_attention, and :748-752 passes or_mask_function=blockwise_overlay(...) + and_mask_function=sliding_window_overlay(...).
findings.fix_sketch: Implement the two hooks in vmap_create_causal_mask the way transformers' masking_utils composes them (vectorized mask_function -> OR with or_mask_function -> AND with and_mask_function) using vmap-safe tensor ops, and make every short-circuit in vmap_create_sliding_window_causal_mask / vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask refuse to elide when either hook or block_sequence_ids is present. Add a gemma3 parity case with use_bidirectional_attention=True.

findings.title: Fail-closed guard for unregistered HF families does not see PEFT-wrapped models
findings.claim: The #814 fix decides whether to fail closed with `isinstance(model, transformers.PreTrainedModel)`. peft.PeftModel inherits torch.nn.Module + PushToHubMixin, not PreTrainedModel, so a LoRA-wrapped model of an unregistered HF family takes the warn-and-return branch at _router.py:144-149. detect_family still resolves the family correctly through PeftModel's attribute forwarding, so the router knows it is looking at an HF architecture it cannot patch and proceeds anyway. Two vmap-safety patches are lost, not one: disable_dropout (_router.py:165-168) and the PeftModel batchify patch (_router.py:171-183) are both below the early return. DP-LoRA on a Hugging Face causal LM is the primary documented Opaque workflow, so the escape hatch is wider than the one the fix intended for custom non-HF nn.Modules.
findings.failure_scenario: A user DP-fine-tunes a LoRA adapter on an unregistered HF family (e.g. falcon) through DPTrainer. No error, only a warning. Dropout survives, and under vmap(grad) with randomness='same' (_clipped_fun.py) every example in the batch shares one dropout mask, so per-example gradients differ from both ordinary training and the dropout-free configuration the trainer documents; the PeftModel batchify shim that makes the wrapper vmap-safe is also never applied. Privacy is unaffected — clipping still bounds sensitivity.
evidence: Reproduced on transformers 5.15.1 / peft 0.20.0: `supported_families()` does not contain 'falcon'. Bare FalconForCausalLM -> ConfigurationError 'opaque: compatibility/dropout/batchify patches require a registered transformers family; got 'falcon' (FalconForCausalLM)'. peft.get_peft_model(FalconForCausalLM(cfg), LoraConfig(...)) -> isinstance(pm, peft.PeftModel)=True, isinstance(pm, transformers.PreTrainedModel)=False, detect_family(pm)='falcon', apply_model_patches(pm) raises nothing and logs only WARNING 'opaque: no registered apply function for model family falcon; no model-level patches applied.'
After that call the model still has ('base_model.model.transformer.h.0.self_attention.attention_dropout', 0.3) and config.attention_dropout=0.3 / hidden_dropout=0.3.
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/_router.py:149 `return` precedes both the dropout block (:165-168) and the PeftModel batchify block (:171-183).
packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/test_public_factory.py:548-563 only covers a bare PreTrainedModel subclass; no test wraps an unregistered family in PEFT.
findings.fix_sketch: Make _is_hf_pretrained_model unwrap PEFT: treat the model as an HF model when it is a PreTrainedModel, or when peft is importable and isinstance(model, peft.PeftModel) and the unwrapped base (get_base_model() / model.base_model.model) is a PreTrainedModel. Equivalently, key the decision off detect_family(model) returning a non-None model_type that is absent from the registry, which already works through the PEFT wrapper. Add a test that get_peft_model over an unregistered PreTrainedModel raises ConfigurationError.

findings.title: The #895 dataset guard covers the scoring half only: train_subset()/train_indices() still accept a dataset the partition was not built from
findings.claim: e6e3d478 (#895, closing #830/OPQ-352) records dataset_size on CoinFlip (:168) and asserts it in _scoring_loader (attacks/_helpers.py:159-178), but the two methods that turn the partition into the training set are left unguarded. train_indices(dataset_size: int | None = None) resolves 'size = self.dataset_size if dataset_size is None else dataset_size' (:189) - an explicit argument silently overrides the recorded value with no consistency check - and train_subset() always supplies one: 'return Subset(dataset, self.train_indices(len(dataset)))' (:209), so the recorded size is never consulted on that path at all. train_subset() is the tutorial's training path (docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb:153, :505) and train_indices(len(dataset)) is the user guide's (docs/user-guide/auditing.md:38, :151, :268). The wrong-dataset-object hazard OPQ-352 describes is therefore closed for scoring and open for training, in the same class whose two dataset objects (base vs concatenated 'audited') the finding named.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced on the shipped code. The target model is then trained with no canary either in or out; the subsequent scoring pass runs against `audited`, passes the new length check, and the audit reports no detectable leakage for a mechanism it should flag - the same silent under-detection #829 was closed to prevent. The milder variant is equally silent: cf built on a 20-row dataset with out_indices=[2], cf.train_subset(a different 30-row dataset) returns 29 rows and excludes row 2 of the wrong dataset.

findings.title: #895 compares dataset length only, so an equal-length reordering is still scored silently

findings.title: The grid-floor justification comment cites a measurement that does not reproduce, and the test validates the floor only at n=1
findings.claim: The comment 3ccf15ba (#890) put above _MIN_GRID_SIZE says 'at grid_size=16 a fully separable 500/500 canary split audits as eps=0'. A fully separable 500/500 split is u=0, and on the shipped code GdpMethod(grid_size=16).epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) returns 32.80 for it (37.28 at grid 64) - not 0. The configuration that does collapse, and the one the commit's own regression test builds (test_gdp.py:293-297, 'best threshold makes exactly 250 errors'), is u=250, i.e. 75 % attack accuracy, not full separation. The same comment says the floor 'is validated against the v_k order-statistic identity (Xiang et al. 2025, Eq. 12)', but the test that landed with it (test_gdp.py:148-158) checks only the n=1 case v_1 = Phi(-mu/2); the n=1 identity constrains nothing about the high ranks of a 10^3-10^4-canary audit, which are what dominate the Chernoff sum the floor exists to resolve. The floor itself is adequate - I swept m=1000..100000 and grid 1_000 tracks grid 10_000 within 0.035 absolute and agrees on the eps=0 boundary - so this is the recorded justification being wrong, not the constant.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer revisiting the floor - when the ~1.2 s/query cost is questioned, or while working open #828, whose RuntimeError the floor makes slower to reach - reads the comment, checks the cited case (fully separable, grid 16), measures eps=32.8 instead of the claimed 0, concludes the floor rests on a mismeasurement and lowers it back toward 16. That reinstates the real collapse at u=250-350 (eps 0.0 instead of 5.11/2.30) which #829 closed. The n=1 'validation' offers no counter-argument, since it holds at grid 16 as well.

measured on the shipped GdpMethod: u=0 grid 16 -> eps 32.801667; u=0 grid 64 -> 37.275869; u=250 grid 16 -> 0.0; u=250 grid 64 -> 2.700027 (n_in=n_out=500, delta=1e-5)

packages/opaque-auditing/tests/auditing/test_gdp.py:290-297 - the regression test's own docstring describes the u=250 configuration, not a separable one
findings.fix_sketch: Restate the comment with the configuration the regression test actually uses (500/500 with 250 errors at the best threshold: eps 0.0 at grid 16, 2.70 at 64, 5.08 at 1_000, 5.11 at 10_000) and cite the grid sweep across audit sizes rather than the n=1 identity; if the n=1 test is kept, add a high-rank case (e.g. compare _compute_v_k at grid 1_000 vs 10_000 for n=10_000, top ranks) so the floor has a test that could actually fail.

findings.title: Dependency-confusion defensive registration on PyPI covers only 4 of the 10 published distribution names; the other 6 are free for anyone to claim
findings.line: 34-45 (package table) and 66-81 (install commands); names defined in pyproject.toml:83-94 workspace.members
findings.claim: Opaque publishes to a private-namespace index (packages.jetbrains.team) rather than PyPI, which is the classic dependency-confusion setup. The team recognised this and on 2026-08-12 published JetBrains security-tooling defensive stubs on PyPI at version 999.9.9 whose description reads verbatim "This public copy of the package is a stub published on pypi.org designed to mitigate risks from Dependency Confusion" - but only for opaque-accounting, opaque-auditing, opaque-dpftrl and opaque-optimizers. Querying pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json for every distribution the repo builds shows opaque-base, opaque-engine, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-patches, opaque-transformers and opaque-alignment all return 404, i.e. unregistered and claimable by any third party today. The umbrella name is worse: `opaque` on PyPI is already an unrelated third-party project (opaque 1.0.0, "python libopaque wrapper", author Stefan Marsiske), so it cannot be defensively held at all. The repository's public README table and import-layout block (README.md:34-45, 48-61) publish the exact unregistered names.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker registers `opaque-engine` and `opaque-base` on PyPI (both currently 404) with malicious sdists. Any of these then executes attacker code: (a) a user who reads README.md's package table and types `pip install opaque-engine` without the JetBrains index - the documented per-package install surface in AGENTS.md's installation matrix uses exactly these bare names; (b) any environment that adds PyPI as an extra index (`pip install --extra-index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/... opaque`) - pip merges candidates across indexes and picks the highest version, so a 999.9.9-style attacker release wins; (c) any uv configuration with index-strategy = "unsafe-best-match". Because opaque-base and opaque-engine are transitive dependencies of every other wheel, a single captured name reaches every Opaque install in that environment, inside a DP training pipeline that handles sensitive data.

pypi.org/pypi/{opaque-base,opaque-engine,opaque-dpsgd,opaque-patches,opaque-transformers,opaque-alignment}/json -> HTTP 404 for all six
pypi.org/pypi/opaque/json -> {'name': 'opaque', 'version': '1.0.0', 'summary': 'python libopaque wrapper', 'author': 'Stefan Marsiske'} - an unrelated third-party project
pyproject.toml:83-94 workspace.members lists all ten package directories; README.md:34-45 publishes the ten distribution names in a table
.github/workflows/ci.yml:236-241 and release.yml:124-133 publish these names to https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/legacy/, never to PyPI
findings.fix_sketch: Ask JetBrains security-tooling (security-tooling@jetbrains.com, the address in the existing stubs) to publish the same 999.9.9 defensive stub for opaque-base, opaque-engine, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-patches, opaque-transformers and opaque-alignment, and to re-run that registration whenever a new opaque-* distribution is added (add it as a checklist item next to the workspace.members list). For the umbrella name, which is taken, state explicitly in README.md and docs/getting-started/installation.md that `opaque` on PyPI is a different project and that the index flag is mandatory, and never document a bare `pip install opaque*` without --index-url.

findings.title: Internal JetBrains infrastructure identifiers are committed in the public repository: an access-controlled TeamCity server hostname and an internal GCP Artifact Registry project
findings.claim: Marble #578 ("Remove JetBrains-internal specifics from documentation") is closed, but two internal infrastructure identifiers remain in tracked configuration at origin/main, which is public. `.teamcity/pom.xml:18` hardcodes `<teamcity.server.url>https://jbr-fed.teamcity.com</teamcity.server.url>`; that host is access-controlled (anonymous GET returns HTTP 401), so this discloses the name of a non-public CI server plus, via `.teamcity/README.md` and `.teamcity/settings.kts`, its intended project layout, agent pool (`Linux-Large`, `teamcity.agent.jbHosted`) and pipeline id (`Opaque_LinuxAmd64Tests`). `.github/workflows/build-devcontainer.yaml:77` hardcodes `GAR_IMAGE: europe-west4-docker.pkg.dev/gke-dev-dws-jbr/ml/opaque-devcontainer`, disclosing an internal Google Cloud project id (`gke-dev-dws-jbr`) and repository (`ml`) that the GitHub Actions OIDC workload identity pushes images into. Neither is a secret in the credential sense, but both are precisely the kind of internal specific #578 and #553 claimed to have removed, and neither serves any public reader.
findings.failure_scenario: A public reader of the repository learns the hostname of an internal JetBrains TeamCity instance and the project/repository coordinates of an internal GCP Artifact Registry. That is reconnaissance input for credential-stuffing or phishing against the TeamCity instance and for probing/targeting the GAR path, and it widens the blast radius of any future leak of GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER / GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL because the attacker already knows where to push. The `.teamcity` prototype is additionally dead weight: nothing in .github/workflows references TeamCity, AGENTS.md documents GitHub Actions as the CI, and .teamcity/README.md forward-references a migration ("replaces the GitHub Actions Linux amd64 test matrix") that has not happened - itself a violation of AGENTS.md's "forward-references to features that don't yet exist don't belong anywhere".

findings.fix_sketch: Replace the literal TeamCity server URL in .teamcity/pom.xml with a Maven property supplied at generate time (`-Dteamcity.server.url=...`) or delete the `.teamcity` prototype entirely until the migration is real, and drop its forward-referencing README. In .github/workflows/build-devcontainer.yaml move the GAR image path to a repository variable (`${{ vars.GAR_IMAGE }}`) alongside the two GCP vars it already uses by name, so no internal project id is committed. Re-run a grep for internal host/project identifiers over ALL tracked files, not only docs prose, before declaring #578 complete.

findings.title: Public install documentation's "Extras" commands omit the registry index and resolve to an unrelated PyPI project named `opaque`
findings.claim: README.md:67-72 and docs/getting-started/installation.md:19-27 correctly teach `pip install opaque --index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/`. The Extras blocks immediately below them then drop the flag entirely: README.md:78-81 and installation.md:33-36 show four bare commands (`pip install "opaque[auditing]"`, `"opaque[dpftrl]"`, `"opaque[transformers]"`, `"opaque[all]"`). `--index-url` does not persist across shell invocations, so a reader who copies these lines resolves `opaque` from PyPI, where `opaque` is a different project - version 1.0.0, "python libopaque wrapper" by Stefan Marsiske, which has none of these extras.
findings.failure_scenario: A new user follows the README top to bottom: the first command installs the real Opaque from the JetBrains index; the next line, `pip install "opaque[all]"`, silently downloads the unrelated libopaque wrapper from PyPI, warns only `WARNING: opaque 1.0.0 does not provide the extra 'all'`, and overwrites the installed `opaque` distribution. The user's `import opaque.dpsgd` then fails, or - worse in a CI image built from the docs - the wrong `opaque` ends up in the environment used to reason about differential privacy. The same hazard applies to `uv add` since the second block never re-specifies `--index`.
evidence: README.md:78-81 — `pip install "opaque[auditing]"` / `"opaque[dpftrl]"` / `"opaque[transformers]"` / `"opaque[all]"`, no index flag
docs/getting-started/installation.md:33-36 — identical four commands, no index flag, directly under the `--index-url` block at :19-27
pypi.org/pypi/opaque/json -> {'version': '1.0.0', 'summary': 'python libopaque wrapper', 'author': 'Stefan Marsiske'}
https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/opaque/ lists opaque-0.15.0-py3-none-any.whl etc. — the real project is only on that index
findings.fix_sketch: Repeat `--index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` on every install command in README.md and docs/getting-started/installation.md, or restructure the pages to configure the index once persistently (a `pip config set global.index-url ...` / `[[tool.uv.index]]` snippet) and say so explicitly. Add a one-line warning that the `opaque` name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project. Under ARC-011 these blocks are the tagged executable installation scenarios, so the post-build validator should run them verbatim in a clean environment - which would have caught this.

findings.title: The committed uv.lock still resolves accelerate 1.14.0, which carries an open GitHub-reviewed advisory with a released fix
findings.claim: Marble #574 ("remediate dependency security alerts before public visibility") is closed, but the lockfile at origin/main pins a version with a live advisory. Querying every one of the 218 PyPI packages in uv.lock against OSV.dev returns exactly one hit: accelerate 1.14.0, affected by GHSA-4j2p-28q2-5m79 / CVE-2026-69112 / PYSEC-2026-3804 - path traversal and denial of service via unsanitised `weight_map` entries in sharded-checkpoint indexes consumed by `load_checkpoint_in_model` and `load_checkpoint_and_dispatch` (CWE-22, CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H, MODERATE, github_reviewed 2026-09-08). The advisory's range is `last_affected: 1.14.0` and accelerate 1.15.0 is already published on PyPI, so a fix exists and was simply not taken. accelerate reaches the lock transitively through peft 0.20.0 and trl 1.12.0, i.e. through opaque-transformers / opaque-alignment / opaque-patches[transformers].
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone reproducing the project with the documented `uv sync --group dev --all-packages --extra all` - every contributor and every CI lane - gets accelerate 1.14.0. A DP fine-tuning run that loads a sharded checkpoint from an untrusted or partially-trusted source (an arbitrary Hugging Face Hub repo, which is exactly what examples/train_*.py do) can be made to read arbitrary files off the runner via `../` entries in the shard index, or to hang forever on a named pipe. On the self-hosted persistent GPU runner (`GPU-runner-001`) an arbitrary-file-read primitive is materially worse than on an ephemeral one.

uv.lock:2862 and :4146 — accelerate is required by peft 0.20.0 and trl 1.12.0

OSV querybatch over all 218 locked PyPI packages: 1 hit, accelerate 1.14.0 -> ['GHSA-4j2p-28q2-5m79', 'PYSEC-2026-3804']; OSV vulns/GHSA-4j2p-28q2-5m79 -> aliases ['CVE-2026-69112','PYSEC-2026-3804'], ranges [{introduced 0, last_affected 1.14.0}], database_specific severity MODERATE, github_reviewed_at 2026-09-08
pypi.org/pypi/accelerate/json -> info.version 1.15.0 (fix available)
OSV querybatch over all 61 crates in Cargo.lock: zero hits
.github/dependabot.yml:47-66 — the uv ecosystem entry exists with versioning-strategy lockfile-only and groups all patterns into one PR
findings.fix_sketch: Bump accelerate to >= 1.15.0 in uv.lock (`uv lock --upgrade-package accelerate`). Longer term, the `workspace-dependencies` group in .github/dependabot.yml batches every uv update into a single grouped PR, which makes a security bump wait on an unrelated failing update; give security updates their own ungrouped lane, and add a recurring OSV/`pip-audit` check over uv.lock and Cargo.lock to CI so #574 stays remediated instead of being a one-time sweep.

findings.title: third_party_provenance.toml misattributes riskcal to a nonexistent google-research repository, and one upstream's homepage is prose rather than a URL
findings.claim: ARC-009 requires that "repository provenance references resolve to real attributed sources". Two entries fail. (1) The riskcal upstream declares `homepage = "https://github.com/google-research/riskcal"`; no such repository exists - a GitHub search for `riskcal in:name` returns the real project at `interpretable-dp/riskcal` ("Measure and calibrate operational privacy risks for differentially private algorithms"), and PyPI's riskcal metadata gives project_urls.Repository = https://github.com/interpretable-dp/riskcal.git with authors Bogdan Kulynych and Juan Felipe Gomez. The manifest therefore credits Google Research for work by other authors. (2) The "Random-allocation reference implementation" entry puts a sentence in the `homepage` field - `homepage = 'ICML 2026 reference implementation for "Efficient privacy loss accounting for subsampling and random allocation"'` - which is not a resolvable reference at all, for code the manifest marks `disposition = "adapted"`, `requires_notice = true` and whose derived files ship in opaque-dpsgd.
findings.failure_scenario: A downstream consumer performing an OSS license/attribution review of the published opaque-dpsgd and opaque-accounting wheels follows third_party_provenance.toml - the document ARC-009 designates as the machine-readable provenance source of truth that will generate or validate NOTICE - and cannot locate the riskcal upstream (404) to confirm its MIT terms, and cannot locate the random-allocation upstream at all to confirm its Apache-2.0 terms or satisfy the notice obligation the manifest itself asserts. On a public repository this is a live misstatement of the project's attribution posture, and it will propagate straight into NOTICE the moment the planned generator is built on top of this file.

Give the random-allocation entry a resolvable `homepage` (the arXiv/proceedings URL or the reference implementation's repository) and, if only a paper exists, add a separate `citation` field rather than overloading `homepage`. Add a tiny validator to CI that parses third_party_provenance.toml and asserts every `files` path exists and every `homepage` is an absolute http(s) URL - the same script used here found both defects in one pass, and it is behavioural rather than an inventory check so it does not conflict with #586's intent.

findings.title: The repository's squash setting discards every PR body, contradicting AGENTS.md and the PR template and disabling git-cliff's BREAKING CHANGE detection
findings.line: 97-118 (Pull requests section); config verified via the repository API
findings.claim: AGENTS.md states "The PR title becomes the commit subject; the PR body becomes the commit body (repo-level squash setting = `PR_TITLE` + `PR_BODY`). Both feed `git-cliff`", and .github/pull_request_template.md:7-9 repeats "On squash merge the body becomes the commit body that git-cliff reads." The repository is actually configured with `squash_merge_commit_title: "PR_TITLE"` but `squash_merge_commit_message: "BLANK"`. Every one of the 124 delta commits confirms it: their bodies are empty apart from GitHub-generated `Co-authored-by:` trailers. This is not only stale documentation - cliff.toml:36 contains `{ body = ".*BREAKING CHANGE", group = "Breaking" }` and sets `protect_breaking_commits = true`, both of which read the commit BODY, and AGENTS.md:110-111 explicitly tells contributors that a breaking change may be declared with "a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in the body".
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor follows AGENTS.md and declares a breaking change with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in the PR body instead of a `!` in the title (both are documented as equivalent). The squash merge drops the footer, so the commit body is empty; git-cliff's body parser never fires, the commit is categorised by its type prefix (e.g. `refactor` -> "Changed") instead of "Breaking", and the drafted GitHub Release for that version ships with no Breaking section. Downstream users upgrading on those notes hit an undeclared breaking change. Separately, every release's "What's changed" and permanent `git log` lose the 2-4 sentences of rationale the PR template asks for - exactly the 'why' AGENTS.md says to preserve for "a future spelunker".
evidence: GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque -> {"squash_merge_commit_title": "PR_TITLE", "squash_merge_commit_message": "BLANK", "allow_merge_commit": false, "allow_rebase_merge": false}
AGENTS.md 'Pull requests': 'The PR title becomes the commit subject; the PR body becomes the commit body (repo-level squash setting = `PR_TITLE` + `PR_BODY`)'
.github/pull_request_template.md:7-9 'On squash merge the body becomes the commit body that git-cliff reads.'

findings.title: The required status check "Qodana / Qodana" can never report on a fork pull request, so the documented external-contribution path cannot merge
findings.claim: The active main ruleset requires seven status checks, one of which is the context "Qodana / Qodana" produced by pr.yml's `qodana` job calling the reusable qodana.yml `scan` job (both named "Qodana"). That caller job is guarded by `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, so for a pull request opened from a fork the job is skipped, the reusable workflow is never instantiated, and the "Qodana / Qodana" check context is never created - a required check that never reports blocks merge. The authors clearly understood this hazard elsewhere: pr.yml:184-217 and :221-235 add matrix-independent gate jobs named "Python tests" and "Rust tests" with `if: always()` whose jq explicitly treats skipped `python-tests-cuda*` legs as success, with the comment "Keep a stable, matrix-independent check name for branch protection rules". No equivalent gate exists for Qodana. Meanwhile docs/development/index.md:3,10-11 documents the fork workflow and README.md:186 points contributors at it.
findings.failure_scenario: An external contributor forks the repository as docs/development/index.md instructs, opens a PR, and every check goes green except "Qodana / Qodana", which sits permanently as 'Expected - waiting for status to be reported'. The PR cannot be merged by anyone other than a repository admin using the ruleset's bypass. For a project that went public specifically to accept outside contributions (Marble #553/#557), the advertised contribution path is unmergeable by design. The same guard also means the fork PR receives no static-analysis coverage at all, which is the case where untrusted code most needs it.
evidence: GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/rulesets/12831618 -> required_status_checks includes {"context": "Qodana / Qodana"}; the pull_request rule requires 1 approving review; bypass_actors = [{actor_type: RepositoryRole, actor_id: 5, bypass_mode: always}]
.github/workflows/pr.yml:252-257 — qodana job `if: (success() || failure()) && !github.event.pull_request.draft && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, `name: Qodana`
.github/workflows/qodana.yml:29-31 — jobs.scan has `name: Qodana`, so the composed check context is 'Qodana / Qodana'

.github/workflows/pr.yml:182-186 — comment 'Keep a stable, matrix-independent check name for branch protection rules' above the `python-tests` gate job, and pr.yml:195-217 jq that tolerates skipped CUDA legs — the pattern deliberately applied to Python/Rust but not Qodana
docs/development/index.md:3,10-11 'This guide is for contributors working from a GitHub fork ... Fork JetBrains-Research/opaque, then clone your fork'; README.md:186 links it
Repository is public with allow_forking: true (GitHub API)
findings.fix_sketch: Add a stable gate job to pr.yml in the same shape as `python-tests` / `rust-test-gate` - e.g. a job named "Qodana" with `if: always()` and `needs: [qodana]` that passes when the upstream result is `success` or `skipped` - and make the ruleset require that gate's context instead of the nested "Qodana / Qodana". Alternatively, run Qodana for forks without QODANA_TOKEN in a non-cloud mode, or drop it from the required set and keep it informational as ci.yml already does (ci.yml:132-135 marks the main-branch Qodana job continue-on-error: true). Whichever is chosen, confirm on a real fork PR that all seven required contexts report.

findings.title: Contributor documentation routes public users to GitHub Discussions (disabled) and to label URLs that do not match the repository's actual label names
findings.claim: Marble #566 was closed as `not_planned` and Discussions was never enabled (`has_discussions: false`), but the documentation that #566 was supposed to update was never reverted. CONTRIBUTING.md:87 offers "[Open Discussions](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/discussions)" as a starting point and CONTRIBUTING.md:445 makes it the single answer for "**Questions**" - neither can resolve to a discussions page while the feature is off. In the same block, CONTRIBUTING.md:85-86 links `/labels/good-first-issue` and `/labels/help-wanted`, but the repository's 45 labels include "good first issue" and "help wanted" (with spaces) and neither hyphenated slug exists, so both links land on an empty/invalid label filter. Compounding it, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` does not exist, so the new-issue chooser presents no contact links and offers no alternative route.
findings.failure_scenario: A first-time contributor arriving from the public README opens CONTRIBUTING.md to find something to work on: both 'good first issue' links show nothing, and the 'Questions' route 404s. With no config.yml contact links and Discussions off, the only remaining channel is a public issue - which is also where SECURITY.md tells people NOT to put a suspected vulnerability, so a confused reporter has no visible correct destination short of reading SECURITY.md in full.
evidence: GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque -> "has_discussions": false; issue #566 state_reason "not_planned"
CONTRIBUTING.md:87 '- [Open Discussions](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/discussions)'
CONTRIBUTING.md:445 '- **Questions**: Open a [Discussion](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/discussions)'

CONTRIBUTING.md:85-86 link /labels/good-first-issue and /labels/help-wanted; GET /repos/.../labels?per_page=100 returns 45 labels containing 'good first issue' and 'help wanted', and neither 'good-first-issue' nor 'help-wanted'
ls .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ -> bug_report.yml, documentation.yml, feature_request.yml only; no config.yml
findings.fix_sketch: Either enable Discussions (reopening the #566 decision) or remove both Discussions links from CONTRIBUTING.md and point 'Questions' at the issue tracker with a `question` label. URL-encode the real label names in the two 'good starting points' links (`/labels/good%20first%20issue`, `/labels/help%20wanted`). Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml with `blank_issues_enabled` set deliberately and contact_links covering security reporting and questions, so the new-issue chooser routes people correctly.

findings.title: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is disabled on the public repository and SECURITY.md states no concrete disclosure window
findings.claim: SECURITY.md tells reporters to use a private channel and explicitly forbids public issues or discussions for suspected vulnerabilities, but the GitHub-native private path is off: GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/private-vulnerability-reporting returns {"enabled": false}, so the repository's Security tab shows no 'Report a vulnerability' button and an outside researcher's only private route is the security@jetbrains.com mailto at SECURITY.md:12. The policy also never states a disclosure window; SECURITY.md:41-42 only asks reporters to 'allow reasonable time for a fix or mitigation before public disclosure' and delegates the timeline to the JetBrains Coordinated Disclosure Policy (SECURITY.md:38-40), which is a real, reachable document but is not the project-specific window Marble #554 framed.
findings.failure_scenario: A researcher who finds a privacy-accounting defect with material impact clicks the repository's Security tab, sees no reporting form (the standard 2026 workflow), and either discloses publicly in an issue - which SECURITY.md:14 forbids and which for a DP library means publishing an under-noising defect before a fix - or abandons the report. Because no window is stated, a reporter who does email has no basis for deciding when publication is fair, and neither side has a shared expectation.
evidence: GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/private-vulnerability-reporting -> HTTP 200, {"enabled": false}
GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque -> "private": false, "visibility": "public"
SECURITY.md:10-14 'Report suspected vulnerabilities privately to security@jetbrains.com ... Do not open a public issue or discussion for a suspected vulnerability.'
SECURITY.md:41-42 'Please allow reasonable time for a fix or mitigation before public disclosure.' — no number of days anywhere in the file
https://www.jetbrains.com/legal/docs/terms/coordinated-disclosure/ -> HTTP 200 (the delegated policy is real and reachable)
findings.fix_sketch: Enable private vulnerability reporting in repository Settings -> Security (one toggle; it also unlocks draft GitHub Security Advisories for the published opaque-* distributions) and mention that route first in SECURITY.md alongside the email. Add a concrete acknowledgement and disclosure expectation - e.g. acknowledge within N business days, coordinate publication within 90 days or on fix release, whichever is first - or state explicitly that the JetBrains Coordinated Disclosure Policy's timeline governs and link the specific clause.

findings.title: Removing the contract tests (#586) left the documented torch-free opaque-accounting guarantee with no automated enforcement, in the repository or post-build
findings.claim: 864a6442 (#587, closing Marble #586) deleted tests/contracts/test_accounting_torch_free.py and tests/contracts/test_accounting_factory_leakage.py along with the fragile enumeration checks. The torch-free test was not a structural proxy - it enforced a guarantee the project advertises as a supported installation option (README.md:44 'torch-free standalone'; docs/getting-started/installation.md; packages/opaque-base/pyproject.toml:26-30 'Adding any third-party dependency here would propagate into opaque-accounting ... and break the "torch-free accounting" guarantee'; AGENTS.md installation matrix 'pip install opaque-accounting  # PLD accounting (torch-free standalone)'). Nothing replaced it: a repo-wide grep finds no remaining test asserting the property, and .github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml runs exactly one scenario - install `opaque[all]` and compose a DP-SGD and a DP-FTRL process - never an opaque-accounting-only install in a torch-free environment. The ARC-004/ARC-005/ARC-011 post-build validation meant to take over is still marked 'Planned' in .junie/architecture-contracts.md.
findings.failure_scenario: A future change adds `import torch` (or a torch-importing helper) to packages/opaque-accounting/src or to its tests. Every CI lane passes, because the test runner's environment always has torch installed via the other workspace packages. The published opaque-accounting wheel then declares only opaque-base as a dependency but fails to import in the torch-free environment the README, AGENTS.md and installation docs promise - discovered only by an end user. I verified the property currently still holds (no torch import anywhere under packages/opaque-accounting/{src,tests}; its only dependency is opaque-base>=0.0.0.dev0), so this is an unguarded invariant, not a live break.
evidence: git show 864a6442 --stat — deletes tests/contracts/test_accounting_torch_free.py (55 lines) and tests/contracts/test_accounting_factory_leakage.py (89 lines), plus 8 other enumeration/import tests
git show 864a6442^:tests/contracts/test_accounting_torch_free.py — AST-scanned packages/opaque-accounting/{src,tests} for `import torch` / `from torch...`
.github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml:50-88 — the single 'Run cross-stack scenario' step installs "${opaque_wheels[0]}[all]" and imports opaque.dpftrl/opaque.dpsgd; no torch-free install path
grep -rn 'torch_free|torch-free' over the tree returns only prose/comments (packages/opaque-base/pyproject.toml:26,30; two module docstrings) and one unrelated auditing test comment — no enforcement
.junie/architecture-contracts.md contract table — ARC-004 Backend-neutral distributions: Planned; ARC-005: Planned; ARC-011 Supported installation options: Planned

Current property verified holding: no `import torch` / `from torch` under packages/opaque-accounting/{src,tests}; packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml:13-15 dependencies = ["opaque-base>=0.0.0.dev0"]
findings.fix_sketch: Add one backend-neutral scenario to .github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml: create a venv, install only the built opaque_accounting and opaque_base wheels with --no-deps plus their real deps, assert `torch` is not importable in that venv, and run a minimal accounting operation (e.g. gaussian(1.0) composed and epsilon_at(1e-5)). That is behavioural post-build validation - what ARC-004/ARC-011 describe - so it restores the guard without reintroducing the source-scanning check #586 removed.
