findings.title: Gemma2 silently loses its sliding window under SDPA when attn_logit_softcapping is None
findings.claim: Delta commit d80d3f99 (#954) added `masking_module_patcher=apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch` to the gemma2 family (models/gemma2.py:35). That patcher deliberately returns `None` instead of a dense mask when the compact conditions hold (runtime/masking.py:79-107 `_can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window`: sdpa, no padding mask, no cache, dropout-free-or-no-grad, seq_len > sliding_window), delegating the look-back limit to the family's SDPA replacement. For mistral/ministral that replacement is `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window`, which honours it via `_compact_sliding_window_sdpa`. For gemma2 it is `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2`, whose `softcap is None` branch falls through at attention.py:729-738 to plain `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(...)` WITHOUT passing `sliding_window`; that function accepts `**kwargs` and never applies a window (attention.py:174-241 only does causal SDPA). Before the delta the gemma2 family had no masking patcher, so the mask was always dense and carried the window - the hole is new in this delta. This is an incomplete fix of the same defect class as OPQ-337 / Bazalt #811 ('sliding window dropped under SDPA when attention_mask is None') and directly contradicts Slate #397's invariant.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced end to end on transformers-installed Gemma2. `Gemma2Config(hidden_size=32, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=8, sliding_window=4, attn_logit_softcapping=None, attention_dropout=0.0)`, `_attn_implementation='sdpa'`, float64, `input_ids` of shape (1, 24): unpatched logits vs logits after `apply_runtime_patches()` + `apply_model_patches(model)` differ by 0.4171 max-abs while mean |logit| is 0.0802 - a 5x-the-mean deviation. Control with `attn_logit_softcapping=50.0` (the config default) on the same weights and inputs: 6.1e-08. Direct unit check at the attention level (H=2, S=16, D=8, window 4, float64): `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window` matches an explicit windowed reference to 0.0, `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2(..., softcap=None, sliding_window=4)` deviates 1.9777 from that reference and matches plain full-causal SDPA to exactly 0.0. Disabling `attn_logit_softcapping` is the documented workaround for using SDPA/flash with Gemma2, so this is a realistic configuration; every sliding layer then trains and evaluates on full causal attention with no error or warning.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:729-738 - `return vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(module, query, key, value, attention_mask, dropout=dropout, scaling=scaling, **kwargs)` - `sliding_window` is a named parameter of the enclosing function (line 678) so it is NOT in **kwargs and is dropped entirely

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:174-241 - `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward` has no sliding-window handling at all; it only computes `is_causal` and calls SDPA

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/models/gemma2.py:30-36 - `sdpa_attention_replacement=vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2` paired with `masking_module_patcher=apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch`

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/runtime/masking.py:89-107 - `_can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window` returns True (mask becomes None) without consulting `attn_logit_softcapping`

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/models/mistral.py:32-33 and ministral.py:32-33 pair the same patcher with `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window`, which does honour the window (attention.py:277-305)

git show 4b13d82:.../components/attention.py:160-196 - at the delta base the gemma2 softcap=None branch delegated to stock `sdpa_attention_forward` and gemma2 had no masking patcher, so the dense mask always carried the window
measured: patched-vs-upstream Gemma2ForCausalLM logits max|diff| = 0.4170584599232694 with attn_logit_softcapping=None vs 6.142407904530245e-08 with 50.0, same weights/inputs
findings.fix_sketch: In `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2`, route the `softcap is None` fall-through to `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window(..., sliding_window=sliding_window, ...)` instead of `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward`, so the compact windowed path is used whenever the mask is None. Alternatively make `_can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window` refuse the None-mask skip for gemma2 when softcapping is disabled. Add a parity test that instantiates a gemma2 with `attn_logit_softcapping=None`, `sliding_window < seq_len`, sdpa and no attention mask - the existing sliding-window parity variant always supplies a mask, so this branch is untested.

findings.title: New random-allocation lru_cache retains native PLD handles past calibrate's cache teardown, with a docstring that denies it
findings.claim: Slate #437 replaced every per-method `functools` PLD cache with a bounded registry whose native handles `calibrate` drops in its `finally` (calibration.py:210-212, 356-357 `_clear_all_native_caches()`). Delta commit 20dd47aa (#881) introduced a new `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8)` over `_native.random_allocation_gaussian_pld`. Its return type is `Pld`, which `_base.py:60` aliases as `_native.Pld` - a Rust-backed handle - so the module docstring's claim that the cache holds 'immutable Python Pld objects (no native handles), so it is self-limiting and needs no byte budget or destructor' is false, as is the '~0.5 MB per entry at the default config' sizing comment. The cache is not registered in `_native_cache._registry`, so `_clear_all_native_caches()` is a no-op for it and only the module-private `clear_random_allocation_caches()` (called from tests only) empties it.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured on the current tree with the freshly built extension. (a) `cal.calibrate(cal.epsilon_budget(3.0, delta=1e-5), lambda nm: k_out_of_t(gaussian(nm), k=4, t=64, allocation='block'), 0.5, 4.0)` leaves `epoch_pld.cache_info() == CacheInfo(hits=0, misses=14, maxsize=8, currsize=8)` and a subsequent `_clear_all_native_caches()` leaves currsize at 8 - the calibration retained 8 native PLDs it will never reuse (every probe has a distinct noise multiplier, hence hits=0). (b) Holding 8 distinct `random_allocation_gaussian_pld(sigma_i, 64, 4, default_config)` handles grew RSS from 19.5 MB to 199.7 MB (+180.3 MB, ~22 MB per entry, ~45x the documented 0.5 MB); dropping them returned RSS to 117.0 MB. A long-lived service that calibrates several k-out-of-t or balls-in-bins configurations therefore carries ~100-180 MB of Rust PLD grids the API contract says are released.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_random_allocation_cache.py:5-9 - 'The cache is a bounded LRU over immutable Python :class:`Pld` objects (no native handles), so it is self-limiting and needs no byte budget or destructor.'
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_random_allocation_cache.py:24-27 - '~0.5 MB per entry at the default config'
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:60 - `Pld: TypeAlias = _native.Pld`

packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/calibration.py:356-357 - `finally: _clear_all_native_caches()`; _native_cache.py:26,40-42 iterate only the `NativeCache` weak registry, which this lru_cache never joins
consumers: _k_out_of_t.py:19,114-119 and dpftrl/amplification/_balls_in_bins.py:60 both call `epoch_pld`

findings.title: Python 3.12 is still advertised by every wheel and executed by no CI lane
findings.claim: Slate #428 ('Test the supported Python 3.12 runtime') is still unmet at 12146ec4. findings.title: Published install instructions install an unrelated PyPI project instead of Opaque
findings.claim: The repository is public and its documentation site is live. The 'From JetBrains Packages' commands correctly pass --index-url (installation.md:20, :27; README.md:68, :72), but the 'Extras' block immediately below them drops it: `pip install "opaque[auditing]"`, `"opaque[dpftrl]"`, `"opaque[transformers]"`, `"opaque[all]"`. With no index override pip resolves `opaque` from PyPI, where that name belongs to a different project entirely - `opaque` 1.0.0, 'python libopaque wrapper' by Stefan Marsiske (https://github.com/stef/libopaque). The extras are silently ignored (pip only warns about unknown extras), so the user ends up with an unrelated cryptography binding and no Opaque at all. The Opaque distribution names are largely unclaimed on PyPI: `opaque-dpsgd` 404s, and `opaque-accounting` resolves to a metadata-less 999.9.9 placeholder, so the namespace is not defensively held.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of https://jetbrains-research.github.io/opaque/latest/getting-started/installation/ (live, verified 200) wants DP-FTRL. They copy `pip install "opaque[dpftrl]"` from the Extras block. pip downloads opaque-1.0.0.tar.gz from PyPI and installs a libopaque wrapper; `import opaque.dpftrl` then fails with ModuleNotFoundError and the user concludes the library is broken. Reproduced verbatim in a clean venv: `pip install --dry-run --no-deps "opaque[auditing]"` prints 'Downloading opaque-1.0.0.tar.gz (10 kB)' and 'Would install opaque-1.0.0'. Because `opaque-dpsgd` is an unclaimed name on PyPI, the same missing-index pattern is also the shape a dependency-confusion upload would exploit.

README.md:76-82 - identical Extras block under the --index-url block at :66-73

pip install --dry-run --no-deps "opaque[auditing]" in a fresh python3 -m venv -> 'Downloading opaque-1.0.0.tar.gz (10 kB)' ... 'Would install opaque-1.0.0'
https://pypi.org/pypi/opaque/json -> name 'opaque', version '1.0.0', summary 'python libopaque wrapper', author 'Stefan Marsiske', home_page https://github.com/stef/libopaque
https://pypi.org/pypi/opaque-dpsgd/json -> 404; https://pypi.org/pypi/opaque-accounting/json -> 200 with version '999.9.9', summary null, author null
GitHub API for JetBrains-Research/opaque: visibility 'public', homepage https://jetbrains-research.github.io/opaque/
findings.fix_sketch: Carry the index into every documented command - either append `--index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` to each extras line, or restructure the section as one `pip install --index-url <jb> "opaque[all]"` with a note that the extras names are `auditing`, `dpftrl`, `alignment`, `transformers`, `trl`. Do the same in README.md and packages/opaque-accounting/README.md. Separately, register the `opaque*` distribution names on PyPI (even as placeholders that point at the real index) so the public names cannot be claimed by someone else, and consider an ARC-011 post-build scenario that runs each documented install command verbatim in a clean container and asserts `import opaque.dpsgd` succeeds.

findings.title: privacy_auditing tutorial prices a shuffled fixed-batch loop with Poisson amplification and uses the result as the audit ceiling
findings.line: code cell 13 (theoretical bound); training loop in code cell 9
findings.claim: This is the exact OPQ-355 defect, alive in a sibling notebook that #843's fix did not touch and that the new CI step does not execute. Cell 9 trains with `DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)` - fixed-size shuffled batches, not Poisson sampling. Cell 13 then computes `process = dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(noise_multiplier), sample_rate) * total_steps` and prints it as 'Theoretical epsilon'. Poisson subsampling amplification does not hold for shuffled fixed-size batches; the conservative analysis for that loop is unamplified composition. The notebook then compares the audited epsilon against this understated ceiling and prints 'OK: audited epsilon is within the theoretical bound', which is precisely the sanity check .junie/differential-privacy-review.md says must be sound ('treat an empirical lower bound above the theoretical upper bound as a likely defect'). Cell 9 additionally divides the noised sum by the realised batch size (`p - (lr / bs) * g`) rather than a fixed expected batch size, so the released update is a function of a data-dependent quantity the mechanism never noised - the fixed dp_sgd_training.ipynb explicitly comments the opposite ('Gradients are already normalized by the fixed expected batch size').
findings.failure_scenario: With the notebook's own parameters (noise_multiplier=0.5, batch_size=64, n_epochs=200, ~250 training examples after the coin flip, so total_steps=600 and sample_rate=0.256) the published 'Theoretical epsilon' is 253.2 while the conservative no-amplification bound for the same 600 releases is 1408.9 - a 5.6x understatement. A reader who copies this pattern (shuffled DataLoader + Poisson-amplified accountant) into their own run reports an epsilon 5.6x smaller than anything they can justify, and the notebook's audit 'OK' line actively confirms the wrong number. The same notebook is what the auditing guide points readers at.
evidence: docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb code cell 9: `train_loader = DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)` then `params = tuple(p - (lr / bs) * g for p, g in zip(params, noisy_grads.pytree))`

docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb code cell 13: `sample_rate = batch_size / len(train_data)`; `total_steps = n_epochs * (len(train_data) // batch_size)`; `process = dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(noise_multiplier), sample_rate) * total_steps`; `theoretical_eps = process.epsilon_at(1e-5)`; `if audited_eps <= theoretical_eps: print("OK: ...")`
docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb code cell 7: noise_multiplier = 0.5, batch_size = 64, n_epochs = 200; cell 3: n_samples = 500; cell 5: coin_flip over all 500 leaves ~250 in-canaries
Computed with the shipped accountant at n_train=250: poisson-amplified eps = 253.222, unamplified (dpsgd_acc.gaussian(0.5) * 600) eps = 1408.936, ratio 5.6x

.github/workflows/pr.yml:294-301 executes only accounting_and_calibration.ipynb, dp_sgd_training.ipynb and dp_ftrl_training.ipynb; privacy_auditing.ipynb, sampling_and_microbatching.ipynb, distributed_training.ipynb and llm_finetuning.ipynb are in the mkdocs nav (mkdocs.yml:135-145) but are never executed

docs/tutorials/sampling_and_microbatching.ipynb code cell 9 has the same realised-batch-size normalisation (`p - (lr / bs) * g` with no normalize_by on clipped_grad)

findings.title: Sweep A's executable-docs gate executes no Markdown snippet and only 3 of 7 notebooks
findings.claim: Issue #843's acceptance criteria were 'Every documented accounting and training snippet executes as written, in CI' and 'The executable-docs check runs on every PR, so this class cannot recur silently'. The step 12146ec4 added executes exactly three things: `examples/quickstart.py`, `python -m doctest packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py`, and three of the seven tutorial notebooks. It executes zero of the 369 ```python fences spread across 46 Markdown files under docs/ - including every snippet the ten Sweep A findings were about. The one page that is genuinely protected (quickstart.md) is protected because it was rewritten to transclude the executed script, which is the right pattern but was applied to exactly one page. Nothing prevents the next accounting snippet from drifting, which is the recurrence the issue set out to stop. The same gap exists on main: docs.yml deploys the public site on every push with `mike deploy` (a non-strict mkdocs build) and no doc-execution step at all, so the strict build and the execution step exist only on the PR path.
findings.failure_scenario: A future PR changes an accounting factory signature and updates the reference table but not the snippet in docs/user-guide/accounting.md. `mkdocs build --strict` still passes (it does not execute code), the three notebooks and quickstart.py still pass (they do not use that snippet), and the drifted snippet ships to the public docs site. This is the same mechanism that produced OPQ-357, OPQ-361, OPQ-362, OPQ-363, OPQ-364 and OPQ-365 in the first place. The residual `optimizer.step()` call in reference/rng.md (filed separately) is a live instance that survived Sweep A itself.

docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:11 - `--8<-- "examples/quickstart.py:4:"`; verified live at https://jetbrains-research.github.io/opaque/latest/getting-started/quickstart/ (renders the real source, no leaked snippet marker)

findings.title: Per-group Gaussian noise has no realized-vs-reported conformance test; a 3% shortfall passes the whole suite
findings.claim: OPQ-378's fix sketch named three shapes: 'gaussian_noise, per-group gaussian_noise and mf_gaussian_noise'. PR #871 delivered scalar gaussian_noise and six mf_gaussian_noise strategies but not the per-group path, and no other test binds realized per-group noise magnitude to the reported PerGroup noise_stddev. The only magnitude assertion for per-group noise is a ratio check on 100 samples (`mlp_var > attn_var * 2.5`), which is invariant to a uniform scale error, and test_gaussian_second_moment.py / test_paired_noise_stddevs.py only assert that the reported metadata is a PerGroup of the right values. The paired second-moment streams have the same gap.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified by targeted mutation. With a plugin that makes only the per-group lookup inside gaussian_noise's `_add_noise_tree` return 0.97x its value - so the drawn noise is 3% low while `output.noise_stddev` still reports the correct PerGroup and the accountant is still charged `gaussian(nm)` - the entire PR-gate suite for opaque-dpsgd plus opaque-engine passes: 1355 passed, 26 skipped, 148 deselected, 0 failed. The same 3% shortfall applied globally (scaling torch.randn) is caught by 10 tests. So a regression in the per-group cast/lookup path - an fp32/bf16 round trip, a wrong ParamPath resolution, a recomputed group bound - ships green while users at a reported nm are charged for noise they did not receive.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_per_group_noise.py:44-49 - the only magnitude assertion is `attn_var = ...; mlp_var = ...; assert mlp_var > attn_var * 2.5` over 100-element tensors
packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_noise.py:129-139 and packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise/test_realized_stddev.py:41-48,101-158 - the seven new conformance tests, all scalar-stddev

Mutation A (global, torch.randn * 0.97) over packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise + packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise: 10 failed, 372 passed (baseline 382 passed) - failures include all 7 conformance cases
Mutation B (PerGroup.for_path * 0.97 only when the caller frame is `_add_noise_tree`) over packages/opaque-dpsgd + packages/opaque-engine under the PR marker: 1355 passed, 26 skipped, 0 failed

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py:206-228 - the per-group branch of `_add_noise_tree` that the mutation targets; :340 sets `noise_stddev=effective_stddev` from `_clipped_stddev`, so applied and reported can diverge only inside `_sample`/the path lookup
findings.fix_sketch: Add two cases to the existing `_assert_realized_stddev_matches_reported` helper: one `gaussian_noise` call with a PerGroup max_norm over two 5e5-element leaves, asserting each leaf's realized RMS against `output.noise_stddev.for_path(path)` at 6/sqrt(2n); and one paired `SecondMomentClippingOutput` case checking both `noisy_grads` and `noisy_squared_grads` against their respective reported stddevs. Both are cheap and belong in the same file as the scalar case.

findings.title: TRY003 was enabled in the same commit that introduced a 179-site idiom Ruff cannot see, so the new lint rule enforces nothing
findings.claim: 7b26f655 (PR #760, 'feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy') moved TRY003 from `ignore` into `select` and, in the same commit, rewrote 158 raise sites into the form `raise SomeError(*("message",))`. Ruff's TRY003 matches a long message passed as a positional argument to the exception constructor; a starred tuple is not matched, so every one of those sites is invisible to the rule. The count is now 179 across packages/*/src and was 0 at 4b13d82. The same commit also added TRY003 to the per-file-ignores for `**/tests/**` and `tests/**`, so the rule is disabled in every test tree as well. The result is a lint rule that is nominally part of the merge gate and cannot fire. The comment block that documents the choice still lists TRY003 under 'Omitted only when they fight intentional design', contradicting the `select` entry three lines below it. ff174f11 (PR #897), whose subject is 'restore the lint gate by fixing three TRY003 violations', converted its three findings into exactly this splat form rather than into message-carrying exception classes.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor writes `raise ConfigurationError(f"bands must be >= 1, got {bands}")` the obvious way. Ruff flags TRY003 and the autoformat gate fails. The contributor greps the codebase, finds 179 examples of `raise ConfigurationError(*("...",))`, copies that, and the gate goes green - having changed nothing about the property the rule exists to enforce, while making the call site harder to read and defeating any type checker's arity check on the constructor. Meanwhile the repository carries a merge-gate rule whose violation count is structurally pinned at zero. Verified: `ruff check --select TRY003 packages/ tests/` -> 'All checks passed!'.
evidence: pyproject.toml:248 - "TRY003" in [tool.ruff.lint].select; pyproject.toml:261-267 - `ignore` no longer contains it

pyproject.toml:215-223 - the 'Omitted only when they fight intentional design' comment block still lists TRY003 with the rationale 'public semantic categories carry stable catch contracts without a bespoke exception class per diagnostic message'
pyproject.toml:299-300 - `"**/tests/**" = ["INP001", "D", "PLR2004", "TRY003"]` and the same for `"tests/**"`
git grep -E 'raise [A-Za-z_]+(Error|Exception)\(\*\(' -- packages : 0 hits at 4b13d82, 179 hits at 12146ec4
git show 7b26f655 -- pyproject.toml shows the select/per-file-ignores change; the same commit adds 158 `(*(` raise sites across 170 files
git show ff174f11 converts `raise ValueError("dataset_size must be provided ...")` into `raise ConfigurationError(*("dataset_size must be provided ...",))`

Reproduced: `raise E(f"n_steps must be >= 1, got {n}")` piped through `ruff check --select TRY003 --stdin-filename packages/opaque-engine/src/.../probe.py -` -> TRY003, exit 1; the identical code as `raise E(*(f"...",))` -> 'All checks passed!', exit 0
`ruff check --no-cache --select TRY003 packages/ tests/` on the current tree -> 'All checks passed!'
findings.fix_sketch: Decide which it is and make the config say so. Either keep TRY003 in `ignore` with the existing rationale and revert the 179 splats to plain string arguments (they read better and type-check), or keep the rule and give the exception taxonomy message-carrying constructors so the splat is unnecessary. Either way, fix the comment at pyproject.toml:215-223 so it no longer documents TRY003 as omitted while selecting it.

findings.title: The per-package wheel build inventory in build-distributions.yml has no coverage guard
findings.claim: OPQ-380 named two hand-maintained inventories: the test-package matrix in python-tests.yml and the per-package build steps in build-distributions.yml. PR #870 guarded the first and left the second untouched. build-distributions.yml still has ten literal `uv build packages/opaque-<name> --wheel --out-dir dist` steps (plus opaque-accounting in the separate native job) and nothing checks that list against `packages/*`. This is the higher-stakes of the two inventories: a package missing from the test matrix runs no tests, while a package missing here is never built and never published. The downstream checks do not close it either - `validate-distributions.yml:68` asserts only `len(opaque_versions) > 1`, and `check_wheel_internal_pins.py` validates pins on the wheels that exist rather than checking that all expected wheels do.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor adds `packages/opaque-<new>/` with a tests/ tree and a pyproject. The new #870 guard correctly fails the lane until they add it to python-tests.yml, so the tests get wired up. Nothing forces the corresponding edit to build-distributions.yml. If the umbrella `opaque` distribution does not depend on the new package (the common case for an optional stack), no wheel is ever built, `validate-distributions` still passes (`len(opaque_versions) > 1` holds), and both the dev-wheel publish on main and the release publish ship a set that silently omits it. Users installing from the JetBrains index get an ImportError for a package the repository documents.
evidence: .github/workflows/build-distributions.yml:46-74 - ten hardcoded 'Build opaque-*' steps; opaque-accounting is built separately at :141-163
.github/workflows/python-tests.yml:102-125 - the guard added by 6de5f9ca, scoped to the suite matrix only, reading its own file
.github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml:61-69 - `assert len(opaque_versions) > 1` is the only completeness check on the published set
.github/scripts/check_wheel_internal_pins.py:188-195 - iterates `args.wheel_dir.glob("*.whl")`, i.e. only the wheels that were built
OPQ-380 evidence line: '`build-distributions.yml:73-74` hardcodes per-package build steps the same way'
findings.fix_sketch: Either replace the ten steps with a loop over `packages/*/pyproject.toml` (excluding opaque-accounting, which maturin builds), or add the same comm-based guard used in python-tests.yml as a first step of build-python-wheels. A stronger alternative: have check_wheel_internal_pins.py additionally assert that the set of dist names found in --wheel-dir equals the set of `project.name` values across the root and packages/*/pyproject.toml.

findings.title: The value-level CachedProcess.repeated_pld regression test was deleted one day after it landed, leaving only a mock with no real implementor
findings.claim: OPQ-379 asked for a value-level epsilon assertion on a correlated strategy because the surviving guards used the one strategy where the buggy and correct answers coincide. PR #885 added exactly that (`test_cached_correlated_full_horizon_preserves_epsilon`, band_mf bands=16, n_steps=128) on 2026-09-02. 87404a1b (PR #894) deleted packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_per_step.py in full on 2026-09-03, taking that test with the acc.per_step API it depended on. What remains is the mock test in test_cached.py, which patches `repeated_pld` onto an `eps_delta` process to manufacture a divergence. After #894 there is no subclass in the tree that overrides `repeated_pld` other than CachedProcess itself, so the relay is a no-op on every shipped process and the mock is guarding a contract nothing currently implements - while `DpProcess.repeated_pld`'s own docstring still invites subclasses to override it.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified by mutation: `del CachedProcess.repeated_pld` over packages/opaque-accounting/tests + packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting + packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting gives 1 failed / 601 passed, and the single failure is the mock test. The exposure is forward-looking: when a future mechanism reintroduces a count-sensitive `repeated_pld` override (the docstring at _base.py:428-433 explicitly anticipates 'DP-FTRL per-step adapters, where K steps' joint PLD depends on the deployed N-step strategy's correlation matrix'), the only thing standing between that and a silent reversion to `pld().self_compose(K)` is a mock that will still pass because it patches its own stub. OPQ-005 measured that divergence at 2.17x epsilon for band_mf(bands=16), n=128, K=128.

git log --diff-filter=D 4b13d82..12146ec4 -- packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_per_step.py -> 87404a1b
grep -rn 'test_cached_correlated_full_horizon_preserves_epsilon' over the whole tree -> no hits at 12146ec4
grep -rn 'def repeated_pld' packages/*/src -> only _base.py:418 (the default) and composition/_cached.py:84 (the relay)

Mutation `del CachedProcess.repeated_pld` over the three accounting test trees under the PR marker: 1 failed, 601 passed; the failure is test_cached.py::test_cached_process_preserves_repeated_pld_override with 'assert 3.0 == 2.0'
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:428-433 - docstring still says subclasses whose K-fold behaviour differs 'override this to compute the true K-step PLD directly'
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the mock test, and add a real one next to it: define a two-line DpProcess subclass in the test file whose `repeated_pld(count)` returns a demonstrably different PLD from `pld().self_compose(count)`, wrap it in `acc.cached(...)`, and assert `(cached * n).epsilon_at(delta) == (inner * n).epsilon_at(delta)` while `inner.pld().self_compose(n).epsilon_at(delta)` differs. That guards the relay against both deletion and a wrong-count relay without depending on any mechanism that may later be removed.

findings.title: allow-empty-test-selection still lets two distributed-lane legs report green on zero collected tests
findings.claim: Issue #836 (OPQ-381) was closed as not_planned with no code change, so the exit-5-to-success conversion and the four lanes that enable it are exactly as reported. The CUDA half of the original exposure is now covered by the #832 preflight, which fails a `cuda`-marker lane on a host without CUDA regardless of how many tests were collected. The distributed half is not: nothing asserts that a lane whose marker is expected to select tests actually selected any, and two of the five suite legs still select nothing today, so their green check carries no information.
findings.failure_scenario: Re-measured at 12146ec4 under the distributed lane's exact marker `distributed and not cuda`: opaque-base 0, opaque-accounting 0, opaque-auditing 0 (the whole 'Foundation' leg), opaque-patches 0, and `tests` 0 (the whole 'Integration tests' leg). findings.title: Python 3.12 is claimed by eleven pyproject classifiers with zero CI coverage and no documented endpoints-only policy
findings.claim: Issue #841 (OPQ-386) was closed as not_planned. Neither of its two acceptance branches was taken: there is still no 3.12 leg anywhere, and the endpoints-only choice is not written down as a policy in AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md, both of which enumerate the lanes in detail. `grep -rn '3\.12' .github/` returns zero hits across all fourteen workflows, four composite actions and nine scripts, while `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"` resolves 3.12 and every distribution ships the 3.12 classifier. Bounded in practice because 3.11 and 3.13 bracket most interpreter-sensitive behaviour, and nothing here changes a privacy guarantee. The second-order cost is that the next reader of the lane list cannot tell whether 3.12 is untested by decision or by the accident of the #665 version bump that retargeted the 3.12 lanes to 3.13.

findings.title: docs/reference/rng.md calls optimizer.step(), which the functional optimizer does not have
findings.claim: reference/rng.md was one of the pages Sweep A (#843) covered - OPQ-362 was specifically about this file, and 12146ec4 changed 22 lines in it, correcting every gaussian_noise call to keyword form. The determinism example a few lines above those fixes still ends with `optimizer.step(noisy_grads)`. `opaque.optimizers.sgd(...)` returns a `torchopt.base.GradientTransformation` whose public members are `chain, count, index, init, update`; there is no `step`. Every other end-to-end snippet in the docs uses the correct `updates, opt_state = optimizer.update(...)` then `torchopt.apply_updates(...)` pair. findings.claim: Issue #844 opened by observing that '#419 reconciled the tables once by hand; they drifted again, so the fix needs to be a generator or a check rather than another pass', and its first acceptance criterion was 'Every published default and accepted-value list is generated from, or checked against, its dataclass in CI'. findings.title: Loss-scaler removal deleted ClippingStats.all_finite, the only signal that clipping silently zeroes non-finite per-example gradients; the sanitization it diagnosed is unchanged and nothing replaced the signal
findings.claim: 7f55aae5 (#889) removed the data-dependent loss scaler and, in the same commit, deleted `_all_finite()`, the `aux_dict["all_finite"]` production in `clipped_fun`, the `all_finite` accumulation in `_microbatch_accumulate_stats_only`, and the public `ClippingStats.all_finite` field. The behaviour that field reported is unchanged: `clip_pytree` and `auto_scale` still begin with `tree_map(lambda t: torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0), pytree)` (_pytree.py:601 and :465), so a per-example gradient that overflows or NaNs is replaced by zeros and that record contributes nothing to the released sum. After #889 there is no signal at any layer: `ClippingStats` carries only `num_clipped`, `clipping_rate`, `batch_size`; `ClippedGradAux.grad_norms` is computed after the sanitization so a dropped record reports norm 0.0, indistinguishable from a genuinely zero gradient; and `clipping_rate` goes DOWN when records are dropped, so the failure reads as an improvement. OPQ-330 (#804) was specifically about the feedback loop `stats.all_finite -> LossScaler.update`; the fix also removed the read-only diagnostic, which was never part of the privacy defect — a statistic that is never fed back into training is not an adaptive query.
findings.failure_scenario: Executed on the current tree (repo venv, torch 2.14): fp16 params, `loss(p,x,s) = ((p['w']*x)*s).sum()`, batch rows x=[10,20,30,1000] with per-example scale s=[1,1,1,100]. Because the forward evaluates (p*x)*s, every per-example loss stays finite (`loss_values = [4.0e-3, 8.0e-3, 1.2e-2, 40.0]`, `isfinite().all() == True`) while row 4's gradient x*s = 1e5 overflows fp16 to inf. `clipped_grad(..., clipping_norm=1.0, normalize_by=4, return_aux=True)` returns `grad_norms = tensor([20., 40., 60., 0.])`, `clipped_grad_norms = tensor([0.9995, 0.9995, 0.9995, 0.0000])`; the same call with `return_stats=True` returns `ClippingStats(num_clipped=3.0, clipping_rate=0.75, batch_size=4)`. Row 4 contributed exactly nothing and nothing in the output says so; before #889 the same `return_stats=True` call returned `all_finite=False`. Under `adaptive_clipped_grad` this compounds: the quantile tracker sees the sanitized norm 0.0 for every dropped record, so the adaptive threshold is driven down by exactly the examples that were discarded. No user-facing document states that clipping drops records this way — `grep -rn -iE 'non-finite|nonfinite|NaN/Inf|sanitiz' docs/` returns nothing and `ClippingStats`/`return_stats` appear nowhere under docs/.
evidence: git show 7f55aae5 -- packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py: deletes `def _all_finite(value)`, the field `all_finite: bool = True` with docstring "Whether every pre-clipping output in the batch was finite.", `if return_stats: aux_dict["all_finite"] = _all_finite(value)`, and the `all_finite=all_finite` accumulation in the microbatch path

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_pytree.py:599-606 - `pytree = tree_map(lambda t: (torch.nan_to_num(t, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0) ...), pytree)` at the head of clip_pytree; identical block at :463-470 in auto_scale

executed repro output: loss_values=tensor([4.0016e-03, 8.0032e-03, 1.2001e-02, 4.0000e+01], dtype=torch.float16) True / grad_norms=tensor([20., 40., 60.,  0.]) / stats=ClippingStats(num_clipped=3.0, clipping_rate=0.75, batch_size=4)

docs/user-guide/precision.md:47-48 "Opaque therefore does not expose a loss scaler or an aggregate pre-clipping finiteness signal." and :50-51 "Low-level clipping and noise primitives still accept fp16 tensors" - the docs state the signal is gone but never state that records with non-finite gradients are dropped
grep -rn -iE 'non-finite|nonfinite|NaN/Inf|sanitiz' docs/ -> no matches; grep -rn 'ClippingStats|return_stats' docs/ -> no matches
findings.fix_sketch: Restore a read-only, non-feedback drop counter on ClippingStats (e.g. `num_nonfinite: float | dict[str, float]` computed from the same pre-clipping value `_all_finite` used) and document, in the adaptive-clipping gating style, that it must not drive any training decision. If the signal must stay removed, state explicitly in docs/user-guide/clipping.md and docs/user-guide/precision.md that per-example gradients containing NaN/Inf are replaced with zeros, that the affected records contribute nothing to the release, and that grad_norms == 0.0 is the only (ambiguous) trace.

findings.title: Bounded-Gaussian removal's replacement docs advertise float16/bfloat16 as accepted compute_dtype values on the DPTrainer surface, contradicting precision.md's explicit "do not lower" rule for the same knob
findings.claim: 873de427 (#1021) replaced the `bound` documentation on `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs` with new text that presents `compute_dtype` and enumerates `float16, bfloat16, float32, float64` as accepted string names, with no caveat, in both DPTrainer-facing tables. The same commit added `_validate_compute_dtype`/`_SUPPORTED_COMPUTE_DTYPES` in `_gaussian.py` and `_normalize_gaussian_compute_dtype` in `_training_arguments.py`, both of which accept float16/bfloat16 silently (no warning, no log line). This contradicts docs/user-guide/precision.md:68-70 - the page that owns this knob, rewritten by the sibling removal 7f55aae5 - which states: "Do not lower precision without a separate numerical argument. Setting compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16 or torch.float16 can make the realized sensitivity and noise scale diverge from the accountant's model." A DPTrainer user reading the reference table has no prompt to consult precision.md, and the change is one config line.
findings.failure_scenario: A user sets `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={"compute_dtype": "bfloat16"}` - a value the reference table names - to cut noise-sampling memory. Verified end to end: TrainingArguments accepts it and normalizes to `{'compute_dtype': torch.bfloat16}`; _dp_trainer.py:1676-1690 forwards it verbatim into `gaussian_noise(**_gn_extra)`; _gaussian.py:190-204 then computes `center_c = center.to(torch.bfloat16)` and `sample = center_c + std * noise` entirely in bfloat16, so the released vector's pre-noise component is a bfloat16 rounding of the clipped sum and its norm can exceed the accounted clip norm. Measured over 200 draws of a 4096-dim gradient placed exactly on the clip sphere (C=1.0, noise_multiplier=1e-8): worst realized norm 1.0001227260086283 under compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16 (relative excess 1.23e-4) versus 1.0000001791386004 under torch.float32 (1.79e-7) - the realized sensitivity exceeds the C the accountant is calibrated to by roughly 700x more margin. Separately the noise becomes coarsely discretized: 200000 draws at nm=1.0 gave 2945 distinct values under bfloat16 versus 199721 under float32, so the released mechanism is a coarse discrete approximation of the continuous Gaussian the PLD assumes. Neither effect produces any warning. The measured sensitivity inflation is small (1.2e-4 relative); the discretization effect was not converted into an epsilon delta and would need a floating-point-DP analysis (Mironov 2012) to bound.
evidence: git show 873de427 -- docs/reference/transformers.md: `-| privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs | ... | Forwarded into the noise mechanism factory (e.g. bound for bounded Gaussian). |` replaced by `+| ... | Gaussian accepts compute_dtype as a native torch.dtype or a string name (float16, bfloat16, float32, float64); MF mechanisms accept strategy-specific kwargs. |`
git show 873de427 -- docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md: the same substitution at line 138
docs/user-guide/precision.md:68-70 - the contradicting rule, on the page the sibling removal 7f55aae5 rewrote

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py:60-62 `_SUPPORTED_COMPUTE_DTYPES = frozenset({torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.float64})` and :111-124 `_validate_compute_dtype` - accepts all four, no warning path
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:1556-1584 `_normalize_gaussian_compute_dtype` - maps the string names to torch dtypes, no warning

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py:190-204 - `center_c = center.to(compute_dtype) if in_dtype != compute_dtype else center; sample = center_c + std * noise`, i.e. the clipped sum is downcast before noise is added
executed: TrainingArguments with {'compute_dtype':'bfloat16'} -> OK {'compute_dtype': torch.bfloat16}; 'float64' -> OK torch.float64; 'int8' -> ConfigurationError

measured worst realized norm on the clip sphere over 200 trials: bfloat16 1.0001227260086283 vs float32 1.0000001791386004 (C=1.0); noise value cardinality 2945 (bf16) vs 199721 (fp32) over 200000 samples at nm=1.0
findings.fix_sketch: Either restrict the DPTrainer surface to the dtypes precision.md endorses (float32/float64) and reject float16/bfloat16 in `_normalize_gaussian_compute_dtype` with a message pointing at precision.md, or keep them and emit a one-time RuntimeWarning from `_validate_compute_dtype` whenever compute_dtype is narrower than float32, adding the precision.md caveat inline to docs/reference/transformers.md:196 and docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:138. Independently, stop downcasting the query: compute the noisy sum in the wider of `compute_dtype` and `center.dtype` so lowering compute_dtype cannot inflate the realized sensitivity above the accounted max_norm.

findings.claim: 873de427 (#1021) added an explicit guard rejecting `privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['bound']` at _training_arguments.py:1222-1228 ("is unsupported: Opaque does not provide a matching privacy accountant") and stripped `bound` from the trainer's `_gn_extra` filter, but left `_MECHANISM_KWARGS["gaussian"] = frozenset({"bound", "compute_dtype"})` at :229 untouched. That set is the allow-list `_validate_privacy_kwargs` prints in its unknown-key error, so any typo in the gaussian mechanism kwargs produces an error message recommending the key the very next validator refuses - and naming a mechanism the library deliberately deleted because it has no matching accountant.

findings.title: Default-on fused-CE forward wrapper silently drops Cohere logit_scale / Granite logits_scaling / Gemma2 final_logit_softcapping on its non-fused branch
findings.claim:
c0f95ced (#988 'activate fused loss-only cross-entropy') flipped `fused_linear_cross_entropy` from opt-in to default-on: `_factory.py:374-376` now does `enable_fused_linear_ce = kwargs.get('fused_linear_cross_entropy'); if enable_fused_linear_ce is None: enable_fused_linear_ce = performance`, and `_dp_trainer.py:844-850` always passes `performance=True`. Previously the gate was `kwargs.get('fused_linear_cross_entropy', False)` (git show c0f95ced), so the wrapper was never installed unless explicitly requested. The wrapper replaces the model's own `forward`. When its fused branch is declined it falls through to its own re-implementation of the HF tail:
```python
logits = self.lm_head(hidden_states[:, slice_indices, :])
loss = self.loss_function(logits, labels, self.vocab_size, **kwargs)
```
This omits the post-`lm_head` transform that the upstream HF `forward` applies for five of the seventeen families listed in `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM`: Cohere/Cohere2 `logits = logits * self.logit_scale` (transformers/models/cohere/modeling_cohere.py:503), Granite `logits = logits / self.config.logits_scaling` (granite/modeling_granite.py:497), Gemma2/Gemma3 `final_logit_softcapping` tanh (gemma2/modeling_gemma2.py:527-530). The fused branch handles them correctly (it threads `logit_scale` and `softcap` into the kernels, cross_entropy.py:312-323); only the fallback branch is wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: DPTrainer DP-SFT of a Cohere / Command-R, Granite, or Gemma2 checkpoint on a CUDA GPU with the default `bf16=False` (`_training_arguments.py:415`, `_setup_precision` sets `_amp_dtype=None`). The trainer sets `loss_only=True` (`_dp_trainer.py:2442`) because `_fused_forward_uses_marker` is True by default, but `use_fused_ce` requires `hidden_states.is_cuda and hidden_states.dtype in (bfloat16, float16)`; fp32 hidden states on CUDA fail that test, so the else branch runs and every per-example loss and gradient is computed on untransformed logits. Measured on CPU (forcing the same branch with `shift_labels`, which `_fused_linear_ce_loss_is_supported` also rejects and which is device-independent): Cohere loss 4.92499 vs HF 4.16748 (18.2% error), Granite 4.35990 vs 4.16075 (4.8%), with the fused branch matching HF exactly. findings.title: The multi-output `apply` override added by #987 breaks `torch.func.grad` without an enclosing `vmap` for both linear-CE kernels
findings.line: 278-281 (apply override) and 330 (`_, lse, token_weight = output`); same pattern at linear_cross_entropy.py:1005-1008 and :1061
findings.claim:
a839782e (#987 'reuse fused cross-entropy statistics') changed both linear-CE autograd Functions to return four/three outputs and added a classmethod override that hides the extras:
```python
@classmethod
def apply(cls, *args):
    return super().apply(*args)[0]
```
Under the functorch Grad transform, `custom_function_call_grad` builds a single-level `Generated` function whose `forward` re-enters `custom_function_call(autograd_function, ...)` at the level below (torch/_functorch/autograd_function.py:106-145). With no vmap level left, that lands on the overridden `apply`, which returns only `output[0]`. `Generated.setup_context` then hands that single tensor to `_ChunkedLinearCE.setup_context`, where `_, lse, token_weight = output` tries to unpack the loss vector, raising `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`. `vmap(grad(...))` survives only because the intermediate vmap level intercepts the re-entry; plain `.backward()` survives because it never re-enters `apply`. The identical override and unpack exist in the Triton class (`linear_cross_entropy.py:1005-1008`, `:1061` `_, lse, saved_valids, token_weight = output`), so the CUDA path has the same break.
findings.failure_scenario: `opaque.auditing.gradient_scores` computes per-canary gradient norms with a bare `grad_fn = torch.func.grad(loss_fn)` called once per example (`packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/attacks/_gradient.py:144,159`). Any `loss_fn` that runs a patched HF causal LM with `loss_only=True`, or that calls `opaque.alignment`'s documented per-example `fused_nll_loss`, now raises ValueError instead of returning a gradient, so the gradient-based privacy audit cannot run at all against a model using the fused LM-head loss. Same for any user code following the `torch.func.grad` examples in `opaque.functional`.
evidence: Executed /tmp/.../work/t3_dbg.py: `grad(0)` and `grad((0,1))` over `linear_cross_entropy_chunked` FAIL with `ValueError too many values to unpack (expected 3)`; `vmap(grad(0))` and `vmap(grad((0,1)))` are OK.
Executed /tmp/.../work/t4_old.py against `git show a839782e^:.../_linear_ce_chunked.py`: PRE-#987 both `grad(0)` and `vmap(grad(0))` are OK - this is a regression introduced by the perf commit.

Executed /tmp/.../work/t11_baregrad_model.py: a real `LlamaForCausalLM` + `apply_runtime_patches()/apply_model_patches()` + `make_functional`, `grad(loss_fn)(params, ids[0:1], labels[0:1])` with `loss_only=True` -> `FAIL ... ValueError too many values to unpack (expected 3)`, while `vmap(grad(...))` is OK.
Executed /tmp/.../work/t12_align.py: `opaque.api.alignment.sft.loss._nll.fused_nll_loss` (documented 'per-example' helper) -> `grad` FAILS, `vmap(grad)` OK, on CPU through the chunked path.
Traceback terminates at packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/_linear_ce_chunked.py:330 inside torch/_functorch/autograd_function.py:146 `setup_context`.

packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels/test_linear_ce_chunked.py and test_linear_cross_entropy.py only exercise `vmap(grad(...))` and plain autograd; no test calls bare `grad`, which is why the regression landed.
findings.fix_sketch: Stop overriding `apply`. Return the tuple from `apply` and unpack at the (three) call sites, or make `setup_context` tolerant: `outputs = output if isinstance(output, tuple) else (output,)` is not enough because the aux tensors are genuinely missing at that level. The robust fix is to keep the Function single-output and pass `lse`/`valids`/`token_weight` to the backward through `ctx` fields computed in `forward` (they are all `mark_non_differentiable` anyway), or to wrap the tuple-returning Function in a plain Python function that does the `[0]`. Add a `grad(...)`-without-vmap test to both kernel test modules and to `opaque-auditing`.

findings.title: `_can_use_native_gqa`'s functorch guard never fires on the DP-SGD transform: `is_batchedtensor` is False under `vmap(grad(...))`
findings.claim: b9fb8674 (#985) added `if query.device.type != 'cuda' or torch._C._functorch.is_batchedtensor(query): return False` to keep the native `enable_gqa=True` SDPA (and its `torch.backends.cuda.SDPAParams` probe) away from functorch-wrapped tensors. Under `vmap(grad(f))` - the transform `clipped_grad`/`clipped_fun` actually uses - the tensor reaching the attention forward is a GradTrackingTensor wrapping a BatchedTensor, and `is_batchedtensor` inspects only the outermost wrapper, so it returns False. The repo already knows about this nesting: `_linear_ce_chunked._vmap_batch_factor` (lines 88-103) explicitly loops `is_gradtrackingtensor -> get_unwrapped -> is_batchedtensor`. The guard is masked on CPU by the `device.type != 'cuda'` clause, which is why no test catches it (`test_attention.py:192-201` only checks the positive CUDA case with plain tensors).
findings.failure_scenario: On CUDA, a DP-SGD step under `vmap(grad(...))` reaches `_can_use_native_gqa` with a GradTrackingTensor. The guard passes, `torch.backends.cuda.SDPAParams(query, key, value, ...)` is constructed from a functorch wrapper, and if `can_use_flash_attention` returns True the code calls `F.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., enable_gqa=True)` inside vmap - the exact path the guard was written to avoid. Best case the functorch batching fallback loops per sample (correct but slower than the `_grouped_sdpa` path that was written for it, defeating #985's purpose); worst case SDPAParams reads wrapper geometry and the eligibility decision is made on the wrong shapes/strides. Not reproducible here (no CUDA device), so only the guard's ineffectiveness is proven.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:124 - `if query.device.type != "cuda" or torch._C._functorch.is_batchedtensor(query): return False`.

Executed /tmp/.../work/t7_bt.py: under `vmap(lambda a: ...)` -> is_batched=True, is_gradtrack=False; under `vmap(grad(...))` -> **is_batched=False**, is_gradtrack=True; under `grad(...)` -> is_batched=False, is_gradtrack=True.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py:283 `grad_and_value(...)` wrapped by `_clipped_fun.py:595,682 _vmap(...)` - the DP path is vmap-outside-grad, so the inner tensors are grad-tracking wrappers.
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/_linear_ce_chunked.py:88-103 - the correct two-level unwrap idiom already present in the same package.
packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/components/test_attention.py:192-201 - the only eligibility test uses plain CUDA tensors; no test asserts the guard rejects a functorch-wrapped query.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the single-level check with the same unwrap loop used by `_vmap_batch_factor`, or simply test both predicates: `f = torch._C._functorch; if f.is_batchedtensor(query) or f.is_gradtrackingtensor(query): return False`. Add a CPU-runnable unit test that monkeypatches the device check and asserts `_can_use_native_gqa` returns False inside `vmap(grad(...))`.

findings.title: RMSNorm / fused-add-RMSNorm / RoPE backwards overwrite the upstream gradient buffer on a single backward, not only on a repeated one (wider than tracked #898)
findings.line: 557 (`dX = dY if in_place else torch.zeros_like(dY)`); fused_add_rms_norm.py:322; rope_embedding.py:237-238, 455-458; components/rms_norm.py:35,41 (`in_place_bwd=True`)
findings.claim: Tracked issue #898 ('Audit remaining fused kernels for repeated-backward gap') is scoped to *repeated* backward through fused activations, which #874 addressed by adding `ctx._opaque_backward_done` to SwiGLU/GeGLU/LoRA_MLP. The RMSNorm family and RoPE have a different and wider aliasing: their backward writes the input gradient directly into the *upstream* gradient tensor on the FIRST backward. `_rms_norm_backward_triton` does `dX = dY if in_place else torch.zeros_like(dY)` after `dY = dY.contiguous().view(-1, dim)` - `.contiguous()` is identity for an already-contiguous grad, so `dX` aliases the caller's tensor. The default Llama and Gemma RMSNorm component patches enable this (`components/rms_norm.py:35,41` pass `in_place_bwd=True`). `_RoPEBackward.forward` and `_RoPE_QK_Backward.forward` do the same with the comment 'In-place: overwrite grad_Q buffer (internal gradient, safe to mutate)'. #943, which removed the forward's Q/K clones, deliberately left the backward aliasing in place (it passes `dQ, dQ.stride(0), dQ, dQ.stride(0)` as both in and out pointers).
findings.failure_scenario: `torch.autograd.grad(y, x, grad_outputs=g)` (or `y.backward(gradient=g)`) where the RMSNorm/RoPE node is the first node the engine visits: the engine hands the caller's `g` to that backward unchanged, the Triton kernel overwrites it, and `g` is silently different afterwards. A caller that reuses `g` for a second `torch.autograd.grad` call, or that inspects it (e.g. an auditing or gradient-probe harness that keeps its seed vector), gets numbers derived from already-transformed data. Triton stores bypass the dispatcher so the version counter is not bumped and autograd raises nothing. Not executable here (Triton path is CUDA-only, `torch.cuda.is_available()` is False), so this is a static finding; the aliasing itself is unambiguous from the code.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/rms_norm.py:533 `dY = dY.contiguous().view(-1, dim)` and :557 `dX = dY if in_place else torch.zeros_like(dY)`.
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/fused_add_rms_norm.py:322 `dX = dY if in_place else torch.empty_like(dY)`.

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/rms_norm.py:35,41 - `in_place_bwd=True` for the default llama and gemma RMSNorm patches (only the 'lite'/gemma3 variants at :47,55,61 use False).

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/rope_embedding.py:236-238 `dQ = grad_Q.reshape(...).contiguous()` with the 'safe to mutate' comment, and :262-266 passing `dQ` as both input and output pointer; :455-458 the same for `dQ_out`/`dK_out`.
git show 26f6247b - #943 replaced `Q.clone()` with `torch.empty_like(Q)` in the forwards only; the backward launches still alias in and out.
Guarded classes per grep: only geglu.py:249/515, swiglu.py:251, lora.py:1120 carry `_opaque_backward_done`; rms_norm, fused_add_rms_norm, rope_embedding, moe have none.
findings.fix_sketch: Either document `in_place_bwd`/RoPE backward as taking ownership of the incoming grad and default the component patches to `in_place_bwd=False`, or allocate the output buffer when `torch.is_grad_enabled()` / when the incoming grad is not uniquely owned. Minimum: extend tracked issue #898's scope from 'repeated backward' to 'upstream-gradient aliasing on the first backward', and add a CUDA test that calls `torch.autograd.grad(y, x, grad_outputs=g)` and asserts `g` is unchanged (mirroring the `torch.testing.assert_close(Q_op, Q_before, rtol=0, atol=0)` forward checks #943 already added).

findings.title: Generic fused LoRA QKV wrapper applies RoPE on Cohere2's NoPE (full-attention) layers
findings.claim: Cohere2 alternates sliding-window layers (RoPE) with full-attention layers that are deliberately NoPE: transformers 5.15 modeling_cohere2.py:229 guards the rotary call with `if self.sliding_window is not None:`. The generic fused wrapper `_make_fused_qkv_attention_forward` applies `apply_rotary_pos_emb` unconditionally (qkv.py:131-133), so every 4th Cohere2 layer silently gets rotary embeddings that upstream never applies. Cohere2Attention is routed to this generic wrapper by `_resolve_fused_qkv_forward_factory` (qkv.py:44-45). Fusion is enabled by default (`apply_model_patches(..., peft=True)`), so a Cohere2 + LoRA DP fine-tune on CUDA trains a different model than the one it loaded, with no warning.

Layers 3, 7, 11, ... compute attention with RoPE-rotated Q/K although the architecture defines them as NoPE. Add a device-independent pipeline test in the style of `_install_reference_fused_qkv` (tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:126-139) that compares the generic wrapper against upstream `attn(...)` for a Cohere2 config with num_hidden_layers >= 4.

findings.title: Generic fused LoRA QKV wrapper drops sliding_window and softcap, silently disabling Mistral/Gemma2 windowed attention and Gemma2 logit softcapping
findings.claim: The generic wrapper calls `attention_interface(self, q, k, v, attention_mask, dropout=..., scaling=self.scaling, **kwargs)` and never forwards the family-specific arguments that upstream passes: `sliding_window` (Mistral, Qwen2, Gemma2, Cohere2) and `softcap=self.attn_logit_softcapping` (Gemma2). Opaque's own Mistral/Ministral/Gemma2 family patches install `apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch`, whose `vmap_create_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_causal_mask` deliberately returns `None` for a no-padding SDPA prefill and delegates the look-back limit to the attention implementation via the `sliding_window` kwarg (runtime/masking.py:110-144). Because the fused wrapper drops that kwarg, the window is applied by neither the mask nor the kernel: the model silently becomes full-causal. Gemma2's `vmap_eager_attention_forward_gemma2` / `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2` likewise default `softcap=None`, so `attn_logit_softcapping` is silently disabled. The dedicated Gemma3 and Qwen3 wrappers added in this delta *do* pass `sliding_window` (qkv_gemma3.py:83, qkv_qwen3.py:81) — the generic wrapper they were factored out of was never fixed.
findings.failure_scenario: Mistral-7B-v0.1 (config.sliding_window=4096), LoRA on q/k/v, `attn_implementation='sdpa'`, no padding mask, sequence length > 4096, `opaque.patches.apply_model_patches(model)` on CUDA. `create_sliding_window_causal_mask` returns None (compact path), the fused wrapper omits `sliding_window`, `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window` falls through to plain causal SDPA, and every query attends to the whole prefix. Training silently optimizes a different architecture. Separately, any Gemma2 + LoRA run loses attention-logit softcapping at all sequence lengths.

findings.fix_sketch: Make the generic wrapper forward the same arguments the family's own forward does. Better: replace name-set routing with a per-family wrapper table so that adding a family forces an explicit decision about its extra kwargs, and add a device-independent parity test per eligible family (the `_install_reference_fused_qkv` pattern already used for Gemma3).

findings.title: Fused QKV never got the fp32-adapter fallback that #977 added to the LoRA Linear and MLP paths
findings.claim: Commit 5b41925c 'fix(patches): preserve fused LoRA mixed-precision behavior (#977)' introduced `_active_adapters_use_dtype` / `_lora_projections_use_dtype` (components/_utils.py:20-37) and wired them into `linear.py:52-55` and `mlp.py:58-62`: when CUDA autocast is off and the active adapters are not already in the hidden-state dtype, the fused kernel is bypassed and PEFT's own forward runs so the adapter branch keeps its fp32 precision. `_opaque_fused_lora_qkv` in qkv.py has no such guard — it unconditionally does `hidden_states.to(_active_lora_dtype(hidden_states))` and `Opaque_LoRA_QKV.forward` then casts the fp32 adapters down via `cast_to_dtype(active_cuda_dtype(X), ...)` (kernels/lora.py:511-513). The result is an inconsistency inside one attention block: o_proj and the MLP honour the fp32 adapters, q/k/v do not.
findings.failure_scenario: The standard bf16-weights + fp32-adapters PEFT setup (`model.to(torch.bfloat16)` then `get_peft_model(...)`, which keeps lora_A/lora_B in fp32 by default) run without `torch.autocast`. o_proj falls back to PEFT and computes `base + fp32_delta` with a single rounding; q/k/v run fused and compute the whole adapter delta in bf16. Per-sample gradients on the DP path are then produced from a lower-precision forward for q/k/v only, and the model does not match the PEFT reference the tests in #977 were written to defend.
evidence: CURRENT TREE packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/components/linear.py:52-55 — `if not torch.is_autocast_enabled("cuda") and not _active_adapters_use_dtype(self, target_dtype): return original(self, x, *args, **kwargs)`; mlp.py:58-62 — same guard via `_lora_projections_use_dtype(self, ("gate_proj","up_proj","down_proj"), dtype)`.

CURRENT TREE qkv.py:55-65 — `dtype = _active_lora_dtype(hidden_states)` ... `hidden_states = hidden_states.to(dtype)` ... `return Opaque_LoRA_QKV.apply(...)` with no dtype guard. `grep -rn "_lora_projections_use_dtype\|_active_adapters_use_dtype" packages/` returns only _utils.py, mlp.py and linear.py.

RUN /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/qkvaudit/mixedprec.py (CPU, is_cuda forced, bf16 Llama + fp32 adapters, autocast OFF, LoRA on q/k/v/o): `base weight dtype: torch.bfloat16 | lora_A dtype: torch.float32`, `fused kernels actually invoked: ['Opaque_LoRA_QKV']` (Opaque_LoRA_W correctly declined), `max abs diff (bf16 logits): 0.00390625  ref scale: 0.54296875` vs the PEFT reference.

findings.fix_sketch: Add to `_opaque_fused_lora_qkv` the same early-out used by linear.py/mlp.py: `if not torch.is_autocast_enabled("cuda") and not _lora_projections_use_dtype(self, ("q_proj","k_proj","v_proj"), dtype): return self.q_proj(h), self.k_proj(h), self.v_proj(h)` — but note the fallback has to run *inside* the wrapper, so it is cleaner to move the check into `_auto_fuse_lora`'s runtime path or have the wrapper delegate to `original_forward` when the dtypes disagree. findings.title: Fused QKV validates its preconditions only at patch time and reads only active_adapters[0], so adapter switching silently drops dropout and extra adapters
findings.claim: `_auto_fuse_lora` evaluates `_no_lora_dropout` and `_bias_is_frozen` once, when the wrapper is installed, and then never again. At runtime `_extract_lora_params` reads `lora_linear.active_adapters[0]` only. The sibling `Opaque_LoRA_W` path in linear.py re-derives `dropout_is_noop` on every forward and falls back to PEFT when it is not a no-op (linear.py:37-46), and explicitly folds in `self.active_adapters[1:]` (linear.py:75-82). The fused QKV path does neither, so (a) after `set_adapter()` to an adapter with `lora_dropout>0` the fused Q/K/V projections silently skip dropout while o_proj and the MLP still apply it, and (b) with several active adapters the fused Q/K/V silently apply only the first while o_proj applies all of them.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) Patch a model whose 'clean' adapter has dropout 0, then `pm.add_adapter('noisy', LoraConfig(lora_dropout=0.9, ...)); pm.base_model.set_adapter('noisy'); pm.train()`. Q/K/V run deterministically with no regularization; the user believes dropout 0.9 is active. (b) Multi-adapter serving/training with `set_adapter(['a','b'])`: adapter b's contribution to Q/K/V is dropped entirely, and its q/k/v LoRA parameters receive zero gradient.
evidence: CURRENT TREE _router.py:78-97 — the gate block runs once inside `_auto_fuse_lora`, then `attn.forward = types.MethodType(fused_qkv_fwd, attn); attn._opaque_lora_qkv_patched = True`. components/_utils.py:50-58 — `if (lora_linear.disable_adapters or not lora_linear.active_adapters or lora_linear.active_adapters[0] not in lora_linear.lora_A): return W, None, None, 0.0` / `active = lora_linear.active_adapters[0]`.
Contrast components/linear.py:37-46 (`dropout_is_noop` recomputed per call, falls back to `original`) and linear.py:75-82 (`for adapter in self.active_adapters[1:]: ... result = result + lora_out`).

Gate behaviour at patch time is correct and was verified separately (/tmp/.../qkvaudit/gates.py): bias='all' -> fused=False, bias='lora_only' -> fused=False, lora_dropout=0.1 -> fused=False, partial target_modules -> fused=False.

findings.title: Fused QKV wrapper closes over a bound original_forward, so a deepcopy of a patched model routes the copy's fallback to the original model's attention
findings.claim: `fused_qkv_fwd = fused_forward_factory(attn.forward)` captures a *bound* method of that specific attention instance inside the wrapper's closure, and the wrapper is then installed as an instance attribute. `copy.deepcopy` rebinds the outer `types.MethodType` to the copy (via `_deepcopy_method`) but copies the wrapper function — and hence its closure cell holding the original bound `original_forward` — by reference. Every non-CUDA call on the copy (qkv.py:109-117, qkv_gemma3.py:110-117, qkv_qwen3.py:108-115) therefore executes the *original* model's attention, reading the original model's weights. On a CPU-only host the fallback is the only path, so a deepcopied model is entirely aliased through attention.
findings.failure_scenario: TR-DPO builds its reference model as `ref = ref_model if ref_model is not None else copy.deepcopy(model)` (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_dpo_trainer.py:729). On a CPU run (`args.device` == cpu, so `ref.to(self._precompute_device)` keeps it on CPU) the reference model's attention silently tracks the *policy* model's live LoRA weights, so the DPO reference logprobs move with the policy and the KL term collapses. The same aliasing hits any CPU evaluation copy or any EMA/averaged copy of a patched model.
evidence: CURRENT TREE _router.py:89-96 — `attn._opaque_fused_qkv = types.MethodType(_opaque_fused_lora_qkv, attn)` / `fused_qkv_fwd = fused_forward_factory(attn.forward)` / `attn.forward = types.MethodType(fused_qkv_fwd, attn)`. qkv.py:87-117 — the factory's `forward` closes over `original_forward` and calls it verbatim when `not hidden_states.is_cuda`.

RUN /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-opaque/2c6b9515-9455-539f-b005-ebecde2ecc66/scratchpad/qkvaudit/deepcopy.py (plain CPU, no is_cuda patch, so the fallback is live): `patched: True`, `clone forward __self__ is clone attn: True`, `captured original_forward bound to ORIGINAL attn?: [True]`, and after `attn.q_proj.lora_B['default'].weight.add_(5.0)` on the ORIGINAL model, `clone output changed after mutating ORIGINAL model: 0.6004`.

Reachable call site: packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_dpo_trainer.py:729 `ref = ref_model if ref_model is not None else copy.deepcopy(model)`; :685 and :732 `ref.to(self._precompute_device).eval()`; :405 `self._precompute_device = args.device`.
`_opaque_fused_qkv` itself is safe because `_opaque_fused_lora_qkv` is a module-level function, so deepcopy rebinds `__self__` correctly — only the captured `original_forward` is stale.
findings.fix_sketch: Capture the *unbound* function and re-bind at call time: `original_forward = type(attn).forward` in `_auto_fuse_lora`, and have the wrappers call `original_forward(self, hidden_states, ...)`. Add a `__deepcopy__`-safe smoke test: deepcopy a patched model, perturb the original's adapters, assert the copy's CPU output is unchanged.

findings.title: No fused-vs-unfused parity test exists for the generic QKV wrapper on any device; the Gemma3 device-independent pipeline pattern was not reused for Qwen3 or the generic path
findings.line: 26-51 (only CPU test is routing/fallback); 54 (@pytest.mark.cuda gates everything numeric)
findings.claim: The four delta commits each shipped tests, but the parity coverage is family-shaped rather than wrapper-shaped. Gemma3 got a genuine device-independent pipeline suite (`TestGemma3FusedWrapperPipeline`, tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:143-234) that stubs `_opaque_fused_qkv` with the unfused projections and compares the wrapper against upstream `attn(...)` on CPU. Qwen3 got no equivalent — `_fused_qkv_qwen3_attention_forward` is referenced by no test at all (verified by grep), and its numeric tests are inside the `@pytest.mark.cuda` class. The generic wrapper `_make_fused_qkv_attention_forward`, which serves five of the eight eligible families (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Gemma2, Granite, Cohere2, Qwen2, GLM4), is referenced by no test whatsoever, and every CUDA parity test uses Qwen2/Qwen3/Gemma3/GLM4 — the families where the generic wrapper happens to be faithful. The two silent-corruption defects above are exactly what that shape of coverage cannot see. (Distinct from tracked #880, which is about restoring CUDA markers for existing LoRA kernel tests, and from #968, which proposes packing more projections.)
findings.failure_scenario: Any future change to the generic wrapper, or any new family added to `_FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES`, ships with no test that would notice a dropped attention argument, a wrong rotary placement, or a missing q_norm — the failure mode already realized for Cohere2, Mistral and Gemma2.
evidence: `grep -rn "_make_fused_qkv_attention_forward|_fused_qkv_qwen3_attention_forward" packages/` — no hits under packages/*/tests; only src and .pyc.

packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/test_fused_lora_qkv.py:26 `def test_qwen3_qkv_fusion_routes_and_falls_back_on_cpu()` asserts only `hasattr(attn, "_opaque_fused_qkv")` and `torch.isfinite(model(input_ids).logits).all()`; line 54 `@pytest.mark.cuda class TestFusedLoRAQKV` contains every numeric test.
packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/test_glm4_lora.py:21 `pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(...)` + :43 `@pytest.mark.cuda` — the whole GLM4 file is CUDA-only.

packages/opaque-patches/tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:126-139 `_install_reference_fused_qkv` — the working pattern that would have caught the generic-wrapper defects if applied to Cohere2/Mistral/Gemma2.

The only Cohere2 fused test (test_fused_lora_parallel_residual.py) compares vmap vs eager of the *same fused* model and uses num_hidden_layers=1, so it is structurally unable to detect a wrapper-vs-upstream divergence.

Coverage of family routing itself was checked and is currently exact: a scan of all 478 importable `transformers.models.*.modeling_*` modules in transformers 5.15.1 found exactly the ten expected attention classes resolving through `_resolve_fused_qkv_forward_factory`; no look-alike family is mis-routed.
findings.fix_sketch: Parameterize the Gemma3 `_install_reference_fused_qkv` pipeline test over every entry in `_FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES` plus the two dedicated sets, building each family's tiny config with a sliding-window/softcap/NoPE-bearing layer count (>= 4 layers for Cohere2, seq_len > sliding_window for Mistral/Gemma2) and asserting `allclose(wrapper_out, attn(...))` on CPU. That is device-independent, cheap, and would have failed on all three defects.

findings.title: _auto_fuse_lora skips MLP fusion for any layer whose attention is already QKV-patched
findings.claim: The idempotency guard `if getattr(attn, "_opaque_lora_qkv_patched", False): continue` continues the *outer per-layer loop*, not just the QKV block, so on any second call to `apply_peft_model_patches` the MLP-fusion half of the loop body (lines 99-137) never runs for that layer. A layer whose MLP became eligible only after the first call therefore never gets fused.
findings.failure_scenario: `apply_model_patches(model)` runs during DPTrainer construction and fuses QKV (MLP not eligible yet, e.g. adapters added to gate/up/down afterwards); a later `apply_peft_model_patches(model)` short-circuits on the QKV flag and silently leaves every MLP unfused. Performance-only — results stay correct — but the intended optimization is silently absent with no log line.
evidence: CURRENT TREE packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/_router.py:68-72 — `attn = getattr(layer, "self_attn", None)` / `if attn is not None:` / `    if getattr(attn, "_opaque_lora_qkv_patched", False):` / `        continue`; the MLP block begins at line 99 inside the same `for layer in layers:` body.
`git log -L 60,75:.../peft/_router.py` shows the `continue` predates and survives both 41722a0b (#947) and 8ced13cf (#951), which rewrote the surrounding gate.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace `continue` with a guarded block, e.g. `if attn is not None and not getattr(attn, "_opaque_lora_qkv_patched", False): <qkv fusion>` so control falls through to the MLP section.

findings.title: poisson() now accepts whole-horizon and composed processes as its base, silently accounting a mechanism no Opaque sampler realizes
findings.claim: 3b22a6af (#850) replaced `_Inner = Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` with `_Inner = DpProcess` and replaced the factory's type match with `isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess)` (_poisson.py:21, :40-46). Any DpProcess is now accepted, including `DpHorizonProcess` subclasses whose PLD covers a complete fixed horizon (`KOutOfT`, `CyclicPoisson`, `BallsInBins`, `BMinSep`) and `Repeated`/`Composed` spines. Nothing at construction or PLD time distinguishes a per-step base from a whole-horizon base, yet the factory docstring still reads 'Returns a single-step process - compose externally with ``* num_steps`` for full-training privacy' (_poisson.py:185) and docs/reference/accounting.md:232 advertises the widening with no caveat ('Plain Poisson accepts any Opaque `DpProcess` as its base mechanism'). The resulting number is a valid bound only for 'draw ONE dataset-level Bernoulli(q) coin per record, then run the entire horizon on the survivors' - a mechanism no shipped Opaque sampler implements (PoissonSampler redraws per step; KOutOfTSampler has no dataset-level coin).
findings.failure_scenario: Executed at HEAD with a freshly built extension: `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.0), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'), 0.01).epsilon_at(1e-5)` is accepted and returns 0.009738873655638745 for the whole 100-step run. The same horizon unamplified reports 1.233938641105668 (127x higher) and the closest realizable per-step reading, `(dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.0), 0.01) * 100).epsilon_at(1e-5)`, is 0.7180658390624926 (74x higher). Before #850 the same call raised `TypeError: poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner mechanism, got KOutOfT` (git show 4b13d82a:.../amplification/_poisson.py, factory `match inner:` arm). A user who follows the documented 'single-step, compose externally' contract and reports 0.0097 (or 0.087 after `* 100`) for a run driven by KOutOfTSampler publishes an epsilon that no Opaque-realizable configuration attains.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:21 `_Inner = DpProcess`

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:40-46 `if not isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess): raise InputTypeError(...)` - the only inner-type check on the plain path
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:158-169 plain path calls `_native.poisson_pld(self.inner.pld(...), self.sample_rate)` for every inner type

docs/reference/accounting.md:232 'Plain Poisson accepts any Opaque `DpProcess` as its base mechanism.'

pre-#850 rejection: `git show 4b13d82a:packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py` ends with `match inner: case Gaussian() | AdaClip() | NonPrivate(): pass; case _: raise TypeError(...)`
no guard exists on the horizon side either: `dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t(...) * 2` also succeeds (returns 1.639800931306253), so neither side flags the category error
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the generalization but gate it: reject `DpHorizonProcess` instances in `Poisson.__post_init__` (they declare `n_steps` and are not per-step releases), and reject `Repeated`/`Composed` unless the caller opts in with an explicit flag naming the 'one dataset-level coin for the whole inner process' model. Document that model separately from the DP-SGD per-step reading, and say which sampler (none today) realizes it. At minimum, `_poisson.py` and docs/reference/accounting.md:232 must state that the base must be a single release drawn afresh under an independent per-step Poisson draw.

findings.title: Generic Poisson transform costs ~4 orders of magnitude of tightness against the external oracle, and the cross-validation tolerances were relaxed 60x-220x to absorb it
findings.claim: 3b22a6af (#850) deleted the analytic `poisson_gaussian_pld` and routed the Poisson-subsampled Gaussian through `poisson_pld` -> `poisson_from_gaussian` -> `disc_dist` -> `project_transformed_atoms` (poisson.rs:24, :45, :233), i.e. it discretizes the Gaussian loss first and then Connect-the-Dots-projects the transformed atoms, instead of evaluating the exact subsampled hockey-stick curve at each knot. The result is still a strict upper bound (verified, see evidence) but ~4 orders of magnitude looser against Google dp_accounting. The same commit relaxed the external-oracle tolerances from a single `ATOL = 1e-6` to `POISSON_EPSILON_ATOL = 6e-5`, `POISSON_ADVANTAGE_ATOL = 1.3e-5`, `POISSON_BETA_ATOL = 2.2e-4` (test_cross_validation.py:51-54) and retargeted the tight 1e-6 assertion onto goldens generated from opaque's own output (`_POISSON_EPSILON_GOLDENS`, asserted at ATOL on :265, :343). The truncated-Poisson sibling kept the analytic curve (truncated_poisson.rs:57-61 only falls back to `poisson_pld` when `p_trunc == 0.0`), so the two Poisson paths now differ in accuracy by four orders of magnitude. The module comment at test_cross_validation.py:55-57 still claims 'opaque and dp_accounting agree to ~1e-9 relative error'.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured by A/B on the test's own 34-point grid, using a fresh HEAD build of the extension and the pre-#850 .so still checked into packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.abi3.so (which still exports `poisson_gaussian_pld`): worst |new - dp_accounting| in epsilon_at(1e-5) = 5.33e-5 (sigma=0.5, q=1e-3, 1000 steps: new 3.2389339 vs old 3.2388806 vs google 3.2388806), whereas worst |old - dp_accounting| = 3.98e-9. Over a wider 108-point sweep the worst relative gap is 5.7e-4 (sigma=4, q=0.25, 5000 steps) and the minimum signed gap is +9.2e-8, i.e. always conservative. beta_at(0.1) moves by up to 2.1e-4 against riskcal and advantage by up to 1.2e-5, always in the conservative direction. Consequence: a future change that loses another 6e-5 of epsilon (or 2.2e-4 of beta) against the oracle now passes the cross-validation suite; the only remaining tight check is against opaque's own committed numbers, which are regenerated whenever they drift.
