findings.title: ParallelPoisson inner-mechanism guard added by #850 lives only in the factory, so direct construction and deserialization bypass it and fail later with a self-contradictory message
findings.claim: 3b22a6af (#850) widened `Poisson`'s inner type and compensated by adding a `match inner: case Gaussian() | AdaClip() | NonPrivate()` guard to the `parallel_poisson()` factory (_parallel_poisson.py:131-140). `ParallelPoisson.__post_init__` (:24-38) validates only `num_workers` and `truncated_batch_size`, so the guard is bypassed by direct construction and by `opaque.serialization.from_state_dict`. This contradicts the convention the very same file family documents: `Poisson.__post_init__` carries the comment 'Validate truncation pairing here (not only in the factory) so direct construction and deserialization can't pass an unpaired (truncated_batch_size, dataset_size) ... and fail at PLD time' (_poisson.py:68-72). The deferred error is also wrong: the `case _` arm reports 'ParallelPoisson requires a Poisson inner mechanism, got Poisson' (:93-98), naming the wrapper instead of the unsupported innermost mechanism.

findings.title: torch_compile=True aborts DP training on the first step for every supported dense HF causal-LM family: the now-default fused loss-only CE forward is not Dynamo-traceable under fullgraph=True
findings.claim: c0f95ced (#988) flipped `fused_linear_cross_entropy` from an explicit opt-in to `inherits from performance` (_factory.py:374-376, and DPTrainer always calls apply_model_patches(performance=True) at _dp_trainer.py:843-851), so the fused causal-LM forward wrapper is now installed on all 17 dense families in `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM`. The same commit made DPTrainer's *training* loss set the marker: `compute_per_example_loss` adds `loss_only=True` whenever `not return_logits and self._compute_loss_func is None and self._fused_forward_uses_marker` (_dp_trainer.py:2437-2442), which is exactly the training path. The wrapper's fused branch then executes `return_dict = return_dict if return_dict is not None else self.config.use_return_dict` (cross_entropy.py:257-259). In the pinned transformers 5.15.1, `PretrainedConfig.use_return_dict` is a deprecated property whose body is `logger.warning_once("`use_return_dict` is deprecated! ...")` (.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/transformers/configuration_utils.py:464-467). Meanwhile fae93a55 (#979) / afa0247f (#989) made the chunk compiler strict with no fallback: `_compile_strict_chunk` is `torch.compile(fn, backend=..., mode=..., fullgraph=True, dynamic=True)` (_dp_trainer.py:209-218) and `_grad_compiler` wraps it with nothing else (_dp_trainer.py:4366-4370). Dynamo refuses to trace the logger call under fullgraph, the exception propagates through `_microbatch_accumulate_reduced` -> `training_step` -> `_synchronize_grad_failure` (which only special-cases torch.OutOfMemoryError, _dp_trainer.py:1310-1318) and the run dies. A second, independent blocker sits behind it: the portable chunked kernel's tile planner calls the pybind builtin `torch._C._functorch.is_gradtrackingtensor` (_linear_ce_chunked.py:96, reached from `_tile_plan` at :120), which Dynamo also cannot trace.
findings.failure_scenario: `DPTrainer(model=LlamaForCausalLM(...), args=TrainingArguments(torch_compile=True, ...)).train()` raises `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: logging.Logger method not supported for non-export cases` on step 1 and never trains. Reproduced on this tree (CPU, torch 2.14.0, transformers 5.15.1) for LlamaForCausalLM and Qwen2ForCausalLM. A/B isolation: the identical run with `performance_kernels_config={'fused_linear_cross_entropy': False}` compiles and completes its steps, and Phi3ForCausalLM (not in `_FUSED_CE_CAUSAL_LM`, so `_fused_forward_uses_marker` is False) also compiles and completes. Neutralizing only the deprecated property then exposes the second blocker: `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: Attempted to call function marked as skipped ... is_gradtrackingtensor`. `torch_compile` is documented as supported in docs/reference/transformers.md:218 and docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:216. The existing compile tests cannot see this: packages/opaque-transformers/tests/opaque_transformers/test_compile_and_kernel_args.py builds `nn.Linear` / a hand-written `_TinyLM` (lines 46, 56-67), neither of which receives the family patch, and the engine-level test packages/opaque-engine/tests/clipping/test_compile_chunks.py compiles a pure tensor lambda.

findings.title: SFT loss-only DFT evaluation scores an unscaled-logit objective: `_fused_dft_loss_only` routes prediction_loss_only=True through `fused_dft_loss`, which ignores config logit scaling, so eval_loss measures a different objective than training on Cohere/Cohere2/Granite
findings.claim: 7edd41be (#929) added `self._fused_dft_loss_only = args.loss_type == 'dft' and self._lm_head_param_name is not None` (_sft_trainer.py:233-235) and widened the handle resolution to `_resolve_fused_handles(model, args.loss_type == 'dft')` (:230-232). The loss dispatch then became `elif self._fused_dft or (not return_logits and self._fused_dft_loss_only):` (:596), so a loss-only call takes the fused primitive even when `_fused_loss_eligible` is False. Because `SFTConfig.log_completion_metrics` defaults to True (_sft_config.py:90), `_fused_loss_eligible` and therefore `_fused_dft` are False at defaults - training keeps the eager `dft_loss(out.logits, labels)` path (:610-615) - while `prediction_step` asks for the no-logits closure whenever `prediction_loss_only` is set (:666-670), and `DPTrainer.evaluate()` sets `prediction_loss_only=True` whenever `compute_metrics is None` (_dp_trainer.py:3187). `fused_dft_loss` computes DFT against the raw projection `hidden @ lm_head_weight.T`: the fused branch calls `linear_nll_sum(...)` which hardcodes `logit_scale=1.0` (_fused_lce.py:113-114 and :120-122) and the eager fallback is `dft_loss(hidden_states @ lm_head_weight.transpose(-2,-1), labels)` (_dft.py:147). Neither applies `config.logit_scale` (Cohere/Cohere2, `logits = logits * self.logit_scale` in HF 5.15.1) nor `config.logits_scaling` (Granite, `logits = logits / self.config.logits_scaling`). This is the exact sibling the c0f95ced logit_scale work fixed for the model-level fused CE (cross_entropy.py:308-320, 336) and did not fix for the DFT primitive.
findings.failure_scenario: `SFTTrainer(model=CohereForCausalLM(...), args=SFTConfig(loss_type='dft', eval_strategy='steps', metric_for_best_model='eval_loss', load_best_model_at_end=True))`. Reproduced end to end on this tree: `trainer.evaluate()['eval_loss']` = 0.060834 while the training objective mean `dft_loss(model(...).logits, labels).mean()` = 0.064736 (6.0% off); Granite with logits_scaling=8.0 gives 0.063957 vs 0.064878 (1.4%). Per-batch: Cohere loss-only [0.059140, 0.062529] vs training/metrics-path [0.064630, 0.064842]; the metrics path (`prediction_loss_only=False`) matches training to 0.0, so the same checkpoint reports two different eval losses depending only on whether compute_metrics is configured - the exact inconsistency test_sft_dft_eval_loss_consistent_across_metric_modes was written to prevent, but that test only uses a tiny Llama (logit_scale absent) so it passes. Because the DFT weight is the detached softmax confidence, an unscaled temperature changes the per-token weighting, not just the value: with a synthetic logit_scale of 8 the gap is 633x. Sibling path (untouched by this commit, same root cause): with `log_completion_metrics=False` the same `fused_dft_loss` becomes the *training* objective (`_fused_dft` True), so a DP-SFT run on Cohere/Granite optimizes a differently-tempered DFT loss than the one documented in _dft.py, silently.

findings.title: The fused-CE wrapper's non-fused fallback branch recomputes logits without family logit scaling, silently changing the trained objective and the returned logits on the CUDA fp32 path
findings.claim: When a loss-only call is made but the fused kernel is declined, the wrapper falls through to `logits = self.lm_head(hidden_states[:, slice_indices, :]); loss = self.loss_function(logits, labels, self.vocab_size, **kwargs)` (cross_entropy.py:358-364). That branch reproduces stock Llama's tail and nothing else: it does not apply `config.logit_scale` (Cohere/Cohere2), `config.logits_scaling` (Granite) or `config.final_logit_softcapping`, all of which the wrapper *does* compute and pass into the kernels on the fused branch (:308-320, :336). The declining condition is `use_fused_ce = loss_only and _supported and ((hidden_states.is_cuda and hidden_states.dtype in (bf16, fp16)) or not hidden_states.is_cuda)` (:282-289): on CUDA with fp32 hidden states the whole expression is False, so the fallback runs. c0f95ced made this reachable for the plain DPTrainer at defaults, because it both installs the wrapper unconditionally (_factory.py:374-376) and makes the DP training loss set `loss_only=True` (_dp_trainer.py:2437-2442). Before that commit the wrapper was opt-in and DPTrainer never sent a marker, so only an explicit `fused_linear_cross_entropy=True` (or SFT chunked_nll) could reach this branch.

Every training step then computes the per-example loss - and its gradient - from unscaled logits, and `output.logits` handed back to eval / compute_metrics is likewise unscaled. Nothing warns. I could not execute the CUDA+fp32 gate in this CPU-only sandbox - that half of the reachability chain is read from :282-289 - but the branch's arithmetic defect is demonstrated directly.

findings.title: Adaptive clipping releases a {0,1} clipped-count query while AdaClip accounting prices it at the {-1/2,+1/2} sensitivity, under-pricing the quantile release 2x in mu (4x in variance)
findings.claim: The adaptive-clipping quantile release computes its statistic from a 0/1 clipping indicator: `_clipped_fun.py:362` `num_clipped = float((norms > effective_cn).sum().item())` and `:365` `clipping_rate=num_clipped / float(batch_size)`, then `_adaptive.py:121-122` `noise = torch.randn(1, generator=generator).item() * fraction_noise_std; return clipping_rate + noise`. Under add/remove adjacency one record moves the count by up to 1, so the per-record sensitivity of the released rate is ~1/|B|. The accountant instead assumes 1/2: `adaclip.rs:33` returns `(1.0/(z*z) + k/(4.0*sigma_b*sigma_b)).sqrt()` with `sigma_b = expected_batch_size * fraction_noise_std` (`_adaclip.py:78`), i.e. mu_b = 1/(2*sigma_b); the non-Gaussian branch does the same with `_native.gaussian_pld(2.0 * sigma_b, ...)` (`_adaclip.py:124`). The /4 (equivalently the 2x on sigma_b) is exactly the TF-Privacy / Andrew et al. convention that is only valid when the indicator is shifted to {-1/2,+1/2}; TF Privacy's quantile_estimator_query.py does `below = tf.cast(record <= params.current_estimate, tf.float32) - 0.5` with the comment 'the maximum that a single record could affect the count is 0.5', making 'the sensitivity of the below_estimate count query 0.5 instead of 1.0'. Opaque never applies that shift anywhere, so the accounted mu for the quantile stream is half the true value and the reported epsilon is too small. A second, smaller error compounds it: the runtime divides by the *realized* batch size (`_clipped_fun.py:365`, `_adaptive.py:107`), while the accountant divides by the constant `expected_batch_size`, so on a below-average Poisson draw the true per-record sensitivity is larger still.
findings.failure_scenario: DPTrainer with `clipping_mode='adaptive'` (wired at _dp_trainer.py:4476-4480 with `expected_batch_size=a.train_batch_size` and the default `fraction_noise_std=0.05`). Measured with the repo's own accountant (fresh target/release rust ext), delta=1e-5, plain-Poisson DP-SGD: nm=0.8, W=64, N=50000, K=4 groups, T=2000 -> reported eps=0.5791 while the correctly-priced release (sensitivity 1 instead of 1/2, obtained by halving sigma_b) gives eps=0.8467, a 46% understatement. nm=0.8, W=32, N=20000, K=8, T=1000 -> reported eps=1.3536 vs true 5.3562 (3.96x). Even the single-group default (nm=1.1, W=256, N=50000, K=1, T=1000) is understated: 0.7316 vs 0.7354. findings.title: Resuming a DDP run restores rank 0's sampler key on every rank, so all ranks draw the same local indices and Poisson/b-min-sep/BnB amplification loses its independent-inclusion hypothesis
findings.line: 5151-5197 (rank-0-only `_save_dp_runtime`), 5273-5294, 1870-1877 (restore on every rank), 3945-3949 (rank fold-in only on a fresh build); packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_poisson.py:229-266
findings.claim: On a fresh start the trainer folds the rank into the sampler key (`_dp_trainer.py:3945-3949`), which is what makes each shard's Bernoulli(q) mask independent. The sampler snapshot, however, carries its own absolute key (`_state_dict_poisson` stores `key_seed`, `_poisson.py:220-221`) and is written only by the saving rank: `_save_dp_runtime(staging_dir, ctx)` sits inside `if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp):` (`_dp_trainer.py:5151,5196`), and `should_save` returns `ddp.is_world_zero` by default (`_distributed.py:211-222`). On resume every rank runs `ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)` (`_dp_trainer.py:1875-1877`) and `_from_state_dict_poisson` rebuilds from the snapshot's seed (`_poisson.py:261`). All ranks therefore share one stream over shards that are the same length (the dataset is trimmed to a multiple of world_size, `_dp_trainer.py:3893-3908`), so they select *identical local index sets* for the rest of the run. The per-record marginal inclusion probability is still q, but the inclusions are no longer independent: the W records sharing a local position are always in or out together. The Poisson amplification theorem (and the b-min-sep and balls-in-bins analyses) require the target record's inclusion indicator to be independent of the rest of the batch - that is exactly what lets M(D') decompose as (1-q)P + qQ against the same P. With the indicators coupled, the reported epsilon is no longer a proven upper bound, and an adversary holding the other shards' same-index records can read the indicator off the release and recover the unamplified guarantee. The in-code comment at `_dp_trainer.py:3880-3886` acknowledges the collapse but asserts 'the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected', which is the part that is wrong - marginal preservation is not what the amplification proof uses. Every sampler family is affected, because all five serializers restore the saved absolute key: `_poisson.py:261`, `_k_out_of_t.py:218`, dpftrl `_poisson.py:304`, `_b_min_sep.py:259`, `_balls_in_bins.py:260`. For BandMF cyclic-Poisson and balls-in-bins it is worse than for plain Poisson, because the *partition / bin assignment* is also derived from the key, so after resume the ranks share a permanent co-participation structure rather than a per-step one.
findings.failure_scenario: Multi-GPU DP-SGD run (world_size W) that is checkpointed and resumed - the ordinary long-run workflow. After the resume point, at every step the global batch is the union over ranks of one shared local index set. An adversary who controls the dataset except the target record x (the standard DP threat model) places the W-1 records sharing x's local position on the other shards, all with clipped gradient C in one direction v, and zeros everywhere else. The v-component of the release is (W-1)C/normalize_by against noise nm*C/normalize_by, i.e. SNR (W-1)/nm - at W=8, nm=1.1 the inclusion indicator for x is recovered with error probability ~7e-4 per step. Conditioned on the (now-known) indicator, the test for x's presence is the *unamplified* Gaussian. Quantified with the repo's own accountant at nm=1.1, q=0.01, T=1000, delta=1e-5: the reported epsilon is 1.5154, while the mechanism that reveals the per-step indicator (K ~ Binomial(1000,0.01) plain Gaussian releases, delta(eps) = E_K[Phi(mu/2-eps/mu) - e^eps Phi(-mu/2-eps/mu)] with mu = sqrt(K)/nm) has epsilon = 20.4283 - a 13.5x understatement. Reproduced the mechanical collapse directly: two PoissonSampler instances built with rank-folded keys yield different batches on a fresh start, but after `from_state_dict` with rank 0's snapshot both restore the identical `_stream_key` and emit byte-identical index lists.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1875-1877 -> `ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)` runs unconditionally on every rank

Epsilon quantification (repo accountant + analytic Gaussian delta): reported (poisson(gaussian(1.1),0.01)*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.5154; indicator-revealed mixture over K~Bin(1000,0.01) = 20.4283

The July audit's clean-areas note (AUDIT-master-list.md:194) certified exactly this path - 'Rank-folded sampler keys keep draws independent without changing the marginal. No accounted-q vs actual-q drift' - which holds only for a fresh start, so the resume path has never been checked
findings.fix_sketch: Make the sampler stream key rank-derived at *restore* time rather than a stored absolute: either (a) persist only the rank-independent base key plus the cursor, and re-apply `fold_in(base, rank)` in `from_state_dict` (needs the sampler serializers to take the rank from the restoring process rather than the snapshot), or (b) write a per-rank sampler snapshot (`dp_state.rank{r}.pt`, alongside the per-rank RNG snapshot that `_save_rng_state` already writes on every rank at `_dp_trainer.py:5205-5210`) and have each rank restore its own. Until then, fail closed: refuse to restore a sampler snapshot when `world_size > 1` unless the snapshot records the rank it was written for and that rank matches, and correct the comment at `_dp_trainer.py:3880-3886`, which currently tells a reader the accounting is unaffected.

findings.title: Generalizing `dpsgd_acc.poisson()` to any DpProcess removed the inner-type guard, so an already-amplified whole-horizon process is silently re-subsampled and reports a smaller epsilon
findings.claim: Before commit 3b22a6af ('feat(accounting): generalize Poisson PLD amplification (#850)') the module declared `_Inner = Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` and `poisson()` rejected anything else with `InputTypeError`. It now declares `_Inner = DpProcess` (`:21`) and the only construction-time check is `if not isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess)` (`:40`). The underlying Rust transform is sound for an arbitrary dominating-pair realization, so no error is raised - but the *mechanism it prices* is 'apply the whole inner process to one Poisson subsample', which is not what a caller wrapping an already-amplified or already-composed process means. In the direction that matters, this is fail-open: subsampling an amplified whole-horizon DP-FTRL process reports a materially smaller epsilon than the correct accountant for the same run, where the previous version raised. Nothing rejects a `DpHorizonProcess` inner, and the `poisson()` docstring still says 'Returns a single-step process - compose externally with `* num_steps`', so the surface reads as if only per-step mechanisms are accepted.
findings.failure_scenario: A user with a BandMF DP-FTRL run reaches for the DP-SGD Poisson factory (the one the DP-SGD guide teaches) instead of `ftrl_acc.poisson`. With bands=8, nm=1.0, q=0.08, T=1000, delta=1e-5: the correct `ftrl_acc.poisson(ftrl_acc.mf_gaussian(nm, s), sample_rate=q, n_steps=T).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 6.2286, while `dpsgd_acc.poisson(<that same CyclicPoisson process>, q)` is accepted and reports 2.6974 - a 2.3x understatement with no warning. Nested subsampling is accepted too: `(dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01), 0.01) * 1000).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 0.0098 against the intended 1.5154 (155x). On the current build both constructions raise nothing; on the pre-#850 build both raised `InputTypeError`.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py:21 -> `_Inner = DpProcess`; :40-47 -> the only inner check is `isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess)`

`git show 3b22a6af -- .../_poisson.py` diff: `-_Inner = Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` / `+_Inner = DpProcess`; the `Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` guard survives only on the truncated branch (:88-95)

Reproduction (repo accountant, fresh rust ext): `ftrl_acc.poisson(mf_gaussian(1.0, band_mf_strategy(bands=8)), sample_rate=0.08, n_steps=1000).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 6.2286; `dpsgd_acc.poisson(<same process>, 0.08).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 2.6974 (accepted, no warning)
Reproduction: `(dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01), 0.01)*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 0.0098 vs `(dpsgd_acc.poisson(gaussian(1.1),0.01)*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5)` = 1.5154

packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_horizon.py:12-18 -> `DpHorizonProcess` is documented as 'a complete fixed-horizon process that cannot be accounted by prefixes', but is a bare marker with no operator-level enforcement
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the generalized transform but restore a semantic guard in `Poisson.__post_init__` (so direct construction and deserialization are covered, not just the factory): reject `DpHorizonProcess` inners outright - they already describe a complete amplified run - and reject inners that already contain an amplification node (Poisson / ParallelPoisson / KOutOfT / CyclicPoisson / BMinSep / BallsInBins) unless an explicit opt-in kwarg is passed. Add the same guard to `ParallelPoisson` and to `dpftrl_acc.poisson`. Cover it with a test asserting `dpsgd_acc.poisson(ftrl_acc.poisson(...), q)` raises.

findings.title: `paired_noise_stddevs` docstring prescribes a second-moment sensitivity `first * first` that is n times too small for the averaged release the library actually produces
findings.claim: The docstring tells a caller that the second-stream sensitivity is 'Typically obtained as ``first * first`` element-wise'. With averaged clipping `first = C / normalize_by = C/n`, so `first*first = C^2/n^2`. The quantity actually released on the second stream is `(sum_i g_i (*) g_i) / normalize_by`, whose per-record L2 bound is `||g (*) g||_2 / n <= ||g||^2 / n = C^2 / n` - n times larger. The shipped call sites are correct: `_clipped_fun.py:393` sets `squared_bound = (current * current) / normalize_by` = C^2/n and `resolve_paired_clipped` reads that off `ClippedPytree.max_norm`, so nothing in the library follows its own docstring. But the helper is a real entry point for monorepo callers (the module header lists `paired_noise_stddevs` as an exposed helper), and a caller who follows the recipe gets a joint Mahalanobis budget inflated by roughly n^2 while the accountant still reports `gaussian(nm)`.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor wiring a new paired first/second-moment mechanism follows the docstring and calls `paired_noise_stddevs(nm, first=C/n, second=(C/n)*(C/n))`. The second stream is then noised as if its per-record sensitivity were C^2/n^2 while it is C^2/n, so the joint release's true mu is ~n times the accounted 1/nm and the reported epsilon is far too small, with no runtime error and no test failure (the shipped paths never exercise the documented recipe).
evidence: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/noise_allocation.py:208-211 -> 'second: Second-stream per-record sensitivity Delta^2. Typically obtained as ``first * first`` element-wise'
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:391-394 -> `squared_bound = (current * current) / normalize_by` (C^2/n, not (C/n)^2)
packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/clipping/_adaptive.py:396-397 -> `_output_squared_bound` returns `(clipping_norm * clipping_norm) / normalize_by`, same convention

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_fun.py:466-472 -> docstring on `second_moment` states the correct rule: 'the second-stream sensitivity is the per-record squared bound ``C^2`` (averaged: ``C^2 / normalize_by``)'
findings.fix_sketch: Change the `second` parameter doc to 'the per-record squared bound divided by the same `normalize_by` as the first stream - `C**2 / normalize_by`, not `first * first`', mirroring the wording already used in `clipped_fun`'s `second_moment` doc, and add an assertion-style unit test that `resolve_paired_clipped` on a `second_moment=True` clipping output yields `second == first * normalize_by * first` so the relation stays pinned.

findings.title: Accounting privacy-metric queries have no argument-domain validation: epsilon_at(delta>1) silently returns 0.0 and delta_at(NaN) returns a plausible finite delta
findings.claim: The exception taxonomy commit 7b26f655 converted every *constructor* validation in opaque-accounting to ConfigurationError / PrivacyBudgetError / CalibrationError, but left the five privacy-metric *query* methods on DpProcess and Accountant with no argument validation at all, in Python or in Rust. `DpProcess.epsilon_at(delta)` accepts any float; `Pld::delta_at` (pld/mod.rs:270-272) is `metrics::delta(self, epsilon).clamp(0.0, 1.0)` with no domain guard, and the epsilon_at counterpart likewise. Out-of-domain arguments return numbers instead of raising. Measured on `da.poisson(da.gaussian(1.0), sample_rate=0.01) * 100` with the freshly built extension (target/release/libopaque_accounting.so at 12146ec4): epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.71807 (the true value), epsilon_at(2.0) = 0.0, epsilon_at(1e300) = 0.0, epsilon_at(inf) = 0.0, epsilon_at(nan) = nan, delta_at(nan) = 5.00000096e-16, delta_at(-inf) = 1.0, beta_at(2.0) = 0.0. The same library validates these exact domains on the *auditing* side -- packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/one_run/_stats.py:25 raises ConfigurationError('delta must be in [0, 1], got ...') and _gdp.py:173 raises ConfigurationError('alpha must be in [0, 1], got ...') -- so `est.epsilon_at(delta=2.0)` on a OneRunEstimate raises while `proc.epsilon_at(2.0)` on the process that actually reports the guarantee returns 0.0. `Accountant.beta_at` even documents the precondition it does not enforce: _accountant.py:183 'alpha: Type-I error rate (false positive). Must be in [0, 1].'
findings.failure_scenario: A user transposes the two dual queries or feeds a delta computed by arithmetic that went out of range -- e.g. writes `acct.epsilon_at(3.0)` meaning `acct.delta_at(3.0)`, or derives `delta = 1 - confidence` with a sign error. Opaque returns `0.0` with no exception, no warning and no log line, and the run is reported as epsilon = 0.0 (perfect privacy) for a mechanism whose true epsilon at a legitimate delta is 0.718. The NaN case is worse in the opposite direction: `delta_at(float('nan'))` returns 5.0e-16, a value indistinguishable from a real, excellent delta, so a NaN that propagated from upstream arithmetic is laundered into a publishable-looking privacy number. Reproduced end to end with uv run python against the current tree.

findings.title: DpProcess.risk_at / Accountant.risk_at let a Rust panic escape as pyo3 PanicException, which `except Exception` cannot catch
findings.claim: `Pld::risk_at` computes `let max_risk = prior.min(1.0 - prior); metrics::bayes_risk(self, prior).clamp(0.0, max_risk)`. For any `prior` outside [0, 1] (or NaN) `max_risk` is negative (or NaN), and Rust's `f64::clamp` panics when min > max or either is NaN. The panic unwinds through pyo3 as `pyo3_runtime.PanicException`, whose MRO is `(PanicException, BaseException, object)` -- it does NOT derive from `Exception`. Neither the Python wrapper (`_base.py:335-369`, which forwards `prior` untouched to `.risk_at(prior)`) nor the Rust function guards the domain. Reproduced against the 12146ec4 extension: `p.risk_at(1.5)` -> `pyo3_runtime.PanicException: min > max, or either was NaN. min = 0.0, max = -0.5`; same for prior = -0.5, inf, -inf, nan, 1e300. prior = 0.0, 0.5 and 1.0 return normally.
findings.failure_scenario: A dashboard or callback that logs privacy metrics defensively -- `try: log(acct.risk_at(prior)) except Exception: pass` -- does not catch a PanicException, so a single bad prior (read from a config file, or a prior expressed as a percentage such as 50 instead of 0.5) aborts the whole training process at an arbitrary point with a Rust backtrace rather than a handled configuration error. Verified: `try/except Exception` around `p.risk_at(1.5)` does not catch; only `except BaseException` does. This is the one metric in the family that crashes rather than returning a wrong number, which also makes it the only one whose misuse is not silently absorbed -- but it crashes in a way callers cannot defend against.

packages/opaque-accounting/src/python/pld.rs:135-136 -- `fn risk_at(&self, prior: f64) -> f64 { self.inner.risk_at(prior) }` (no guard, no PyResult)
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_base.py:369 -- `).risk_at(prior)` forwards unvalidated

findings.title: Serialization docs promise InputTypeError for an unregistered leaf; the code raises a bare TypeError, and the regression test cannot tell the difference
findings.line: 37-47 (_unrecognized_leaf returns TypeError), raised at 79 and 114; doc claim at docs/reference/serialization.md:17-20
findings.claim: Commit 7b26f655 rewrote docs/reference/serialization.md:19 from 'raises `TypeError`' to 'raises `InputTypeError` on both save and restore instead of being silently skipped', but did not convert the raise. `_unrecognized_leaf` still builds and returns a plain `TypeError` (_structural.py:37-47), raised on the save path at :79 and the restore path at :114. Because `InputTypeError` subclasses `TypeError` and not vice versa, `except InputTypeError:` -- the handler the documented taxonomy invites -- does not catch it, and neither does `except OpaqueError:`. Verified: `opaque.serialization.state_dict(object())` raises `TypeError: Cannot serialize builtins.object at the root: ...` and `isinstance(exc, opaque.exceptions.OpaqueError)` is False; same for `from_state_dict(object(), {})`. The sibling array-leaf contract on the same doc page *was* converted -- packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/serialization/_structural.py:38 imports CheckpointError and raises it at :51 and :69, matching docs/reference/serialization.md:41 -- so this is an incomplete conversion, not a deliberate carve-out. The existing test asserts `pytest.raises(TypeError, match="Cannot serialize")` (packages/opaque-base/tests/serialization/test_fail_closed_dispatch.py:64-71), which passes identically before and after the conversion, so nothing in CI holds the documented contract.
findings.failure_scenario: A team writes the checkpoint-resume guard the exceptions page recommends -- `try: state = from_state_dict(template, torch.load(path)) except CheckpointError: abort_resume() except InputTypeError: report_unregistered_type()` -- around a DP state tree that acquired a new unregistered leaf (a custom optimizer state object, a third-party schedule). The fail-closed TypeError sails past both handlers and surfaces as an unhandled crash at an arbitrary point in the resume path, or, in a harness that wraps resume in `except OpaqueError` to decide between 'resume' and 'start fresh', is not recognized as an Opaque failure at all. The failure is fail-closed either way (nothing is silently dropped), so this is a broken documented recipe rather than a privacy loss.
evidence: packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/serialization/_structural.py:37-47 -- `def _unrecognized_leaf(obj: Any, prefix: str, verb: str) -> TypeError: ... return TypeError(f"Cannot {verb} ...")`
packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/serialization/_structural.py:79 `raise _unrecognized_leaf(state, prefix, "serialize")` and :114 `raise _unrecognized_leaf(template, prefix, "restore")`

docs/reference/serialization.md:17-20 -- 'A leaf that is neither registered nor a generic container ... nor a primitive raises `InputTypeError` on both save and restore instead of being silently skipped.'
git show 7b26f655 -- docs/reference/serialization.md shows the sentence changed from `TypeError` to `InputTypeError` with no accompanying source change in packages/opaque-base/src

Contrast: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/serialization/_structural.py:38 `from opaque.exceptions import CheckpointError`, raised at :51 and :69 -- the array-leaf shape contract on the same doc page was converted
packages/opaque-base/tests/serialization/test_fail_closed_dispatch.py:64-71 asserts only `pytest.raises(TypeError, ...)`, which cannot distinguish TypeError from InputTypeError
Reproduced: `state_dict(object())` -> TypeError, `isinstance(e, opaque.exceptions.OpaqueError) == False`
The same module docstrings still say TypeError: packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/serialization/__init__.py:8 and _dispatch.py:7
findings.fix_sketch: Change `_unrecognized_leaf` to build `InputTypeError` (import from opaque.exceptions, which opaque-base already owns), update the two module docstrings, and tighten packages/opaque-base/tests/serialization/test_fail_closed_dispatch.py to `pytest.raises(InputTypeError, ...)` so the contract is held by CI rather than by prose.

findings.title: apply_runtime_patches / apply_model_patches swallow ImportError raised inside the patch application, and is_runtime_patched() reports True when nothing was installed
findings.line: 63-86 (model patches), 101-102 (flag set before any patch runs), 110-117 / 119-126 / 128-135 (per-concern swallows), 152-159 (is_runtime_patched docstring)
findings.claim: Every patch-install site in the public patches façade wraps the *call* as well as the import in `except ImportError`, and the runtime flag is set before any patch runs. (a) `apply_model_patches` lines 63-76 put `apply_transformers_model_patches(model, ...)` inside the same try as its import and swallow ImportError at logger.debug with the misleading text 'Hugging Face kernel patches not available'; lines 79-86 do the same for `apply_peft_model_patches` with a bare `pass` and no log at all. (b) `apply_runtime_patches` sets `_runtime_patches_applied = True` at line 102, before any of the four per-concern blocks, and each of those blocks (110-117 vmap_masking, 119-126 vmap_grouped_mm, 128-135 empty_batches) wraps its call in `except ImportError: pass` with no log. (c) `is_runtime_patched()` (152-159) returns that flag while its docstring says it 'lets a script that drives HF primitives without DPTrainer check whether the global shims are installed' -- it reports that the function was called, not that anything was installed. The correct pattern already exists one module away: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/torch/checkpoint/__init__.py:43-60 sets `_is_checkpoint_patched = True` only after the patches actually apply and returns early leaving it False otherwise. Commit 15b89a92 (#899) hardened exactly one sibling of this pattern -- an *unregistered* HF family now raises ConfigurationError from _router.py:135-143 -- but left the registered-family and import-failure paths fail-open. Two further silent skips sit under it: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/_family.py:200-203 and _factory.py:283-286 both do `try: mod = importlib.import_module(module_path) except ImportError: return`, dropping the vmap-safe eager_attention / repeat_kv / sdpa replacements with no signal, and _router.py:59-68 `_patch_forward` returns False silently when the named class is absent from the modeling module.
findings.failure_scenario: Demonstrated: registering a family whose apply_fn raises ImportError ('cannot import name eager_attention_forward from transformers.models.X.modeling_X') and calling `apply_model_patches(model, compat=True)` returns normally, logs only `DEBUG opaque: Hugging Face kernel patches not available.`, and leaves the model completely unpatched -- #899's ConfigurationError never fires because the family IS registered. Also demonstrated: `apply_runtime_patches(performance=False, compat=False)` installs nothing, yet `opaque.patches.is_runtime_patched()` returns True while the sibling `opaque.patches.torch.is_checkpoint_patched()` correctly returns False. The realistic trigger is version drift: opaque-patches pins `transformers>=5.0.0,<6` (packages/opaque-patches/pyproject.toml:32), a range across which HF routinely moves internal symbols. Under the currently pinned transformers 5.15.1 I verified by import that all 26 registered family modules still expose `eager_attention_forward`, `repeat_kv` and every class name listed in their `classes={...}` maps (0 missing), so today the defect is latent -- but on any 5.x where one symbol moved, DP-SGD training proceeds with the un-vmap-safe attention path and the only signal anywhere is a DEBUG line, with no public API able to detect it.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:63-76 -- the try block contains both `from ... import apply_transformers_model_patches` and the `apply_transformers_model_patches(model, ...)` call; `except ImportError: logger.debug("opaque: Hugging Face kernel patches not available.")`
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:79-86 -- same shape for PEFT, `except ImportError: pass` with no log

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:101-102 -- `global _runtime_patches_applied` / `_runtime_patches_applied = True` executed before the vmap_masking / vmap_grouped_mm / empty_batches / vmap_checkpointing blocks
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:152-159 -- is_runtime_patched docstring claims it checks 'whether the global shims are installed'

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/torch/checkpoint/__init__.py:43-60 -- the correct pattern: early `return` on `not vmap_checkpointing` leaving the flag False, `_is_checkpoint_patched = True` only after all applies succeed

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/_family.py:200-203 -- `try: mod = importlib.import_module(module_path) except ImportError: return` before the eager_attention / rope installs
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/_factory.py:283-286 -- identical silent `except ImportError: return`
packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/_router.py:59-68 -- `_patch_forward` returns False when `target_cls is None` (class absent from the modeling module), no log
Commit 15b89a92 (#899) added the fail-closed branch at _router.py:132-143 for family is None / apply_fn is None only
Reproduced: register_family('fakefam', fn_that_raises_ImportError) + apply_model_patches(PreTrainedModel) returns normally, only DEBUG logged, model unpatched
Reproduced: apply_runtime_patches(performance=False, compat=False) -> is_runtime_patched() True, is_checkpoint_patched() False
packages/opaque-patches/pyproject.toml:32 -- `transformers>=5.0.0,<6`
findings.fix_sketch: Narrow each try to the import statement alone so an ImportError from inside a patch propagates. In apply_runtime_patches, track which concerns actually installed and set the flag from that; have is_runtime_patched() report installed concerns (or add is_model_patched(model)) so the documented check is real. Replace the silent `except ImportError: return` in _family.py:200-203 and _factory.py:283-286 with a logger.warning naming the module that failed, and make _patch_forward log when a named class is missing from the modeling module -- a registered family that cannot find its own symbols is the same fail-open #899 closed for unregistered families.

findings.title: Stale 'bound' entry in the trainer mechanism-kwargs allowlist makes the error message advertise a kwarg that a second check rejects
findings.claim: 873de427 (delete(dpsgd)!: remove unsupported bounded Gaussian noise, #1021) removed the bounded-Gaussian mechanism and added an explicit rejection at _training_arguments.py:1222-1228: `if "bound" in self.privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs: raise ConfigurationError(... "privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['bound'] is unsupported: Opaque does not provide a matching privacy accountant.")`. b9b0a23e (fix(transformers)!: validate privacy kwargs, #1024), merged about an hour later the same day, introduced `_MECHANISM_KWARGS` at line 228 with `"gaussian": frozenset({"bound", "compute_dtype"})` -- carrying the removed knob forward into the allowlist. Allowed: ['bound', 'compute_dtype'].` The user reads that `bound` is a supported knob, sets it, and gets `ConfigurationError: privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['bound'] is unsupported`. findings.claim: `clipped_grad`, `auto_clipped_grad` and `per_group` are the *same objects* in both façades (verified: `opaque.dpsgd.clipping.clipped_grad is opaque.dpftrl.clipping.clipped_grad` is True), but their return types are exported asymmetrically. `opaque.dpsgd.clipping.types.__all__` omits ClippedGradAux, ClippedFunAux and ClipPytreeAux while exporting ClippingStats; `opaque.dpftrl.clipping.types.__all__` exports ClippedGradAux, ClippedFunAux and ClipPytreeAux while omitting ClippingStats. Both types are actually produced on both stacks: `opaque.dpsgd.clipped_grad(..., return_aux=True)` returns an `opaque.api.engine.clipping._clipped_grad.ClippedGradAux`, and `opaque.dpftrl.clipped_grad(..., return_stats=True)` returns an `opaque.api.engine.clipping._clipped_fun.ClippingStats`. docs/reference/clipping.md:32-33 documents ClippedGradAux and ClippedFunAux as public types on a page that renders `opaque.dpsgd.clipping.types` at line 89, which does not export them.

findings.title: min_sep=0 crashes past its own guard: ZeroDivisionError from the Toeplitz strategies, raw ValueError/OverflowError from the Rust-backed ones
findings.claim: `minsep_sensitivity_squared` and `minsep_sensitivity_upper_bound` both guard `if min_sep <= 0: raise ConfigurationError('min_sep must be positive')` (_toeplitz.py:495-496, 536-537), but the public strategy path reaches `minsep_true_max_participations` first: BandMfStrategy.sensitivity calls it at _band_mf.py:170-172, and that helper computes `max_part_ub = _ceil_div(n, min_sep)` = `-(n // -0)` (_sensitivity.py:64 and :45), so min_sep=0 dies with a bare ZeroDivisionError before any guard runs. The four strategies also disagree on the error type for the same bad input. Measured on n_steps=16: band_mf and blt give `ZeroDivisionError: integer division or modulo by zero` for min_sep=0 and ConfigurationError for min_sep=-3; bisr and lambda_cgd give raw `ValueError: Invalid parameter: min_sep must be >= 1` (from the Rust extension) for min_sep=0 and raw `OverflowError: can't convert negative int to unsigned` for min_sep=-3. Separately, `mf_gaussian_noise(..., min_sep=0)` and `min_sep=-5` construct successfully (its factory validates n_steps and noise_multiplier but not min_sep), deferring the failure to whenever the strategy's sensitivity is first needed.

Depending on which strategy they picked they get ZeroDivisionError, a bare ValueError, or -- for negative values -- an OverflowError about unsigned conversion; none is in the opaque.exceptions taxonomy, and none names the valid range from the call site the user actually used. All fail closed, so there is no privacy consequence.

findings.title: PEFT/LoRA resume silently restores no adapter weights: the model continues from fresh random init while the accountant, noise counter, sampler cursor and optimizer state are all restored
findings.claim: `_load_model_weights` restores a PEFT checkpoint with `self._model.load_state_dict(new_state, strict=not self._is_peft)`. PEFT's `save_pretrained` writes `adapter_model.safetensors` with the adapter name stripped from every key (`...lora_A.weight`), while the live module's `state_dict()` keys carry it (`...lora_A.default.weight`). With `strict=False` every saved key is 'unexpected' and every model key is 'missing', so the call is a complete no-op; the returned `_IncompatibleKeys` is discarded and nothing is logged. The resumed run therefore trains from the *freshly initialised* adapter while `dp_state.pt` (clip/noise/sampler state), `dp_optimizer.pt` and `accountant.json` are all restored faithfully. HuggingFace's own Trainer, whose parity DPTrainer claims, uses `model.load_adapter(resume_from_checkpoint, active_adapter, is_trainable=True)` for exactly this case (.venv transformers/trainer.py:3440, and :3502 for load_best_model_at_end).
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced end to end on the real trainer: tiny GPT-2 + LoRA(r=4, target_modules=['c_attn']), 4 steps, save_steps=2, resume from checkpoint-2. findings.title: DP-SGD resume keeps the checkpoint's Poisson sample_rate in the sampler but rebuilds the accountant from the new args, so a batch-size change on resume under-reports epsilon behind a log.warning
findings.claim: `_from_state_dict_poisson` deliberately takes `sample_rate` and `truncated_batch_size` from the snapshot and ignores the template, while `_build_mechanism` builds the accountant's `poisson(gaussian(nm), sample_rate=...)` from the *current* `TrainingArguments` (`ctx.sample_rate = train_batch_size / dataset_size`). `sample_rate` is tagged `drift="dp_relevant"` in `RuntimeCheckpoint`, but for `mechanism_kind == "gaussian"` (every DP-SGD run) `_warn_on_arg_drift` only logs a warning and continues. The result is that the sampler runs at the saved q while the accountant charges the new q. This is the exact defect OPQ-322 / closed issue #792 described for `RandomAllocationSampler.num_bins`; the fix (#1019, `fix(dpsgd)!: reject allocation-law drift on sampler restore`) added a `k`/`t`/`allocation` equality guard to `KOutOfTSampler` only. The sibling samplers still resolve the same class of parameter in favour of the snapshot: `PoissonSampler` (`sample_rate`, `truncated_batch_size`), `CyclicPoissonSampler` (`sample_rate`, `bands`, `partition_type`), `BMinSepSampler` (`bands`, `sampling_prob`), `BallsInBinsSampler` (`num_bins`), `SequentialBatchSampler` (`batch_size`). `truncated_batch_size` is not a `RuntimeCheckpoint` field at all, so drifting it produces no warning whatsoever.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced on the real trainer (dataset N=64, nm=1.0, delta=1e-5, 8 steps, save_steps=4). Phase 1 at per_device_train_batch_size=32 (q=0.5) realises batch sizes [32,25,29,31,36,26,41,36] and ends at epsilon=4.75151. Resuming checkpoint-4 with per_device_train_batch_size=8 (q=0.125) realises [36,26,41,36] for steps 5-8 — bit-identical to the q=0.5 continuous run, i.e. the sampler is still drawing at q=0.5 — and reports epsilon=3.25344. The resumed `accountant.json` contains four `"sample_rate": 0.125` Poisson nodes for the post-resume steps while `dp_state.pt`'s `sampler_state` records `sample_rate: 0.5`. Reported epsilon is 31.5 % below the epsilon of the mechanism that actually ran (true 4.75151 vs reported 3.25344). The only diagnostics are three `log.warning` lines ('Resume arg drift on sample_rate (dp_relevant, DP-SGD): saved=0.5, current=0.125', plus expected_steps_per_epoch and expected_batch_size), none of which says which value won.

findings.title: MF noise state carries no derivation-version or execution-identity tag except for BISR, so the #1018 lambda-CGD stream change and any strategy-hyperparameter drift restore silently onto a different mechanism
findings.claim: `MFNoiseState`'s wire format records only `layout_version`, `_step_counter`, `_rng_key`, the max-norm latch and the inner-state field *names*. It records neither the strategy hyperparameters (bands, max_buffers, momentum, alpha/beta, lambda_, normalized), the horizon (`n_steps`, `min_sep`, `max_participations`), the compute dtype, nor a version of the noise-derivation law. `d09d7b9a fix(dpftrl): bound BISR noise state by bandwidth (#886)` gave BISR exactly such an execution identity (`_BisrExecutionIdentity(version, inverse_coefficients, normalized, n_steps, compute_dtype)`, `_bisr.py:43-51, 96-119`) and BISR consequently fails closed on all of these. No sibling strategy got one. `f2d90d61 fix(random)!: namespace lambda-CGD noise stream (#1018)` then changed lambda-CGD's per-step key derivation from `fold_in(key, step)` to `_mf_gaussian_column_key(key, step)` without bumping `_LAYOUT_VERSION` (still 1) or `DP_STATE_BUNDLE_VERSION` (still 7 at that commit). The trainer path is currently protected only by coincidence: an unrelated commit two hours later, `873de427 delete(dpsgd)!: remove unsupported bounded Gaussian noise (#1021)`, bumped the bundle to 8, and all four released tags in the delta (v0.15.4, v0.15.5.rc1, v0.15.5.rc2, v0.15.6.rc1) write 7. Because C^-1 for lambda-CGD is 2-banded, the correlation term at the resume step multiplies a z_{s-1} drawn from the new stream that was never released at step s-1, so the realised operator is not the lambda-CGD strategy matrix the accountant priced. The same silence covers config drift on every non-BISR strategy: restoring a band_mf state into a template built with `n_steps` 8->16 is ACCEPTED and emits different noise (-0.76381 -> -0.70943); `momentum` 1.0->0.5 ACCEPTED (-0.76381 -> -1.01377); bsr `alpha` 0.9->0.7 ACCEPTED (-1.10275 -> -1.03146); lambda_cgd `lambda_` 0.5->0.9 ACCEPTED (-1.27672 -> -1.77366). findings.title: DDP resume installs rank 0's sampler snapshot on every rank, silently re-correlating the per-rank Poisson masks that the per-rank key fold exists to keep independent
findings.line: 3879-3885 (the acknowledging comment, 'written once on rank 0' at :3881), 3944-3949 (per-rank fold), 5036 + 5197 (rank-0-only `_save_dp_runtime`), 1861-1877 (unconditional restore on every rank, `from_state_dict` at :1875)
findings.claim: For `world_size > 1` the trainer folds the rank into the sampler key so each shard draws an independent Bernoulli(q) mask. The sampler snapshot inside `dp_state.pt` stores the concrete stream key (`key_seed`/`key_impl`) and is written only on the saving rank (`if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp):` at :5036), while `_inner_training_loop` restores it on every rank (`ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)` at :1875-1877, with no rank branch). After a resume every rank therefore samples the same local positions. The in-code comment at :3879-3885 acknowledges this and justifies deferring it with 'the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected'. That justification is not sufficient: Poisson amplification requires a record's inclusion indicator to be independent of the rest of the sample, not merely Bernoulli(q) marginally. Under a shared mask the records sharing a local index across the `world_size` shards are included or excluded together, so conditioning on the rest of the batch can reveal the target record's inclusion bit, which is precisely what the amplification hides. No warning is emitted at resume time, and no test covers it (the `distributed` marker lane has no sampler-snapshot case).
findings.failure_scenario: world_size=4, per-rank shard length L, q=0.25. Phase 1: rank r uses key fold_in(seed, r), so the four shards' masks are independent and the global sample is an i.i.d. Poisson sample — the model the `poisson(gaussian(nm), q)` accountant prices. Resume from any checkpoint: all four ranks restore rank 0's `key_seed`, so the record at local index i is now included on all four shards simultaneously. For a neighbouring pair differing in one record x at local index i0, the three co-indexed records on the other shards are included exactly when x is; when their clipped gradients are large relative to sigma = nm*C the aggregate reveals the shared inclusion bit, and conditioned on it the released pair is the *unamplified* Gaussian rather than the q-subsampled one. The accountant continues to charge the amplified per-step PLD for every post-resume step, so the reported epsilon is an underestimate whose size grows with world_size and with 1/nm. I did not run a two-rank Gloo reproduction (the behaviour is asserted by the code comment itself and follows directly from the rank-0-only save plus the unconditional restore), so the magnitude is reasoned, not measured.

findings.claim:

findings.title: A GPU runner with <24 GB silently skips the entire Triton kernel suite (397 tests, 225 CUDA-selected) and the CUDA lane still reports green
findings.claim: `pytest_collection_modifyitems` in the kernels conftest reads `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory` and, when it is below MIN_KERNEL_CUDA_MEM_GB = 24, attaches `pytest.mark.skip` to EVERY collected item whose path is under the kernels directory - not just the stress/perf tests its reason string names. That directory holds the numerical correctness suite for every fused kernel (RMSNorm, SwiGLU, GeGLU, RoPE, cross-entropy, linear-CE, LoRA, MoE, autocast, vmap-grad parity). pytest then exits 0 with everything skipped, `run_python_test_package.sh` records the path as a success (the exit-5 branch is not reached), and the lane is green. The CUDA preflight added by 039fc012 (#876) to close OPQ-377 asserts only that a CUDA device exists and can do arithmetic - it does not check memory - so it cannot distinguish this case from a real run.
findings.failure_scenario: The self-hosted GPU runner is re-provisioned onto a smaller card (a 16 GB A4000/T4/L4 is the common case) or the label GPU-runner-001 is repointed. All three CUDA lanes on pr.yml and all three on ci.yml then run `-m 'cuda and not slow'` / `-m cuda`, collect 225 kernel tests, skip 100% of them at collection, and pass. publish-dev-wheels (ci.yml:199-213) needs exactly those jobs, so main keeps publishing wheels whose Triton kernels - the code path the DP-SGD vmap(grad) pipeline runs on GPU - has had zero validation. The lane passes `-rs`, so the skips appear in the log, but nothing fails on them.

findings.title: OPQ-386 was closed (#841) without a change: Python 3.12 still executes zero tests while all ten wheels advertise it
findings.claim: OPQ-386 asked for either one cheap 3.12 leg or dropping the classifier claim. Neither happened. `grep -rn '3\.12' .github/` over the current tree returns nothing at all; validate-distributions.yml still matrixes `python-version: ['3.11', '3.13']`, python-tests.yml's input still defaults to 3.11, and the dependency-boundary lanes are pinned to 3.11 and 3.13. Meanwhile every one of the ten package pyprojects still carries `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12` and `requires-python = '>=3.11,<3.14'`, and there is no documented endpoints-only policy anywhere in CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md or docs/ (the only 3.12 mention outside pyproject classifiers is AGENTS.md:326, which notes 3.12 is the Cursor VM's default interpreter).
findings.failure_scenario: A 3.12-only regression - an interpreter-specific behaviour in the torch.func vmap/pytree layer, or a dependency resolving to a different wheel on 3.12 - ships in a release whose metadata explicitly advertises 3.12, with no CI signal that ever existed. Bounded: 3.11 and 3.13 bracket most such behaviour, and nothing here changes a privacy guarantee. The specific irony is that AGENTS.md tells agents the development VM runs 3.12, so the interpreter contributors use locally is the one CI never exercises.

findings.title: A shipped feature's only integration regression tests are gated behind a capability probe that turns the feature's removal into a silent skip
findings.claim: `TestPerGroupAutoSxMf` (2 test methods x 6 strategies = 12 tests, the only integration coverage of AUTO-S clipping composed with per-group MF noise) is guarded by an autouse fixture that calls `_per_group_supported_by_mf_noise()`, which invokes `mf_gaussian_noise` with a PerGroup bound and returns False if it raises a TypeError mentioning 'PerGroup'. findings.title: Published LLM fine-tuning tutorial reports epsilon 1.09 for an adaptively-clipped run whose true cost is 8.99 — the adaptive-clipping quantile release is never accounted
findings.line: cell 11 (nb JSON lines 420-429, `expected_eps = ...`) and cell 13 (`dp_step = ...`); published output at nb JSON line 377
findings.claim: The flagship 'Fine-tuning an LLM' tutorial trains with `adaptive_clipped_grad(..., target_quantile=0.80, ...)` (default `fraction_noise_std=0.05`, i.e. a noisy clip-rate query released every step) but prices the run with `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(NOISE_MULTIPLIER), sample_rate, truncated_batch_size=MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dataset_size=len(train_dataset)) * NUM_STEPS` — the plain Gaussian chain, with no `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(...)` wrapper. The string `adaclip` does not appear anywhere in the notebook (`grep -c adaclip docs/tutorials/llm_finetuning.ipynb` -> 0). Opaque's own user guide mandates the opposite: docs/user-guide/clipping.md:230-249, 'Adaptive clipping introduces an additional privacy cost (the noisy clipping rate query). Account for it using `dpsgd_acc.adaclip()`', and examples/train_dpsgd.py:1553 does exactly that. The notebook therefore publishes a privacy number that omits NUM_STEPS noisy-quantile releases.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader follows the tutorial (the only published LLM example, linked from docs/tutorials/README.md:18 and mkdocs.yml:140), adopts its accounting line for their own adaptive-clipping run, and reports an epsilon roughly 8x below the guarantee their mechanism actually provides. Measured at the notebook's own constants (nm=1.5, q=8/500, truncated_batch_size=12, dataset_size=500, 20 steps, delta=1e-5): the notebook's chain gives epsilon=1.0944 (matching its published 'Expected final epsilon: 1.09'); the same chain with `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.5), fraction_noise_std=0.05, expected_batch_size=8)` as inner gives epsilon=8.9928 — an 8.2x understatement. The notebook is not in the CI execution list, and executing it would not catch this anyway: the wrong formula runs without error.

findings.title: API reference defines `dpftrl_acc.poisson`'s `sample_rate` as the whole-dataset per-round probability; the implementation requires the per-active-band conditional rate (up to 100x optimistic epsilon)
findings.line: 468 (`- \`sample_rate\` (float): Poisson sampling probability per round.`); same omission in docs/user-guide/accounting.md:327-340 and 495-512, docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md:73-80 and 103-112, docs/index.md:84-89
findings.claim: `dpftrl_acc.poisson(inner, sample_rate, *, n_steps)` treats `sample_rate` as the inclusion probability *conditional on the active band*, not as the whole-dataset rate. The implementation says so only in a module docstring (packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:50-54, 'BandMF requires cyclic sampling over fixed dataset partitions; `sample_rate` is conditional on the active partition'), and the trainer converts explicitly (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:154, `group_rate = float(sample_rate) * local_size / group_size`, i.e. roughly q_global * bands). The API reference bullet says the opposite in plain global terms, and neither docs/user-guide/accounting.md nor docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md nor docs/index.md mentions the conversion anywhere. The only correct statement in the docs tree is a Tips bullet at the bottom of a different page, docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/band-mf.md:321-325.
findings.failure_scenario: A user computes `sample_rate = expected_batch_size / dataset_size` — the convention used by every DP-SGD example on the very same pages, and the exact quantity DPTrainer takes — sizes `CyclicPoissonSampler(sample_rate=q_cond, bands=B)` so the realized batch matches, and passes the global q to `dpftrl_acc.poisson`. Nothing raises (q_global < q_cond is always in range), and the reported epsilon is far below the truth. Measured on the configuration published at docs/user-guide/accounting.md:506-510 (band_mf_strategy(bands=64), n_steps=15_624, nm=1.0, delta=1e-5): sample_rate=0.01 gives epsilon=0.9857, while the conditional rate that actually realizes a 1%-of-dataset batch (0.64) gives epsilon=102.1295 — a 104x understatement. At the bands=10 / n_steps=1000 configuration on docs/index.md and docs/reference/accounting.md, 0.7181 vs 7.0469 (9.8x).
evidence: docs/reference/accounting.md:468: `- \`sample_rate\` (float): Poisson sampling probability per round.`

findings.title: Sampling reference states CyclicPoissonSampler has no batch-size cap and that `dpftrl_acc.poisson` matches uncapped draws only — both are false, and the cap silently applies for bands>1 where no accountant supports it
findings.claim: The page asserts 'There is no batch-size cap on this sampler; `dpftrl_acc.poisson` matches uncapped Poisson draws only.' Both halves are false at HEAD. `CyclicPoissonSampler.__init__` accepts `truncated_batch_size: int | None = None` and applies it, and `dpftrl_acc.poisson` accepts `truncated_batch_size` and `dataset_size`. The parameter table at docs/reference/sampling.md:184-190 and docs/user-guide/sampling.md:164-172 both omit the parameter, while the mkdocstrings block on the very same reference page (`::: opaque.dpftrl.sampling.CyclicPoissonSampler`, docs/reference/sampling.md:258) renders the class docstring, which documents the cap ('truncated_batch_size: Optional cap on per-step batch size ... Only the ``bands == 1`` / ``IdentityMf`` combination is supported in :func:`opaque.dpftrl.accounting.poisson`'). The rendered page therefore contradicts itself.
findings.failure_scenario: Library users (the trainer path is fail-closed) can construct `CyclicPoissonSampler(ds, sample_rate=0.5, bands=4, n_steps=20, truncated_batch_size=60, key=...)`; verified, every batch comes back at exactly 60 where the uncapped sampler yields 112-136. `dpftrl_acc.poisson` rejects truncated arguments for BandMfStrategy (ConfigurationError, 'truncated Poisson is only supported for IdentityStrategy inner'), so the user's only option is to account with the plain-Poisson PLD — which is optimistic for a capped sampler. In the DP-SGD analogue on the same docs (docs/user-guide/sampling.md:487) truncation is priced at roughly 2.4x plain Poisson (measured 9.2359 vs 3.8333 at nm=1.1, q=0.032, 500 steps), so the understatement is large. A reader who trusts the reference sentence also never learns that `dpftrl_acc.poisson(..., truncated_batch_size=, dataset_size=)` exists for identity MF.
evidence: docs/reference/sampling.md:194-196: 'account with `dpftrl_acc.poisson(mechanism, sample_rate, n_steps=...)`. There is no batch-size cap on this sampler; `dpftrl_acc.poisson` matches uncapped Poisson draws only.'
`inspect.signature(CyclicPoissonSampler.__init__)` -> `(self, data_source, sample_rate, bands=1, n_steps=1, partition_type=PartitionType.EQUAL_SPLIT, truncated_batch_size: int | None = None, *, key)`
`inspect.signature(opaque.dpftrl.accounting.poisson)` -> `(inner, sample_rate, *, n_steps, truncated_batch_size: int | None = None, dataset_size: int | None = None)`

Executed: `CyclicPoissonSampler(ds, sample_rate=0.5, bands=4, n_steps=20, truncated_batch_size=60, key=key(0))` -> all 20 batch sizes == 60; same sampler without the cap -> [112, 120, 121, 133, 136, ...]

packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/sampling/_poisson.py:15-18 and 68-73 document the cap; packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpftrl/amplification/_poisson.py:120-130 rejects it for BandMfStrategy
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dpftrl.py:229-236 rejects the combination in the trainer, so the exposure is the direct library surface only
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the two sentences with the true statement: the sampler accepts `truncated_batch_size`, and it may only be used with `bands == 1` / IdentityStrategy, where `dpftrl_acc.poisson(..., truncated_batch_size=, dataset_size=)` supplies the matching truncated-Poisson PLD; add the parameter to both tables. findings.title: Privacy-auditing tutorial prices a shuffled fixed-batch DataLoader with Poisson amplification and under-counts its own steps — the exact OPQ-355 defect, surviving in the sibling notebook the sweep did not touch
findings.line: cell 9 (nb JSON line 271, `train_loader = DataLoader(train_data, batch_size=batch_size, shuffle=True)`) and cell 13 (nb JSON lines 372-373)
findings.claim: OPQ-355 ('the Quick Start and the DP-SGD tutorial publish a Poisson-amplified epsilon for a `torch.randperm` shuffled fixed-batch loop, and both under-count steps') was closed as part of sweep #843. It is fixed in docs/getting-started/quickstart.md (now an include of the runnable examples/quickstart.py, which uses PoissonSampler) and in docs/tutorials/dp_sgd_training.ipynb (cell 13 now iterates a PoissonSampler and composes step-exactly). The identical pattern survives untouched in docs/tutorials/privacy_auditing.ipynb, which trains with a shuffled fixed-batch `DataLoader` and then computes its 'Theoretical epsilon' with `sample_rate = batch_size / len(train_data)` and `total_steps = n_epochs * (len(train_data) // batch_size)` fed into `dpsgd_acc.poisson(...)`. Shuffled fixed-size batching is not Poisson subsampling, and the floor division under-counts the batches the loader actually yields (`drop_last` defaults to False).
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced with the notebook's own constants (n_samples=500, batch_size=64, n_epochs=200, nm=0.5, delta=1e-5): `cf.train_subset` yields 252 rows at HEAD, so the loader yields 4 batches/epoch = 800 steps, while the notebook computes `200 * (252 // 64) = 600`. Poisson-amplified epsilon at the documented 600 steps is 250.89; at the 800 steps actually run, 314.46; and with no amplification at all (the honest model for a deterministic shuffled partition in which each record participates once per epoch, 200 participations) 519.70. The published number the reader sees is the smallest of the three. The notebook then prints 'OK: audited epsilon is within the theoretical bound', teaching that this is the way to compute the bound an audit is checked against. It is not executed by CI.

findings.title: "Documented privacy examples execute in CI" is a partial check: zero of 369 markdown snippets run, 4 of 7 tutorials are never executed, and no executed notebook's published output is ever compared to a fresh run
findings.claim: HEAD (12146ec4, 'docs(accounting): execute documented privacy examples (#1034)') added one CI step. What it actually covers: `examples/quickstart.py`; `python -m doctest packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/accounting/__init__.py`; and `jupyter execute` on copies of 3 of the 7 tutorial notebooks. What it does not cover: (a) the 369 fenced ```python blocks across 46 docs/*.md pages — nothing executes them (`grep -n doctest pyproject.toml conftest.py` finds nothing, there is no doctest-glob, no markdown plugin); (b) distributed_training.ipynb, llm_finetuning.ipynb, privacy_auditing.ipynb and sampling_and_microbatching.ipynb, all four in the mkdocs nav (mkdocs.yml:139-145), three of which carry stored outputs that are published verbatim; (c) the other 7 `examples/*.py`; (d) any numeric assertion in the doctest — running it with `-v` shows '4 tests in 1 items, 4 passed', and all four are bare statements with no expected output, so it is an import smoke test. findings.title: Paired second-moment accounting is documented as unconditionally equal to the first-moment mechanism; the equality only holds when the second-moment strategy's participation blow-up does not exceed the first's, which is neither documented nor enforced
findings.line: 336-338 ('privacy accounting is exactly the underlying first-moment mechanism'); same claim at docs/reference/noise.md:85-90; docs/limitations.md:8-9 repeats the benign framing
findings.claim: The Mahalanobis allocation argument the docs give is correct as far as it goes: `paired_noise_stddevs` sets sigma^i_g = nm*sqrt(Delta^i_g * S) with S = sum(Delta^1 + Delta^2), and sum_{g,i} (Delta^i_g/sigma^i_g)^2 = 1/nm^2 exactly (verified numerically to 1e-16 for scalar and PerGroup). But for DP-FTRL the runtime sizes both streams from SINGLE-participation column norms — packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_second_moment.py:140-145 computes `c1` and `c2` with `min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1` — while the accountant prices the first stream at the actual multi-participation sensitivity. Writing rho_i = sens_multi_i / sens_single_i, the joint Mahalanobis sensitivity equals the accounted one iff rho_2 <= rho_1; when rho_2 > rho_1 the realized release exceeds the accounted budget by sqrt((D1*rho_1^2 + D2*rho_2^2)/(rho_1^2*(D1+D2))). Nothing enforces rho_2 <= rho_1: `mf_gaussian_noise(..., second_moment_strategy=...)` accepts an arbitrary, different-family strategy. This is the delta on open issue #359 ('Define BandMF participation sensitivity and price second moments', blocked/needs-design): the docs assert as settled exactly what that issue tracks as unresolved, and give a BandMF code sample for it.
findings.failure_scenario: A user follows docs/mechanisms/dp-ftrl/lambda-cgd.md:71 ('auto-deriving the second-moment strategy is not supported for lambdaCGD. Pass `second_moment_strategy` explicitly') and passes a second-moment strategy whose multi-participation blow-up is larger than the first stream's. Verified accepted with no warning: `mf_gaussian_noise(params, band_mf_strategy(bands=10), second_moment_strategy=bisr_strategy(bandwidth=4), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=10, noise_multiplier=1.0, key=key(0))` constructs successfully. Measured blow-ups at n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=10: band_mf(bands=10) rho=3.1623, bisr(bandwidth=4) rho=3.8106. With D1 ~ D2 that is a ~11% higher realized sensitivity than accounted, i.e. an effective noise multiplier about 10% below the one epsilon was computed from — silently, under a documentation sentence that says accounting 'is exactly the underlying first-moment mechanism'.

findings.title: The README and installation guide's extras block installs an unrelated PyPI project named `opaque`; six of the ten distribution names are unclaimed on PyPI
findings.claim: The documented primary install correctly pins the JetBrains index (`pip install opaque --index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` — verified reachable anonymously, HTTP 200, serving opaque 0.15.x wheels and all ten sub-distributions). But the 'Extras' block immediately below it drops the index: `pip install "opaque[auditing]"`, `"opaque[dpftrl]"`, `"opaque[transformers]"`, `"opaque[all]"`. Those resolve against PyPI, where the name `opaque` belongs to a different project (version 1.0.0, author Stefan Marsiske, homepage https://github.com/stef/libopaque, summary 'python libopaque wrapper'). pip only warns about an unknown extra, so the copy-pasted command installs that package. AGENTS.md's installation matrix (lines 127-137) is index-less too: `pip install opaque-base`, `opaque-engine`, `opaque-dpsgd`, `opaque-patches`, `opaque-transformers` are all unregistered on PyPI (HTTP 404), so those names are open to takeover. Defensive dependency-confusion stubs at version 999.9.9 were published on 2026-08-12 for only four of the ten names (opaque-accounting, opaque-auditing, opaque-dpftrl, opaque-optimizers). findings.title: Patching gpt_oss / deepseek_v4 silently deletes the attention sink and freezes the `sinks` parameter
findings.claim: `make_apply_family_patches` defaults `eager_attention_replacement=vmap_eager_attention_forward` (`transformers/_family.py:126, 212-215`), and neither `models/gpt_oss.py:16-19` nor `models/deepseek_v4.py:16-20` overrides it. Both upstream families compute attention with an extra sink logit — `sinks = module.sinks.reshape(1,-1,1,1)...; combined_logits = torch.cat([attn_weights, sinks], dim=-1)` (transformers `modeling_gpt_oss.py:251-252`, `modeling_deepseek_v4.py:724-725`) and pass `s_aux=self.sinks` into the attention interface (`modeling_gpt_oss.py:329`, `modeling_deepseek_v4.py:849`). Opaque's replacement takes `**kwargs` (`attention.py:373`), swallowing `s_aux`, and delegates to `_grouped_eager_attention`, a plain llama-shaped softmax with no sink term. Both families declare `_supports_sdpa = False` (`modeling_gpt_oss.py:387`, `modeling_deepseek_v4.py:1171`), so the module-global `eager_attention_forward` the patch rebinds is the only path a non-flash run can take.
findings.failure_scenario: Fine-tune a GPT-OSS or DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint with DPTrainer or any `apply_model_patches(model)` flow. Verified on a tiny GptOssForCausalLM with DEFAULT kwargs (no `eager_attention=True` needed): after `apply_model_patches(m2)`, `transformers.models.gpt_oss.modeling_gpt_oss.eager_attention_forward` is `vmap_eager_attention_forward`, forward logits shift by 1.54e-01 max abs versus the unpatched model, and after a backward pass `model.layers[0].self_attn.sinks.grad is None` — the attention-sink parameter receives no gradient and never trains. The parity suite cannot catch this: `gpt_oss` and `deepseek_v4` are in `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` (test_parity.py:88-92) so forward parity is skipped, and in `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` (:97-103) so grad parity is skipped; clearing the latter makes `test_backward_grads_parity` fail immediately with `missing={'model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks'}`. Privacy is unaffected (clipping still bounds per-record sensitivity), but the model being trained is not the model the user loaded, and `docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:215-218` states the opposite: for GPT-OSS and DeepSeek-V4 "only RMSNorm, RoPE (where standard), and cross-entropy are patched".

findings.title: Grad-parity harness is non-deterministic under dropout and mis-attributes the failure to the patches
findings.claim: `assert_parity_grad` and `assert_parity_vmap_grad` put both the unpatched reference and the patched model into `.train()` and run them one after the other off the shared global torch RNG, and `get_tiny_config_kwargs()` sets no dropout keys. Any family whose config defaults to nonzero dropout therefore draws different dropout masks in the two runs, and the helper reports the difference as a patch-parity failure. GPT-2 is the only currently registered such family, which is why the suite's `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` entry for gpt2 carries the (incorrect) reason "kv_cache/batchify patches alter backward graph".
findings.failure_scenario: Running `assert_parity_grad(GPT2LMHeadModel, GPT2Config, cpu, config_kwargs=<tiny>)` with GPT-2's default `resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.1` mismatches ALL 28 parameters and even the two losses (4.198710918 vs 4.208966732). Setting the three probabilities to 0.0 in the same call makes the losses bit-identical and 0 of 28 gradients mismatch; `assert_parity_vmap_grad` likewise fails (c_attn.bias abs_err=4.36e-03) at dropout 0.1 and passes at dropout 0.0. The consequence is twofold: a real family was written off as having broken gradients when it is bit-exact, and any newly registered family with default dropout (or any future config default change upstream) will produce the same false failure, which the suite's existing habit is to resolve by adding another name to the skip set.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/_test_utils.py:14-27 — `get_tiny_config_kwargs()` returns vocab/hidden/layers/heads/rope only; no dropout keys
_test_utils.py:461-482 — both models `.train()`, `loss_ref = unpatched(...)`; `loss_ref.backward()`; then the patched forward/backward, with no reseed between them
_test_utils.py:525-556 — `assert_parity_vmap_grad` has the same structure via `_vmap_grads(unpatched)` then `_vmap_grads(patched)`

Measured: dropout 0.1 -> 28/28 parameters mismatch and losses differ; dropout 0.0 -> `n mismatch 0 of 28` and losses identical. vmap variant: `drop=0.1: FAIL -> gpt2 drop=0.1: vmap_grad transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias mismatch: abs_err=4.36e-03`, `drop=0.0: VMAP GRAD PARITY PASSES`

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/models/gpt2.py:32-49 — family shims all disabled (`repeat_kv_replacement=None`, `eager_attention_replacement=None`, `rope_replacement=None`); only batchify + kv_cache apply
packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:97-99 — the skip entry and its incorrect reason
findings.fix_sketch: Force every dropout probability to 0 in `get_tiny_config_kwargs()` / `_base_config_kwargs()` (or call `torch.manual_seed(seed)` immediately before each of the two forward passes in both grad helpers), then drop gpt2 from `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES`. Add one regression case that runs grad parity on a family with nonzero default dropout so the determinism is pinned rather than accidental.

findings.title: Three registered families have no forward-parity coverage either, a hole no child of #769 covers
findings.claim: OPQ-339 and its child #813 are scoped to the *gradient* skips. The same test module carries a second, independent exemption set for the forward test: `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {"deepseek_v4", "gpt_oss", "qwen3_next"}` at :88-92, applied by `test_forward_logits_parity` at :251-252 with `pytest.skip(f"{family} requires runtime compatibility shims")`. Combined with `_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES`, these three families have **no** parity coverage at all — not forward, not backward, not vmap-grad — while `test_parity_families_covered` (:508-520) only subtracts the one-element `_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES` and therefore reports them as covered. #769's completion criterion ('Every registered family passes forward, gradient, and vmap-gradient parity against a genuinely unpatched reference') is stated for forward parity too, and no sub-issue addresses it.
findings.failure_scenario: A patch regression that changes `deepseek_v4`, `gpt_oss` or `qwen3_next` forward logits — a rebind of the wrong attention forward, a dropped softcap, a mis-scaled RoPE — is invisible to the parity suite, which reports these families as covered because the coverage guard cannot see either skip set. The user gets wrong logits and wrong gradients with no test signal. That said, the skip reason is partly legitimate for these three: the unpatched reference itself needs runtime shims, so a 'genuinely unpatched' reference may not exist — which is why the criterion needs an explicit exemption mechanism rather than silence.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:86-92 — `# These families require runtime compatibility shims even for an ordinary forward, so no strict-upstream parity reference is available.` / `_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES = {"deepseek_v4", "gpt_oss", "qwen3_next"}`
